_readme: Cover URLs and neutral blurbs for everything the viewer app renders. Three namespaces because the tabs are keyed differently: `media` by book-cache.json key, `readMedia` by a slug of the books-read.md title, `rejectMedia` by a slug of entity+author in book-rejects.jsonl. Fully regenerable: run tools/fetch-media.py. Kept out of book-cache.json so a cover refresh never has to reserialise that hand-formatted file. Blurbs say what the book IS; whether the reader would like it is book-estimates.jsonl's `why` and must not be duplicated here. A slug join is deliberately loose - editing a title in books-read.md costs a placeholder cover, never a broken row. `coverOL` is an Open Library cover for a row whose `cover` is on obalkyknih.cz, which serves only registered library catalogues; the GitHub Pages copy of the viewer shows it instead, and null means Open Library had none.
_cover: Open Library cover id resolved by title+author search, rendered as https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/id/<id>-M.jpg. Null with a 'coverNote' means no match - the app draws a typographic placeholder, which is a missing cover and not an error.

morning-star.blurb: Third of the Red Rising books: Darrow's rebellion against the Gold caste comes to open war across the solar system.
morning-star.pitch: Darrow's rebellion against the Gold caste, which you have followed since the first book, goes from hidden sabotage to open war across the solar system. You come back to the people he has gathered and the loyalties tested between them, in the same world of rigid caste and ambition you already know from Red Rising.

mistborn-final-empire.blurb: A street thief joins a crew of magic-users planning to overthrow an immortal god-emperor, in a world where metals grant specific, rule-bound powers.
mistborn-final-empire.pitch: Vin, a street thief, joins a crew with a plan that should be impossible: bringing down an immortal god-emperor. Magic comes from burning metals, each with its own exact rules, and the heist is built on knowing them. You get to know Vin from the inside, and her world is as carefully thought out as the plan.

leviathan-wakes.blurb: An ice hauler and a station detective stumble into the same conspiracy as Earth, Mars and the asteroid Belt slide toward war.
leviathan-wakes.pitch: An ice hauler and a station detective stumble into the same conspiracy while Earth, Mars and the Belt slide toward war. One invented drive reorganises a whole civilisation around water, air and how much gravity bodies can tolerate. Two anchored viewpoints keep the opening clear, and half the book is the detective working a missing-person case.

fahrenheit-451.blurb: A fireman whose job is burning books begins to wonder what is in them.
fahrenheit-451.pitch: A fireman burns a house full of books, rides home, and meets a seventeen-year-old neighbour whose questions begin to unsettle him. The idea fits in a sentence: a public that gave up reading for speed, screens and never giving offence, and now burns what is left. The captain who explains it makes it hold.

mans-search-for-meaning.blurb: A psychiatrist's account of surviving Auschwitz, and the theory of meaning he built out of it.
mans-search-for-meaning.pitch: A psychiatrist's account of surviving Auschwitz, and the theory of meaning he built out of it: that a person can still find a reason to go on where nearly everything has been taken. It is testimony that examines what is true rather than bare recollection, and it leaves you a question to carry afterwards.

half-a-king.blurb: A maimed prince, raised to be a scholar rather than a king, is betrayed and sold into slavery, and swears to take back what was his.
half-a-king.pitch: Yarvi, a maimed prince raised to be a scholar, is betrayed and sold into slavery, and swears to take back what was his. It is a short book that moves fast, like The Hunger Games. He has real flaws to overcome, and his own voice keeps you inside his head the whole way.

jurassic-park.blurb: A billionaire clones dinosaurs for a theme park, and the control systems he built fail exactly as the mathematician warned they would.
jurassic-park.pitch: A billionaire clones dinosaurs for a theme park, and the book is built on the park's own safety systems failing exactly as the mathematician warned they would. The systems are laid out clearly, so the thrill comes from watching each one break as it was always going to.

three-musketeers.blurb: A young Gascon arrives in Paris to join the King's musketeers and lands in the middle of a war between the crown and the cardinal.
three-musketeers.pitch: A young Gascon arrives in Paris to join the King's musketeers and lands in the middle of a war between the crown and the cardinal. It has a vivid cast of friends and the same pace you liked in Monte Cristo, and it plays loose with history in a way that stays out of the way of the fun.

night-flight-wind-sand-stars.blurb: Two short works by a pioneer airmail pilot on flying, danger and what it is that men owe each other.
night-flight-wind-sand-stars.pitch: Two short works by a pioneer airmail pilot on flying, solitude, danger and what men owe each other. They share the reflective register of The Little Prince, with real ideas about duty behind it, written by someone who actually flew the routes.

leva-ruka-tmy.blurb: An envoy arrives alone on a glacial world whose people have no fixed sex, and has to understand its politics before he can explain his own.
leva-ruka-tmy.pitch: Genly arrives alone on a glacial world whose people have no fixed sex, and has to understand its politics before he can explain his own. With sex taken out of politics, it asks what is left of loyalty and love, and sets patriotism against fear of the other. Much of it is two people learning each other, first through misread motives, then on the ice.

narod-nation-pratchett.blurb: A tsunami leaves one island boy and one shipwrecked English girl to rebuild a people from nothing - Pratchett outside Discworld, on belief and what survives it.
narod-nation-pratchett.pitch: A tsunami leaves one island boy and one shipwrecked English girl to rebuild a people from nothing, in an alternate nineteenth-century Pacific with no magic in sight. It is Pratchett outside Discworld, in the voice you liked in Mort, asking what makes a people and whether the gods exist, with belief a thread inside a survival story.

divine-cities.blurb: A diplomat investigates a murder in a conquered city whose gods were killed but whose miracles have not entirely stopped.
divine-cities.pitch: A diplomat investigates a murder in a conquered city whose gods were killed but whose miracles have not entirely stopped. The world grows from one event, the gods' deaths, and its consequences are the setting, with strong ideas on conquest and erased history. Shara is a loyal spy you can cheer for. It is built the same way as the world of Čaropisci.

silo-wool.blurb: Humanity lives in a buried silo under rules nobody questions, and the one forbidden question is what is actually outside.
silo-wool.pitch: Humanity lives in a buried silo where one question is forbidden: what is really outside. You follow the people who start to ask it, Juliette above all, a mechanic with real flaws and real nerve. The society is built like a machine that has to keep running, and readers still argue about what it is really protecting.

darce-the-giver.blurb: A boy in a community that has abolished pain, choice and colour is assigned to inherit the memories everyone else has been spared.
darce-the-giver.pitch: In a community that has abolished pain, choice and colour, a boy is chosen to receive the memories everyone else has been spared. The memories are the unknown, and what they show him about what the community hides is what sets him moving. One strong idea, carried all the way, that leaves you asking what is lost when pain is taken away.

draci-cesta.blurb: An epic fantasy that runs on banking, grain and debt rather than battle, following an orphan banker, an ageing spymaster and a war nobody can afford.
draci-cesta.pitch: An epic fantasy that runs on banking, grain and debt instead of battle, so the page time goes to what people want and why. An orphan banker, an ageing spymaster and a war nobody can afford drive it, and the politics are absorbing while they run.

koseni-scythe.blurb: Death has been cured, so a professional order is licensed to kill by quota, and two teenagers are apprenticed to it.
koseni-scythe.pitch: Death has been cured, so a professional order is licensed to take lives by quota, and two teenagers are apprenticed to it. A society that has abolished death and must still administer it is the whole idea, and the book follows it through. The two young leads carry you inside the order and its rules.

naslouchej-nozi.blurb: On a colony world where every man's thoughts are audible to everyone, a boy finds a pocket of silence and has to run.
naslouchej-nozi.pitch: On a colony world where every man's thoughts are audible to everyone, a boy finds a pocket of silence and has to run. The idea of audible thoughts is carried through consistently, and told in a first-person voice with a dialect of its own.

neuromancer.blurb: A burned-out console cowboy is hired for one last job by an employer who turns out to be an artificial intelligence trying to complete itself.
neuromancer.pitch: A burned-out console cowboy takes one last job for an employer that is an artificial intelligence trying to complete itself. It is canon for a reason, dense with ideas, and Gibson throws you straight into its world without a guide, on purpose.

children-of-time.blurb: A terraforming experiment loses its human overseers and succeeds on the spiders instead, and the book follows both species for millennia.
children-of-time.pitch: A terraforming experiment loses its human overseers and takes hold in spiders instead. From the first chapter you know what the virus does, and then the book follows the consequences across millennia: a spider civilisation whose technology, politics and faith all grow from its own body, and the question of what happens when two species finally meet.

day-of-the-triffids.blurb: A man wakes in hospital to find nearly everyone blinded overnight and the cultivated carnivorous plants no longer contained.
day-of-the-triffids.pitch: A man wakes in hospital to find nearly everyone blinded overnight and the cultivated carnivorous plants no longer contained. He tells it himself, plainly, and has to learn the rules of a changed world he knows nothing about in order to survive it. You watch the collapse unfold through its consequences.

sin-slavy-mistru-sf.blurb: The SFWA Hall of Fame anthology in Czech - the short stories the field's own writers voted canonical.
sin-slavy-mistru-sf.pitch: The SFWA Hall of Fame anthology collects the short stories the field's own writers voted canonical, edited by Ben Bova and gathered here in Czech. It spreads across a dozen authors, so it is a cheap way to sample the classics of the genre. Individual stories land very well.

skyward.blurb: On a planet under permanent aerial siege, a pilot's daughter fights for a place in flight school and finds a derelict ship that talks back.
skyward.pitch: Spensa, a pilot's daughter on a planet under permanent aerial siege, fights for a place in flight school and finds a derelict ship that talks back. Alongside the training she uncovers what her father really did and what the planet once was. The Defiant caste order grows out of the war, so the world follows from its situation.

tri-tvare-sandersona.blurb: A Czech collection of three shorter Sanderson works; the exact contents are not confirmed in the catalogue record.
tri-tvare-sandersona.pitch: Three shorter Sanderson works gathered in one Czech volume. Sanderson is known for settings built on clear rules and magic that has consequences, and short pieces let you meet a complete world in a single sitting. The exact contents are not confirmed, so check the shelf before you pick it up.

agent-to-the-stars.blurb: First contact goes to a Hollywood agent, because the aliens smell terrible and need a publicist.
agent-to-the-stars.pitch: First contact goes to a Hollywood agent, hired to represent the aliens who have made contact because they smell terrible and need a publicist. A light comic standalone in clear prose, with its one situation stated on page one and the comic voice doing the work.

dark-matter.blurb: A physics professor is abducted by a version of himself who took the other path, and has to find his way back through the lives he didn't live.
dark-matter.pitch: Built on real quantum vocabulary and a question everyone asks at some moment: what if you had taken the other road? It moves at thriller speed, and the hook is a man who has to find his way back through the lives he did not live, with a version of himself standing in the way.

pillars-of-the-earth.blurb: Twelve generations of ambition, politics and violence around the building of a cathedral in twelfth-century England.

the-blade-itself.blurb: A barbarian, a crippled torturer and a vain nobleman are pulled into a wizard's plan, in a fantasy that keeps undercutting its own heroics.
the-blade-itself.pitch: A barbarian, a crippled torturer and a vain young nobleman are each pulled into a wizard's plan, in a fantasy that keeps poking fun at its own heroics. The chapters rotate between them, so you spend most of your time inside their heads, wanting what they want.

dungeon-crawler-carl.blurb: Earth's buildings are demolished and the planet becomes a televised dungeon crawl; Carl enters in his underwear with his ex-girlfriend's cat.

murderbot-all-systems-red.blurb: A security android that has hacked its own governor module and would rather watch soap operas is assigned to protect a survey team.
murderbot-all-systems-red.pitch: A security android has hacked its own governor module and would rather watch soap operas than do its job, until it is assigned to guard a survey team. You get one clear first-person voice and an idea at the centre, personhood: what it means to be someone when you were built as a thing. It is short, and it stays on that idea.

the-will-of-the-many.blurb: A hidden heir enrols in an imperial academy in a republic where citizens cede their will - and thus their strength - upward to their betters.
the-will-of-the-many.pitch: A young man with a hidden past enrols in an imperial academy in a republic where citizens hand their will, and the strength it carries, upward to their betters. He tells the story himself, and every scene has him wanting something, with a secret to keep from the very people training him. The hierarchy grows naturally out of that one power rule, and it comes from the author of Licanius.

recursion.blurb: A neuroscientist builds a chair that lets people return to their own memories, and reality starts accumulating contradictory pasts.
recursion.pitch: A neuroscientist builds a chair that lets people return to their own memories, and reality starts piling up contradictory pasts. Two people carry it, each wanting one thing all the way through: a father who lost his daughter and a scientist whose mother is losing herself. You always know what they want, and the book rarely lets up.

we-are-legion.blurb: A software engineer wakes up a century after death as the computer core of a self-replicating interstellar probe, and keeps making copies of himself.
we-are-legion.pitch: A software engineer wakes a century after death as the computer core of a self-replicating interstellar probe and keeps making copies of himself. Funny and easy to read, told in one clear voice, with an idea you can sum up in a breath.

ted-chiang-vydech.blurb: Nine stories, each taking one precisely stated premise - a mechanical universe, a device that records every moment - and following it exactly where it leads.
ted-chiang-vydech.pitch: Nine stories, each starting from one precisely stated idea and following it exactly where it leads. The collection opens with its strongest pieces: a narrator facing a past cruelty and refusing to be that man again, then the title story, a mechanical universe thought through to the end of its own logic. You finish with ideas you keep turning over.

ted-chiang-pribehy-vaseho-zivota.blurb: Eight stories including the linguistics-of-first-contact novella filmed as Arrival, plus a Babel tower, a golem-making alphabet and a proof of God.

martanska-kronika.blurb: Linked stories covering the colonisation of Mars from first landing to the ruins left behind.
martanska-kronika.pitch: Linked stories follow the colonisation of Mars from the first landing to the ruins left behind, written as elegy rather than adventure. Each story pays for the one before it, so the whole becomes a single arc, carried by a quiet sadness for a planet people came to and could not keep.

rebelka-hirsi-ali.blurb: A Somali woman's account of Islam, forced marriage, escape to the Netherlands, and becoming a parliamentarian under police protection.
rebelka-hirsi-ali.pitch: A Somali girl raised in a devout family is married off by arrangement, escapes to the Netherlands and ends up in parliament under police protection. You get a first-person look at how belief, family and obedience feel from inside a world far from yours, and at what it takes to examine what you were taught is true. It sits close to what you valued in Seeking Allah, Finding Jesus.

prezila-jsem-cinsky-gulag.blurb: A Uyghur woman's account of two years in a Xinjiang re-education camp, written after her release to France.
prezila-jsem-cinsky-gulag.pitch: A Uyghur woman's first-person testimony of two years in a Xinjiang re-education camp, written after her release to France. It is a contemporary, contested situation told from inside, the sort of insight into how another group experiences the world that you valued in Seeking Allah, Finding Jesus.

cekam-az-si-pro-me-prijdou.blurb: A Uyghur poet's account of the surveillance state closing around his family, and the decision to leave.
cekam-az-si-pro-me-prijdou.pitch: Tahir Hamut Izgil, a Uyghur poet, watches the surveillance state tighten around his family in Xinjiang and works to get them out before arrest comes. You see the state's reach through one family's decisions, with more of the inner life than reportage usually carries. It shows how another group experiences the world, as Seeking Allah, Finding Jesus did.

mnich-v-zajeti-islamistu.blurb: A Syrian monk's account of the months he was held by Islamic State, and of the Muslim neighbours who had been his community.
mnich-v-zajeti-islamistu.pitch: A Syrian monk tells of the months he was held by Islamic State, and of the Muslim neighbours who had been his community. Faith runs through the account as part of a lived story rather than as a lecture. It is a first-person view of life in a mixed community, and of what it means to be taken out of it.

pan-much.blurb: Schoolboys stranded on an island build a society, and it comes apart in the order Golding argues it must.
pan-much.pitch: Schoolboys stranded on an island build a society, and the book follows, step by step and with rigour, how and why it comes apart. It is bleak but full of ideas, an argument about people made into a story. Short and idea-driven, it leaves you something to think over, in the way Animal Farm did.

jonathan-livingston-racek.blurb: A short allegory about a gull who cares more about flying well than about eating.
jonathan-livingston-racek.pitch: A very short fable about a gull who wants more from flying than food, and about pursuing mastery for its own sake. It is built on a single idea and carried in an earnest, uncomplicated voice, and it is over before you have had time to get tired of it.

fantasticke-povidky-dostojevskij.blurb: Dostoevsky's short fantastic fiction, including the dream of a man who has decided to shoot himself.
fantasticke-povidky-dostojevskij.pitch: Dostoevsky's short fantastic fiction has real philosophical weight, and the dream of the man who has decided to shoot himself is an idea rather than a mood. The Ridiculous Man's dream is among the best-known pieces, a question about what a life is for, and it stays with you long after the story ends.

vrchol-vulkanu-ellison.blurb: Ellison's own selection of his award-winning stories - short, confrontational, idea-first SF.
vrchol-vulkanu-ellison.pitch: Ellison's own selection of his award-winning stories: short, confrontational, idea-first SF. Each story carries its own genuine idea, and the register is deliberately varied and transgressive. A career retrospective picked by the author himself.

tabaterka-z-bagomba-vonnegut.blurb: Vonnegut's early magazine stories, collected: small-town American lives, told straight and quick.
tabaterka-z-bagomba-vonnegut.pitch: Vonnegut's early magazine stories, small-town American lives told straight and quick. They were written to sell to Collier's rather than to argue anything, and the voice is already there. It is an easy way to meet the author before his canonical work.

vul-v-chryzantemach-saki.blurb: Edwardian comic short stories built on a cruel wit and a last-line reversal.

hana-mornstajnova.blurb: Czech family novel in three time layers: a girl orphaned by the 1954 typhus epidemic in a small Moravian town is left with an aunt whose own past explains everything.
hana-mornstajnova.pitch: A Czech family novel in three time layers, set in a small Moravian town: in 1954 a typhus epidemic leaves a girl orphaned and in the care of an aunt whose own past explains everything. The whole book is about why Hana became who she is, and what drove each woman in the line. The epidemic is real and researched, and the setting is your own town.

europeana-ourednik.blurb: A short, deadpan prose collage of twentieth-century Europe, assembling its wars, ideologies and statistics into one continuous voice.
europeana-ourednik.pitch: The twentieth century told as a deadpan catalogue of its own wars, ideologies and statistics, in one continuous voice. It is short and idea-dense, an argument about how the century narrated itself. You read it for the ideas and the method, not for a plot or a hero.

modlitba-horovitzova.blurb: Novella: a group of wealthy Jewish prisoners is persuaded to buy its way out of a camp, in a transaction that was never real.
modlitba-horovitzova.pitch: A short novella in which a group of wealthy Jewish prisoners is persuaded to buy its way out of a camp, in a transaction that was never real. The whole plot is a con, so the book is built on weighing what these people can and cannot believe. You read it as a study of belief under pressure.

zert-kundera.blurb: A student's sarcastic postcard destroys his life under Czech Stalinism; decades later he engineers an elaborate revenge that misfires.
zert-kundera.pitch: A student's sarcastic postcard destroys his life under Czech Stalinism, and decades later he plans an elaborate revenge. Four narrators, staggered rather than simultaneous, tell it, with penal labour and a friend's crisis of faith along the way. The book asks what a joke is worth, what a man can take back after decades and what he has actually punished.

spalovac-mrtvol.blurb: A mild, sentimental crematorium employee in occupied Prague is drawn by degrees into serving the Nazi machine.
spalovac-mrtvol.pitch: A mild, sentimental crematorium employee in occupied Prague is drawn by degrees into serving the Nazi machine. Short and idea-driven, it asks how a mild man becomes a monster, told in the first person from inside his head.

nadace-foundation.blurb: A mathematician predicts the fall of a galactic empire and founds a colony meant to shorten the dark age that follows; the book follows its first centuries in jumps.
nadace-foundation.pitch: A mathematician foresees the fall of a galactic empire and founds a colony meant to shorten the dark age that follows. Psychohistory is laid out precisely and the decline follows from it, and almost all the page time is people talking and scheming rather than fighting. It gives you the same pleasure of a big idea followed through that you named in Old Man's War.

ruze-pro-algernon.blurb: Charlie Gordon, a man with an IQ of 68, keeps a diary through the experimental surgery that makes him a genius, and through what comes after.
ruze-pro-algernon.pitch: Charlie Gordon, a man with a low IQ, writes his own progress reports before and after an experimental operation, so every page is inside one mind: what he wants, fears and remembers. His past surfaces memory by memory as he changes, and the people who made him a laboratory subject treat him as one. It leaves you thinking about what intelligence is worth without emotional growth.

mesicni-prach.blurb: A tourist dust-cruiser sinks beneath the Moon's Sea of Thirst with its passengers alive inside, and the rest is a rescue worked out against the clock.
mesicni-prach.pitch: A tourist dust-cruiser sinks beneath the Moon's Sea of Thirst with its passengers alive inside, and the rest is engineering against the clock. The dust is dry and fine and flows like water, and everything that follows obeys that: heat, air and a second cave-in. It is problem-solving with a whole group trapped together, and Pat Harris is a likeable lead.

architekti-svetu.blurb: Fifty years after moon-sized Architects reshaped inhabited planets into sculpture, a salvage crew finds evidence they have come back. First of The Final Architecture.
architekti-svetu.pitch: Fifty years after moon-sized Architects reshaped inhabited planets into sculpture, a salvage crew finds evidence they have come back. Unspace has firm rules, and the plot runs on them. Idris, an Intermediary who keeps paying a real price for what he wants, anchors the story, and the crew's viewpoints weave in around him.

muz-ktery-si-pletl-manzelku.blurb: Twenty-four neurological case histories: patients who lose the ability to recognise faces, to feel where their limbs are, or to remember anything new.
muz-ktery-si-pletl-manzelku.pitch: Twenty-four case histories of people whose brains work differently: a man who cannot recognise his wife's face, another who no longer feels where his limbs are, another who cannot remember anything new. Each chapter is short and built around one question about what is really happening and what it is like from inside. You come away thinking about what a self is made of.

siddhartha.blurb: A brahmin's son leaves home to find enlightenment, tries asceticism, commerce and love in turn, and learns that wisdom cannot be handed over.
siddhartha.pitch: A brahmin's son leaves home in search of enlightenment and tries asceticism, commerce and love in turn. It is short, with one protagonist and one idea followed to its end: that wisdom cannot be handed over, only lived. Siddhartha actually changes along the way, and what holds you is what he wants and why.

lovec-draku.blurb: Kabul in the 1970s: a wealthy boy betrays his servant's son, and spends the next thirty years, through the Soviet and Taliban decades, trying to undo it.
lovec-draku.pitch: Kabul in the 1970s: a wealthy boy betrays his servant's son, and spends thirty years, through the Soviet and Taliban decades, trying to undo it. Guilt and the wish to make amends drive the story, and you stay close to Amir's reasons, a flawed man you can still root for. It shows how Afghans lived through those decades, from within.

ostre-sledovane-vlaky.blurb: A young trainee dispatcher at a small Czech station in 1945, preoccupied with his own humiliation, ends up carrying out an act of sabotage.
ostre-sledovane-vlaky.pitch: In 1945 a young trainee dispatcher at a small Czech station, preoccupied with his own humiliation, ends up carrying out an act of sabotage. It is about ninety pages with one protagonist, and his private shame is what drives the public act. Milos is interesting throughout, and the idea fits in a phrase.

predehra-k-nadaci.blurb: Hari Seldon arrives on Trantor with a mathematical theory nobody believes in, and spends the book on the run while it becomes psychohistory.
predehra-k-nadaci.pitch: Hari Seldon arrives on Trantor with a mathematical theory nobody believes, and spends the book on the run while it becomes psychohistory. He is on the page from the first chapter to the last, so the science arrives as one man's problem, and you tour the capital through his eyes.

slysim-te-vsude.blurb: An outpatient procedure is meant to let couples feel each other's emotions; it goes wrong and one woman starts hearing everyone's thoughts instead.
slysim-te-vsude.pitch: An outpatient procedure meant to let couples feel each other's emotions goes wrong, and one woman starts hearing everyone's thoughts instead. Willis takes the social consequences of that idea seriously enough that the comedy comes out of the rules rather than around them. You will root for the lead, the story stays on one thread, and romance is central but not the whole story.

2001-vesmirna-odysea.blurb: A monolith buried on the Moon points at Saturn, and the ship sent to follow it carries a computer that begins to lie.
2001-vesmirna-odysea.pitch: A monolith buried on the Moon leads toward Saturn, and the ship sent to follow it carries a computer that begins to lie. Clarke's physics is exact and kept, and the HAL section is pure motive: why a machine that cannot lie starts lying. It leaves ideas behind, and the journey toward an unknown signal drives it.

pohrbeny-obr.blurb: An elderly couple leave their village to find the son they can barely remember, in a Britain where a mist is eating everyone's memory.
pohrbeny-obr.pitch: An elderly couple, Axl and Beatrice, set out to find a son they can barely remember, in a Britain where a mist is eating everyone's memory. You will want them to reach him, and recovering their own past and the land's is what they need to do it. Underneath is the question of what a people should be made to remember.

skorapka.blurb: A nine-months-unborn narrator, upside down in the womb, overhears his mother and his uncle planning to poison his father.
skorapka.pitch: Narrated by an unborn child, upside down in the womb, overhearing his mother and his uncle plan his father's murder. One conceit, set out on the first page and kept to the end, in about two hundred pages. The killers' motives are the whole story, and the narrator can only listen and think.

wolf-hall.blurb: Thomas Cromwell rises from a blacksmith's son to Henry VIII's indispensable servant across the years of the king's first divorce.
wolf-hall.pitch: Thomas Cromwell rises from a blacksmith's son to Henry VIII's indispensable servant across the years of the king's first divorce. Almost nothing happens except people calculating, and that is the method: he is both interesting and unusually easy to root for. Mantel writes from inside his head, and you learn the Tudor court through his eyes.

pulnocni-knihovna.blurb: A woman at the end of her rope wakes in a library where every book is a life she could have lived, and is allowed to try them.
pulnocni-knihovna.pitch: A woman at the end of her rope wakes in a library where every book is a life she could have lived, and is allowed to try them. You will want her to find her way, and the idea about unlived lives is simple to grasp, reads quickly and stays with you.

syn-lowry.blurb: A young mother in the walled community gives birth as a Vessel, loses the child, and spends years searching outside for him. Fourth of The Giver.
syn-lowry.pitch: A young mother searches for the child taken from her, one want stated plainly and pursued the whole way. The fourth Giver book takes you outside the walled community, and its engine is that search, carried entirely by what drives her.

nezna-dostojevskij.blurb: A pawnbroker stands over his young wife's body and talks himself through the marriage, minute by minute, trying to explain why she jumped.
nezna-dostojevskij.pitch: A pawnbroker stands over his young wife's body and talks himself through the marriage, minute by minute, trying to explain why she jumped. In fifty pages it is a single monologue, and motives are the text itself. The idea fits in a phrase, and it is the whole book.

blaznovy-zapisky.blurb: Gogol's Petersburg tales: a clerk whose diary slides into madness, a nose that leaves its owner and takes up a career, an overcoat worth a life.
blaznovy-zapisky.pitch: Gogol's Petersburg tales: a clerk whose diary slides into madness, a nose that leaves its owner and takes up a career. Each piece has an idea you can name in a phrase, and the humour is strange and sharp, so you can dip in and come out with something to think about.

ortel-kafka.blurb: A young merchant writes to a friend abroad about his engagement, shows the letter to his bedridden father, and is sentenced.

cizinec-camus.blurb: Meursault buries his mother without crying, drifts into killing a man on a beach, and is condemned less for the murder than for his indifference.
cizinec-camus.pitch: Meursault buries his mother without crying, drifts into a killing on a beach, and is condemned less for the murder than for his indifference. One idea carried all the way without flinching, in about a hundred and twenty pages, and easy to state in a sentence.

bozska-komedie.blurb: Guided by Virgil and then Beatrice, the poet descends through the circles of Hell, climbs Purgatory, and ascends the spheres of Paradise.
bozska-komedie.pitch: Guided by Virgil and then Beatrice, Dante descends through Hell, climbs Purgatory and rises through the spheres of Paradise. Ideas are the whole architecture of it, a reverent allegory of sin, judgement and grace. The Mikes translation is the readable modern one to look for.

icehenge.blurb: A monument of ice stands at Pluto's north pole and nobody can prove who built it; three narrators, centuries apart, argue over the evidence.
icehenge.pitch: A monument of ice stands at the north pole of Pluto and nobody can prove who built it. Three narrators, centuries apart, argue over the evidence, which turns history itself into something arguable rather than known. The question of who built it, and whether anyone can ever really know, pulls you through.

jonathan-strange-norrell.blurb: English magic returns during the Napoleonic wars through two very different magicians, and the fairy one of them summons will not be dismissed.

neviditelny-zivot-addie-larue.blurb: A woman trades her soul in 1714 for a life without end, on the condition that nobody she meets can remember her, until three hundred years later someone does.
neviditelny-zivot-addie-larue.pitch: Addie LaRue strikes a bargain for a life without end, and the terms are exact: nobody she meets can remember her, she cannot say her own name, and she cannot leave a mark. You will want her to win, and the book is about what it is to live unremembered and what it means when someone finally remembers.

dvanact-povidek-o-poutnicich.blurb: Twelve stories about Latin Americans adrift in Europe: an exiled president selling his possessions, a woman locked in an asylum by mistake.
dvanact-povidek-o-poutnicich.pitch: Twelve stories about Latin Americans adrift in Europe, among them an exiled president selling his possessions and a woman locked in an asylum by mistake. They are built on situations rather than atmosphere, and several carry an idea you can state in a phrase. By García Márquez, with an audio edition from Tympanum.

jana-eyrova.blurb: An orphaned governess takes a post at Thornfield Hall, falls in love with its master, and discovers what he keeps upstairs.
jana-eyrova.pitch: Jane tells her own life in the first person, and what she holds to against every pressure is the heart of the book: her right to run her own conscience. You will be on her side, an orphan governess who takes a post at Thornfield Hall and keeps her own counsel there, with a Gothic atmosphere around the romance.

starec-ktery-cetl-milostne-romany.blurb: An old man in an Amazon river town reads romance novels for pleasure, and is the only person who understands the ocelot the hunters have provoked.
starec-ktery-cetl-milostne-romany.pitch: An old man in an Amazon river town reads romance novels for pleasure, and he alone understands the ocelot the hunters have provoked. A short book with one setting and a clean line about what outsiders do to a place they do not understand. Slight in the best sense: you can finish it in an afternoon and carry the idea for a good while after.

dynastie-pampelisek.blurb: Two friends, a bandit's son and a fallen duke, bring down an empire together and then find themselves on opposite sides. First of The Dandelion Dynasty.
dynastie-pampelisek.pitch: A bandit's son and a fallen duke bring down an empire together, and then find themselves on opposite sides, so the book asks how a rebellion turns on the people who made it. The silkpunk world is invented with rules, and the story is told in the voice of a chronicle, which gives it a sweeping, mythic scale.

pate-rocni-obdobi.blurb: On a continent where the earth kills regularly, the people who can still it are enslaved for it; three women's stories run in parallel. First of The Broken Earth.
pate-rocni-obdobi.pitch: On a continent where the earth kills regularly, those who can still it are enslaved for it, and the whole civilisation is organised around that power and its real costs. Three women's stories run in parallel, and what the catastrophe is and what the obelisks are keeps pulling you on. Hugo-winning, first of the Broken Earth.

general-ve-svem-labyrintu.blurb: Simon Bolivar's last journey down the Magdalena river, dying and abandoned by the republics he made.
general-ve-svem-labyrintu.pitch: Bolivar's last river journey, as straight historical fiction about a man's motives as he loses everything he built. There is no magical realism here. It is a portrait of power and disillusion from the inside, told as one long voyage down the Magdalena.

pohreb-velke-matky.blurb: Eight stories from Macondo and its neighbours, ending with the state funeral of a matriarch who owned everything, including the weather.

rijnova-zeme.blurb: Nineteen macabre stories: a jar at a carnival, a skeleton the narrator wants removed, and the Elliotts, a family of amiable monsters.

hvezdy-jako-prach.blurb: A student on a tyrant-ruled world flees an assassination attempt and joins a search for the document that could break the Tyranni.

sila-psa.blurb: Two brothers run a Montana ranch; when the younger marries a widow, the elder sets about destroying her and her son, and why he is cruel is the point.
sila-psa.pitch: Two brothers run a Montana ranch, and when the younger marries a widow, the elder sets about destroying her and her son. The whole book is the question of why Phil is cruel, an answer that is withheld and then earned. Savage renders the ranch and its landscape at length.

ministerstvo-pro-budoucnost.blurb: After a heatwave kills twenty million people in India, a UN body is created to represent everyone not yet born, and told to fix the climate.
ministerstvo-pro-budoucnost.pitch: After a heatwave kills twenty million people in India, a UN body is created to represent everyone not yet born, and told to fix the climate. Kim Stanley Robinson treats the climate crisis as a problem of institutions and people who do not exist yet. The book carries an enormous payload of ideas, in essays, riddles and eyewitness fragments.

totoznost-kundera.blurb: A woman starts receiving anonymous admiring letters; her lover, who is writing them, watches the fiction take her over.
totoznost-kundera.pitch: A woman starts receiving anonymous admiring letters, and her lover, who is writing them, watches the fiction take her over. Short, one conceit, kept tight: who we are to the person who loves us. Kundera follows it through in a hundred and fifty pages, and an audio edition from Supraphon also exists.

milosrdenstvi.blurb: Colonial Virginia in the 1680s, before race had hardened: a farmer takes a slave child in payment, and four women on his land tell what follows.

pampeliskove-vino.blurb: One summer in a small Illinois town in 1928, in the vignettes of a twelve-year-old boy: a ravine, a Tarot witch, a machine for happiness.

plujici-ostrov.blurb: A string quartet is kidnapped onto Standard Island, a self-propelled artificial island owned by millionaires, and watches it split in two.

pomalost-kundera.blurb: A libertine night at a French chateau in the eighteenth century and a conference at the same chateau today, interleaved as an essay on hurry.

okamziky-cechov.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-08-31)
okamziky-cechov.blurb: A selection of Chekhov's short stories: provincial doctors, clerks and landowners caught at the moment a life quietly settles.

dublinane.blurb: Fifteen stories of Dublin lives at the point where they stop moving: a boy, a clerk, a spinster, and a party where a husband learns something.

prilis-mnoho-stesti.blurb: Ten stories of Ontario lives, ending with the Russian mathematician Sophia Kovalevsky's last journey.

pritelkyne-z-mladi.blurb: Ten stories about women looking back at the moment their lives turned, told in Munro's doubling-back way.

nepritel-pritel-ctitel.blurb: Nine stories, including a housekeeper tricked by a forged love letter into travelling to a man who never wrote it.

schizofrenicke-evangelium.blurb: Early experimental Hrabal: collage, overheard talk and lyrical digression rather than narrative.

pabitele.blurb: Hrabal's palaverers, the tram conductors, scrap-yard workers and pub philosophers who talk their way through a story.

zvirata-hrdinove.blurb: Animal life stories by the founder of the genre, a mustang, a hound and a lynx, written as biographies rather than fables.

niziny-muller.blurb: Prose fragments of a German-speaking childhood in Ceausescu's Banat, where the village and the state are equally close.

city-and-its-uncertain-walls.blurb: A man searches for the girl he loved as a teenager, in a walled city where shadows are removed at the gate and he reads old dreams.

inheritance-paolini.blurb: Eragon and Saphira face Galbatorix at last, with the Varden marching on the capital. Fourth of the Inheritance Cycle.
inheritance-paolini.pitch: Eragon and Saphira face Galbatorix at last, with the Varden marching on the capital. This is the fourth and last volume of the Inheritance Cycle, where the conflict set up in the earlier books comes to a head. Its magic is rule-bound, worked through the ancient language, and the cycle builds a full world around it.

erendira-marquez.blurb: After accidentally burning down her grandmother's house, fourteen-year-old Erendira is sold into years of forced prostitution across a string of desert towns to pay off the debt, until a young smuggler named Ulises falls for her and tries to free her.

hodiny-mcewan.blurb: Deserted by his wife with an infant son in 1986, Roland Baines revisits his life from a 1950s childhood in Libya and an English boarding school - where, at eleven, a piano teacher begins a relationship with him that continues into his teens - through the Cold War, the fall of the Berlin Wall and the Covid pandemic.

muzi-kteri-nemaji-zeny.blurb: Seven linked short stories about men separated from women in their lives - by death, infidelity, or simple unknowability - including a widowed actor who hires a female chauffeur to talk through his late wife's affairs, a housebound man visited by a woman who tells him stories after sex, and a reverse retelling of Kafka's Metamorphosis in which a creature wakes up human and is named Gregor Samsa.

prvni-osoba-jednotneho-cisla.blurb: Eight loosely autobiographical first-person stories - some straight nostalgia (a Beatles-era teenage romance, a piano-recital invitation gone strange), some outright fabulist (a talking monkey who confesses to stealing women's names) - narrated by men looking back and not always sure what the memory adds up to.

oci-modreho-psa.blurb: A 1974 collection of eleven early short stories (written 1947-1955, before the author's Nobel-era style) built around death-in-life states, dreams and inherited curses -- including the title story, in which a man and a woman meet only in each other's dreams and can never recognize each other awake.

spanek-murakami.blurb: A married woman stops sleeping for seventeen straight nights with no physical decline, and spends her new waking hours re-reading Anna Karenina, eating chocolate and drinking brandy, and reconsidering the routine of her marriage from an unfamiliar angle. The story ends with her alone at night in her car as two unidentified men rock it back and forth, unresolved.
spanek-murakami.pitch: A married woman stops sleeping for seventeen nights with no physical decline, and uses her new waking hours to re-read Anna Karenina, eat chocolate and see her routine marriage from outside. Nearly the whole story is her own examination of what she wants and why. The strange condition is never explained, and the book does not need it to be.

svab-mcewan.blurb: A cockroach hive-mind wakes to find itself running the British government; the new Prime Minister, Jim Sams, pushes 'Reversalism' - an inverted economy in which employees pay to work and shops pay customers to shop - as a satire of Brexit-era politics, splitting the country into Reversalists and Clockwisers.

inkvizitor.blurb: Sent back to England after the fall of Hookton, Thomas of Hookton pursues his dead father's hints of a hidden Holy Grail, survives the Scottish invasion of 1347, and is drawn into a Dominican inquisitor's hunt for the Vexille family's heresy.
inkvizitor.pitch: Thomas of Hookton chases his dead father's hints of a hidden Holy Grail, survives the Scottish invasion of 1347, and is drawn into a Dominican inquisitor's hunt for the Vexille family's heresy, which puts his own faith under real pressure. His friendship with the Scottish noble Robbie Douglas gives the book loyalty under strain. It is the middle volume of a trilogy.

sharpuv-regiment.blurb: The South Essex Regiment in Spain is starved of replacements and facing disbandment; Sharpe returns to England to find out why, and traces the failure to a fraudulent recruiting ring protected by powerful men in London.
sharpuv-regiment.pitch: Sharpe's South Essex Regiment in Spain is starved of replacements and facing disbandment, so he returns to England to find out why. This entry trades the series' battles for scheming and its consequences. Sharpe is the underdog you cheer for, defending his men against the people who should be backing them, and readers single out its clever detail.

2061-treti-vesmirna-odysea.blurb: In 2061 Heywood Floyd, now over a hundred, travels aboard a liner to land on Halley's Comet, while a second ship is forced down on Europa, where humans have been warned not to go.

3001-posledni-vesmirna-odysea.blurb: Frank Poole, thrown into space by his ship's computer a thousand years earlier, is recovered and revived in the year 3001, and takes a part in humanity's dealings with the monoliths.
3001-posledni-vesmirna-odysea.pitch: Frank Poole, thrown into space by his ship's computer a thousand years ago, is recovered and revived in the year 3001. The first stretch is a guided tour of what changed, told through one man learning it. An astronaut left for dead wakes in a future he has to catch up on, and the monoliths are still out there.

a-zrodi-se-nadace.blurb: Hari Seldon works across four decades to establish psychohistory and protect it from a decaying Galactic Empire, through political intrigue, personal loss, and the discovery that his granddaughter can read minds.
a-zrodi-se-nadace.pitch: Hari Seldon's life from forty to eighty-one, as a book about one man who wants to save civilisation and what that costs him. Unusually for Asimov, the page time stays on one figure for its whole length: the funding stripped year after year, the people he loves paying for his work, and the work continuing anyway.

alcatraz-versus-dabelsti-knihovnici.blurb: On his thirteenth birthday Alcatraz Smedry inherits a bag of sand, accidentally burns his foster parents' kitchen, and learns from a grandfather he has never met that a secret order of Librarians is hiding the truth about the world. They go to steal the sand back.

alcatraz-versus-legie-zakladatelovych-ko.blurb: Alcatraz travels to Nalhalla, the country his family comes from, and instead ends up in the Library of Alexandria hunting for his missing father, pursued by a Librarian assassin built partly of metal.

ani-sami-bohove.blurb: A physicist works out that the Electron Pump, which supplies Earth with limitless energy by exchanging matter with a parallel universe, will eventually make the Sun explode, and nobody will listen. The middle section follows three beings of the other universe, one of whom reaches the same conclusion from her side.
ani-sami-bohove.pitch: A pump trades matter with a neighbouring universe and gives everyone free energy, and a physicist works out that it will make the Sun explode, but nobody who benefits wants the calculation checked. The whole book is that one idea and its political consequences, followed to the end, with a long section seen from the other universe.

anna-na-krku-a-jine-povidky.blurb: A Czech selection of Anton Chekhov's short stories spanning his whole career, from the brief early humoresques to the mature serious work. The title story follows Anya, married off to an elderly official, as she turns her new social standing to her own use.

automat-svet.blurb: A selection of Bohumil Hrabal's short stories set among railwaymen, pub regulars and outsiders on the Prague periphery, with an afterword by Emanuel Frynta. The title story begins with the discovery of a hanged girl in the Liben arcade housing the automat Svet.
automat-svet.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-08-31)

betonova-zahrada.blurb: Four siblings are left alone in a suburban house after both parents die. To avoid being separated by the authorities they hide their mother's body in cement in the cellar and keep house themselves.

blokada.blurb: Mars is in alien hands and the outer solar system is blockaded. Andrew Grayson ships out on a warship attempting to break through to a cut-off colony, alongside the rival human alliance that was recently the enemy.

bojove-rozkazy.blurb: Four years after the aliens were pushed back, the peace is holding but the threat is not gone. Major Andrew Grayson and his special tactics team ship out on the warship Washington for a reconnaissance run deep into enemy-held space.
bojove-rozkazy.pitch: Four years after the aliens were pushed back, Major Andrew Grayson and his special tactics team ship out on the warship Washington for a reconnaissance run deep into enemy-held space. It starts clean: one ship, one objective, and you know within a page what the situation is and what is wanted. One first-person narrator carries it throughout.

brany-athen.blurb: Athens, 490 BC. The general Xanthippos, the ambitious Themistokles and the incorruptible Aristides meet the first Persian invasion at Marathon, then spend a decade quarrelling over the city while Xerxes prepares a second.
brany-athen.pitch: Marathon, and the long years afterwards when Athens had to decide what to do with the men who saved it. Xanthippos is honourable and hot-headed, Themistokles ambitious and self-made, Aristides incorruptible, and the book is about the politics between them more than the fighting. It leaves you with one thought: a free city can vote out the man who saved it.

cary.blurb: In present-day night-time Tokyo a chain of strangers - among them prostitutes, clients and drifters - meet by chance, each chapter passing the story to another of them.

cas-malin-prezralych.blurb: Autobiographical humorous pieces in which the author recounts trips around the Czech lands, France and Britain, and episodes from her own life. Illustrated by Tereza Budilova; 222 pages.

cytonik.blurb: Spensa flees into the nowhere, a place where time behaves differently, people lose their memories and pirate factions fight for control, following an old path in search of what the delvers are and how they can be beaten.
cytonik.pitch: Spensa flees into the nowhere, where time misbehaves and crossing costs memory, so she spends the very self she is trying to defend. She is searching for what the delvers truly are, and the answer to that question is why the journey matters. Told in her tight first-person voice, with a price paid at every step.

demanty-noci.blurb: Nine stories of Jewish children and young people - in hiding, in the ghetto, in the camps and on a death transport - by a writer who survived the places he describes.

den-kdy-padla-noc.blurb: A sister of a warrior priory whose enemy has not appeared for five hundred years, a young princess of Inys expected to continue her mother's line, and a godsinger in the East are drawn together when dragons wake in the mountains.
den-kdy-padla-noc.pitch: An order of warrior sisters has trained for five hundred years against an enemy that never came, and the younger ones say the whole institution is pointless, until dragons wake in the mountains and draw a sister, a young princess of Inys and a godsinger of the East together. The standout is a woman of about fifty, carried as the real heroine rather than a mentor handing over a sword.

deti-zmaru.blurb: Long after the collapse of human empire, a terraforming crew reaches two habitable worlds and one scientist begins uplifting octopuses, while centuries later a joint human and spider expedition arrives chasing a radio signal from the same system.
deti-zmaru.pitch: One scientist uplifts octopuses, and the book works out what a mind spread through its arms actually builds: a civilisation that settles disagreement by broadcasting emotion rather than by argument. Centuries later a joint human and spider expedition follows a radio signal to the same system, and survival depends on understanding what is out there, including something that cannot be negotiated with.

dezerce.blurb: With Mars still held by the aliens, Andrew Grayson is posted as an instructor while both human alliances rebuild their fleets. A reconnaissance mission then takes him far from the front line and outside his orders.

dole-v-udoli.blurb: Luigi, a forest ranger in the Valsesia expecting a first child with Elisabetta, receives his brother Alfredo back from Canada to settle their dead father's house between them, while a series of dog shootings along the river goes on nearby.

draci-plamen.blurb: On a cold evening in early 1957, Sarah Dewhurst and her father wait at a petrol station for the dragon they have hired to work their failing farm. Elsewhere a young assassin raised by a cult of dragon worshippers is sent to kill the saviour named in a prophecy.
draci-plamen.pitch: On a cold evening in early 1957, Sarah Dewhurst and her father wait at a petrol station for the dragon they have hired to work their failing farm. Elsewhere a young assassin raised by a cult is sent to kill a saviour named in a prophecy. The fantasy does the thinking: a Japanese American family still not accepted after internment, a racist deputy, and an argument over whether dragons have souls.

druha-nadace.blurb: After the Mule's conquest, first he and then the First Foundation itself hunt for the hidden Second Foundation of mind-readers, in two linked narratives sixty years apart - the second led by Arkady Darell, a fourteen-year-old who leaves home to find it.
druha-nadace.pitch: After the Mule's conquest, first he and then the First Foundation itself hunt for the hidden Second Foundation of mind-readers, in two narratives sixty years apart, the second led by fourteen-year-old Arkady Darell. The question driving it is whether history can be steered at all once some people can read and quietly rewrite minds.

dubliners.blurb: Fifteen short stories about the ordinary lives of Dublin's inhabitants, from childhood episodes through portraits of adults in middle age, closing with a Christmas party and its aftermath.

elantris.blurb: On the eve of his wedding the crown prince of Arelon is struck by the curse that turned the shining city of Elantris into a prison of the living dead, and is thrown inside. His unmet bride arrives in the capital as a widow, while a foreign high priest is given three months to convert the kingdom or see it destroyed.

evakuace.blurb: With Mars lost and alien seed ships patrolling the edge of the solar system, the ice colony of New Svalbard is close to starvation. Andrew Grayson, now a combat controller, is caught between the two human alliances and an enemy neither can beat alone.
evakuace.pitch: With Mars lost and alien seed ships patrolling the edge of the solar system, the ice colony of New Svalbard is close to starvation, and combat controller Andrew Grayson is caught between two human alliances and an enemy neither can beat alone. One narrator, one assignment at a time, keeps it easy to follow and fast.

gallant.blurb: Olivia Prior, a mute orphan raised at a school for girls, is summoned by letter to her family's estate, Gallant, and finds her uncle already dead and her cousin unwilling to have her there. Beyond a ruined wall on the grounds stands another version of the house, ruled by a figure who wants her.
gallant.pitch: Olivia Prior, a mute orphan raised at a school for girls, is summoned to her family's estate, Gallant, where her uncle is already dead, her cousin does not want her, and a ruined wall hides another version of the house. The best thing in it is the communication thread: a protagonist whose signing and drawing are how she is known at all. Gothic atmosphere, with a death figure, ghouls and bone shards of Schwab's own invention.

gentleman-v-moskve.blurb: In June 1922 a Bolshevik tribunal sentences Count Alexander Ilyich Rostov to lifelong house arrest in Moscow's Hotel Metropol. He moves from his suite to a small attic room and lives there through three decades of Soviet history.
gentleman-v-moskve.pitch: In 1922 a Bolshevik tribunal sentences Count Rostov to spend the rest of his life inside Moscow's Hotel Metropol, on pain of being shot if he steps outside. The whole book is the consequences of that one condition across three decades, with one lead and nearly all the page time on what he wants and why. It leaves you thinking about how a person keeps purpose and dignity when circumstances are fixed for good.

hannibal.blurb: Syracuse, 213 BC. A Roman army besieges the city; the Carthaginian Hanno serves inside the walls, his former friend Quintus in the legions outside, and Quintus's sister is held captive within.
hannibal.pitch: Syracuse, 213 BC: the Carthaginian Hanno serves inside the besieged walls, his former friend Quintus fights in the legions outside, and Quintus's sister is held captive within. Two friends on opposite sides of a siege, with a captured sister between them, put allegiance and loyalty in genuine conflict. Ben Kane's descriptive combat is praised.

hledani-modre.blurb: In a village that abandons the weak, the orphaned and lame Kira is spared because she can embroider. The Council of Guardians sets her to repairing the robe on which the village's whole history is recorded.
hledani-modre.pitch: In a village that discards the weak, a lame orphan girl is kept alive only because her hands are useful, and her job is to stitch the robe on which the village's whole past and future are recorded. It is short and built on one clear idea: whoever holds the picture of the past owns what a people believes about itself. You will be on Kira's side from the first page.

hluboke-pastviny.blurb: In a future where the oceans are farmed, Walter Franklin, a former spaceman who can no longer face space, retrains as a warden herding whales, and later administers the fisheries when their morality is challenged.
hluboke-pastviny.pitch: In a future where the oceans are farmed, Walter Franklin, a former spaceman who can no longer face space, retrains as a warden herding whales like cattle. Later he runs the fisheries when a religious leader argues that killing such creatures is murder. The idea is thought through rather than waved at, and it is also a story about finding a different kind of work.

hnev.blurb: King Nathair holds the fortress of Drassil and three of the Seven Treasures, and with all seven he can open a gate to the Otherworld for Asroth and his demons. Corban has been taken captive by the Jotun, giant warriors who ride to battle on bears, and his own army is scattered.
hnev.pitch: King Nathair holds the fortress of Drassil and three of the Seven Treasures, and with all seven he can open a gate to the Otherworld for Asroth and his demons, while Corban, captive of the giant Jotun who ride to battle on bears, has his own army scattered. It is the conclusion of a series that has been building for a long time: long-built arcs close, and characters who parted far back cross paths again, with reveals consistent with what came before.

inzerat-na-dum-ve-kterem-uz-nechci-bydle.blurb: Seven stories first collected in 1965. Four are set in the Kladno steelworks of the 1950s and three in Prague, following labourers and men conscripted to manual work - former tradesmen, lawyers and intellectuals - through an era Hrabal called the period of the cult of personality.

jak-byt-zenou.blurb: A first-person account of the author's life from adolescence through work, marriage, childbirth and an abortion, each chapter turning a personal episode into an argument about what is expected of women.

jak-stvorit-divku.blurb: In 1990 Wolverhampton, fourteen-year-old Johanna Morrigan reinvents herself as Dolly Wilde and talks her way into work as a music journalist in London.
jak-stvorit-divku.pitch: In 1990 Wolverhampton, fourteen-year-old Johanna Morrigan reinvents herself as Dolly Wilde and talks her way into work as a music journalist in London. Reviewers repeatedly call her witty, self-aware and sympathetic, a lead you cheer for. The story runs through family poverty, music criticism, class identity and growing up, and it is comic.

jasno-lepo-podstin-zhyna.blurb: In a small Irish seaside town a solitary fifty-seven-year-old man adopts a damaged one-eyed dog from a shelter and addresses the whole narrative to it across a year, until trouble forces the two of them onto the road.

jiskra-v-popelu.blurb: A Scholar girl whose brother is arrested for treason goes undercover as a slave in the household of a military academy's commandant, while one of the academy's top graduates, who intends to desert, is forced into a lethal contest to choose the next emperor.

kaleidoskop.blurb: Seventy short stories drawn from Bradbury's collections of 1950 to 1964, arranged in eight thematic sections ranging from horror and fantasy to future worlds, Mexico, Ireland and small-town America.

klara-a-slunce.blurb: Klara is a solar-powered Artificial Friend who watches the street from a store window until she is bought as a companion for a seriously ill teenage girl.
klara-a-slunce.pitch: Klara is an Artificial Friend who watches the street from a shop window until she is bought for a sick teenage girl, and everything she does is for that girl's good. Her narration is nothing but motive and inference, and it puts one question to her: whether a person is an irreplaceable centre or a learnable set of behaviours. Companionship and self-sacrifice, written quietly.

klec-dusi.blurb: Stefan Advani writes an account of his life from a prison island in the swamps outside Shadrapar, the last city of a humanity living under a dying, hostile sun.

kluby-poezie.blurb: A 1981 volume in which Bohumil Hrabal interleaved excerpts from two of his Liben prose works into a single alternating text, presented as a peripheral ballad in honour of the graphic artist Vladimir Boudnik.

kocka-a-cert.blurb: The town of Beaugency is split in two by the Loire and needs a bridge its citizens cannot build. The mayor strikes a bargain with the Devil, who will build it overnight in exchange for the soul of the first creature to cross.

kralovska-krev.blurb: Geder Palliako, a minor Antean nobleman, rises to Protector of the Prince, while the young banker Cithrin bel Sarcour and the mercenary Marcus Wester begin to grasp what the priests backing him are. War follows.
kralovska-krev.pitch: Continuing directly from the first book, Geder Palliako rises to Protector of the Prince while the banker Cithrin bel Sarcour and the mercenary Marcus Wester begin to grasp what the priests backing him are. Five viewpoints rotate chapter by chapter, each thinking differently, around a real idea: priests who hear certainty and take it for truth, in a world that keeps to its own rule. War follows.

krvavy-kamen.blurb: Twenty years after the Jerusalem Man disappeared, the Deacon rules from Unity and his Jerusalem Riders burn churches and hunt mutants. A wounded rider with no memory begins killing the killers, and word spreads that Shannow has returned.

lev.blurb: Athens after the Persian wars. The young Perikles serves under Kimon through the Delian League's campaigns from Eion to the Eurymedon, and comes of age between the battlefield and the city's assembly and theatre.
lev.pitch: Young Perikles serves under the veteran Kimon, whose respect he wants, in the campaigns after the Persian wars. The book stays close on one young man, and its idea is a generation that inherited a famous victory and has to work out who it is. The middle goes from the battlefield to a marriage, the assembly, and a festival where a man pays for a tragedy.

lincolnova-dalnice.blurb: June 1954: Emmett Watson, eighteen, is driven home to Nebraska after fifteen months in a juvenile work farm, planning to collect his eight-year-old brother and start again in California. Two friends who hid in the warden's trunk have a different destination in mind.
lincolnova-dalnice.pitch: Emmett Watson comes home from a work farm to a foreclosed Nebraska farm with a plan to drive his young brother to California, until two stowaways in the trunk send him east instead. Ten days on the road, told by many voices, each one showing you what that person is after and why. It has the feel of a quest, with a road for a map.

mapa-a-uzemi.blurb: Jed Martin becomes famous twice over, first for photographing Michelin maps and then as a painter of people at their work, while his relations with his dying architect father and with the writer he commissions for a catalogue essay run their course.

mesto-duchu.blurb: Cassidy Blake can cross the Veil that separates the living from the dead, and her best friend is a ghost. When her parents take their paranormal television show to Edinburgh, she meets another girl with the same ability and learns what she is supposed to do with it.

moc.blurb: The continent of the Banished Lands drifts toward war as an old prophecy of two opposed figures begins to be read. Corban, a blacksmith's son in the kingdom of Ardan, trains for his manhood trial while kings, queens and immortals manoeuvre around him.
moc.pitch: Family, loyalty and honour are the real subject here, not decoration. Roughly half the book sits with Corban, a blacksmith's son training for his manhood trial, who knows what he wants and is easy to root for, while kings, queens and immortals manoeuvre around him. A thick plot across a continent drifting toward war.

morantologie.blurb: A collection of the author's newspaper columns and interviews on television, politics, music, celebrity, the welfare state and family life.

most-dusi.blurb: Days after leaving Paris, Cassidy Blake travels to New Orleans with her ghost-hunting parents while a bone-masked emissary of death follows her. She and a fellow in-betweener look for a secret society that may know how to stop it.

my-ostatni-tu-proste-zijem.blurb: Mikey Mitchell is a high-school senior in a small Washington town where the Chosen Ones keep dying heroically. He mostly wants to graduate, keep his friends and tell Henna how he feels, while each chapter opens with a paragraph of the supernatural war going on elsewhere.
my-ostatni-tu-proste-zijem.pitch: Mikey just wants to graduate, keep his friends and tell Henna how he feels, while the Chosen Ones elsewhere keep dying heroically in a war that each chapter opens with in a paragraph. His OCD is written from the inside, and a reader with the condition says it is the first time she met her own symptoms in a book. A warm, funny story about four friends before the end of school.

myslete-na-deti.blurb: Fiona Maye, a High Court judge in the Family Division, must rule on whether a seventeen-year-old Jehovah's Witness dying of leukaemia can be given the blood transfusion he and his parents refuse, while her own marriage breaks open.
myslete-na-deti.pitch: Fiona Maye, a High Court judge in the Family Division, must rule on whether a seventeen-year-old Jehovah's Witness dying of leukaemia can be given the transfusion he and his parents refuse, while her own marriage breaks open. One question is posed precisely and then paid for, with an honest look at belief that neither mocks it nor concedes it.

na-hranicich-nadace.blurb: A Foundation councilman is exiled for arguing that the Second Foundation still exists and sent to look for it, while a rising Second Foundation speaker concludes that a third, stronger power is manipulating the Seldon Plan; both converge on an uncharted world.
na-hranicich-nadace.pitch: A Foundation councilman is exiled for arguing that the Second Foundation still exists and sent to look for it, while a rising Second Foundation speaker concludes that a third power is steering the Seldon Plan. It is driven by motive, with almost all of the page time on who wants what and why, and the question under it is whether a plan that foresees you leaves you anything to decide.

nadace-a-zeme.blurb: Golan Trevize, uneasy about the choice he has made for humanity's future, sets out with the historian Janov Pelorat to find Earth, whose records have been erased from every archive, travelling through a series of long-abandoned worlds.

najdi-odpoved.blurb: Arriving at the city they hoped would save them, Todd and Viola find the Mayor already in charge and are separated. Todd is put to work for the new regime while Viola falls in with the resistance, and each has to decide what they will do to survive and find the other.
najdi-odpoved.pitch: Todd and Viola reach the city that was supposed to save them and find the Mayor already in charge. Separated, Todd is put to work for the regime while Viola falls in with the resistance, and each has to decide what to agree to in order to survive and find the other. The question underneath is where the line between terrorist and freedom fighter lies, and how complicity is reached through small agreements.

nemame-na-vybranou.blurb: During a single day's truce in the Israeli-Arab fighting of 1948, ground crew at a Jerusalem airfield prepare a party for the pilots and nurses. Days earlier two pilots failed to return from a reconnaissance flight, and Johny Cohen is quietly planning what to do about it.

nesmrtelnost.blurb: A narrator watching a woman wave at her swimming instructor invents Agnes and follows her marriage, her sister and her death, interleaved with an account of Goethe's relations with Bettina von Arnim and with the narrator's own commentary on the book he is writing.

nikdy-nevystoupat-na-vrchol.blurb: Cognetti walks a circuit through the Nepalese Himalaya, recording the landscape, the people he meets and his companions, alongside reflections on solitude and friendship.

nokturna.blurb: Five loosely linked stories about musicians and music lovers, set in Venice, London, the English countryside and Beverly Hills.

oblazek-na-obloze.blurb: Joseph Schwartz, a retired tailor from twentieth-century Chicago, is thrown thousands of years into the future onto a radioactive, impoverished Earth that is a despised province of a galactic empire, and becomes the subject of a scientist's experiment while an archaeologist from off-world investigates Earth's claim to be humanity's origin.
oblazek-na-obloze.pitch: A retired tailor in Chicago, a laboratory accident, and he wakes on an Earth thousands of years older, a radioactive backwater despised by the galaxy. The hook is the unknown: a man who knows nothing about this world has to understand it to survive, while an archaeologist investigates Earth's claim to be where humanity began.

odvaha.blurb: The war for the Banished Lands widens as High King Nathair hunts the Seven Treasures and Queen Rhin takes the west. Corban flees his homeland with a small band while the demons of the Otherworld are loosed on the world of flesh.
odvaha.pitch: The war for the Banished Lands widens as High King Nathair hunts the Seven Treasures and Corban flees his homeland with a small band. The prophecy sets two named men against each other, one convinced he is the promised saviour, and the book questions it on the page rather than reciting it, spending its time on what a man wants and why he is wrong about it. The pace tightens as the demons of the Otherworld are loosed.

ohniva-pole.blurb: A year after Mars falls, the rebuilt human fleets launch an assault to take the planet back. Andrew Grayson and Diana Halley go in with the invasion force.
ohniva-pole.pitch: A year after Mars falls, the rebuilt human fleets launch an assault to take the planet back, and Andrew Grayson and Diana Halley go in with the invasion force. It is a campaign novel in which the plan does not survive contact, with combat writing that reviewers praise highly and real drive. One narrator tells it, and the opening is easy to follow.

olga.blurb: The life of a German woman born at the end of the nineteenth century: a village childhood, a long attachment to a man who leaves for the Arctic before the First World War, two wars, and her death in the early 1970s. The final part consists of her letters to him.
olga.pitch: One woman's life, told in order from her birth to her death: a village childhood, an attachment to a man who is always drawn toward the Arctic and far places, two wars. The idea at its core is large: a country taught to want everything on too grand a scale breeds men who chase vastness. The last part is her own letters.

orlove-v-bouri.blurb: Germanicus drives deeper into Germania to recover the last of the eagles lost at Teutoburg, while a Roman centurion pursues a personal reckoning with Arminius and a storm at sea wrecks part of the fleet.

ostri-snu.blurb: Garreth Left, heir to a declining Kithamar merchant house and promised to a strategic marriage, meets a woman by chance, abandons the path set for him and joins the city guard.
ostri-snu.pitch: Garreth Left, heir to a declining Kithamar merchant house and promised to a strategic marriage, meets a woman by chance and abandons the path set for him to join the city guard. Elaine, the prince's daughter, sets out to learn what has changed her father. Duty against desire drives it, both leads are flawed and easy to cheer for, and the city's theology of gods made real by belief is praised. It reads as a standalone.

ozveny-velke-pisne.blurb: The Avatars, a near-immortal caste sustained by failing crystals, rule the remnants of a drowned world. When two moons appear and the Crystal Queen's armies land, the Avatars make common cause with their own subjects.
ozveny-velke-pisne.pitch: The Avatars, a near-immortal caste kept alive by failing crystals, rule the remnants of a drowned world. When two moons appear and the Crystal Queen's armies land, they make common cause with their own subjects. The book spends its time on what rulers and ruled want from each other, with heroism and loyalty inside a small band, starting from a warrior and two companions sent to re-energise the crystals.

pavouci-valka.blurb: The war against the goddess's priests reaches its end: a tired mercenary captain, a banker willing to break the rules of profit, and the last living dragon converge on an empire that has never lost a battle.
pavouci-valka.pitch: The war against the goddess's priests reaches its end, with a tired mercenary captain, a banker willing to break the rules of profit and the last living dragon converging on an empire that has never lost a battle. The question is how to end a war without seeding the next, and who answers for a nation talked into atrocity. Read after the four volumes before it.

perlicka-na-dne.blurb: Bohumil Hrabal's first published book of short stories (1963), portraits of ordinary men from the lower reaches of society - railwaymen, foundry workers, pub regulars - who turn out to be compulsive and brilliant tellers of their own lives.

pisek.blurb: Generations after civilisation was buried under sand, four siblings in a dune-top town search for their father, one of the divers who descend hundreds of feet into the desert for salvage, and for a lost city said to lie a mile down.

platforma.blurb: Michel, a bored official at the French Ministry of Culture, comes into an inheritance and travels to Thailand, where he meets a travel executive named Valerie; together they design a chain of holiday resorts built around paid sex.

posel-v-temnem-lese.blurb: Matty, a boy taken in years earlier by a village that shelters outcasts, carries messages through the forest. As the village turns against strangers and its people begin trading away parts of themselves, he learns what his own gift is for.
posel-v-temnem-lese.pitch: Matty carries messages through the forest for a village that has always sheltered outcasts, and then its people start to trade away parts of themselves at a strange market while the community quietly votes itself a wall. A short allegory built on one clear idea and followed to its consequences, told close to one person, with something to think about afterwards.

posledni-hlidka.blurb: Major Andrew Grayson and the crew of the Washington are stranded nine hundred light years from home in a sunless system, running out of water, fuel and food. The only moon showing signs of life offers food - and is infested with the enemy.
posledni-hlidka.pitch: Major Andrew Grayson and the crew of the Washington are stranded nine hundred light years from home in a sunless system, running low on water, fuel and food. The only moon showing signs of life offers food and is infested with the enemy. A crew rather than a lone survivor, and a question about whether the enemy fought for years as a mindless swarm is really that.

posledni-strazce.blurb: Two years after the Hellborn war, Jon Shannow is found near death in the mountains and drawn into a second conflict, with part of the story set in an ancient civilisation before its fall.

pozdni-zivot.blurb: Martin, a seventy-six-year-old emeritus professor of legal history with a much younger wife and a six-year-old son, is diagnosed with terminal cancer and sets about leaving the boy a letter.
pozdni-zivot.pitch: A man of seventy-six with a young wife and a six-year-old son is told he has about twelve weeks left. The book stays almost wholly inside his head and asks what a father can hand to a child he will not see grow up, and what a life adds up to once the accounting is forced. One man, one situation, and a letter to write.

prach.blurb: The isolated silos converge: a mayor drives a digging machine toward a neighbouring silo while taking air samples outside, and in the silo that controls them all a man and his sister try to stop the shutdown of the rest.
