ohnivy-kvet.blurb: After the warlord Aric Athair's army kills her family, Caledonia Styx captains an all-female crew of survivors on the deadly Bullet seas, determined to bring him down.

opacna-strana.blurb: After his best friend's death, grieving teenager Theo watches his town flip upside-down into a monstrous alternate reality that embodies his depression, and must navigate it with a sharp-tongued girl who understands the flipped world better than he does.
opacna-strana.pitch: After his best friend dies, Theo watches his town flip upside down into a monstrous alternate world that is his depression given form. He has to cross it with a sharp-tongued girl who understands it better than he does. A real feeling made into a place and followed all the way through, and reviewers say the ending feels earned.

opskurno.blurb: In the isolated, self-governing English town of Rotherweird, a new history teacher and the arrival of a sinister newcomer set off a chain of events that begins to expose the magical secret the town has hidden since its Tudor founding.
opskurno.pitch: In the isolated, self-governing English town of Rotherweird, a new history teacher and a sinister newcomer start exposing a magical secret buried since the town's Tudor founding. The town is forbidden to investigate its own past, so history itself is dangerous, and reviewers call the payoff of the layered mystery strong. The Old History interludes show magical-scientific experiments with real costs.

orcigard.blurb: Orcigard, once the realm of the bird-headed pterrs and now a vast swamp of ruined temples, is still nominally ruled by the fading Dark Mage Alarich Touraine as rebellions and treasure-hunters close in. Sylvia Viktorina, the youngest daughter of the Duke of Barro, is swept into the swamp and must find allies among adventurers, orcs and monsters to survive.
orcigard.pitch: Sylvia Viktorina, the youngest daughter of the Duke of Barro, is swept into the swamp of Orcigard and must build alliances among adventurers, orcs and monsters to survive. Readers praise her as a character distinct from the generic love-interest type, interesting and worth cheering for. The swamp is a realm of ruined temples once ruled by bird-headed pterrs.

pan-ledove-zahrady.blurb: Earth commando Vuko Drakkainen is sent alone to an alien planet, Midgaard, to find a missing scientific expedition, and discovers some of its members have seized magical power and declared themselves gods amid a war that is killing the natives.
pan-ledove-zahrady.pitch: Vuko Drakkainen is sent alone to the planet Midgaard to find a lost scientific expedition, forbidden to interfere. He has to understand a culture and a catastrophe he knows nothing about before he can decide what to do, and what happened to the expedition is the question that draws you in.

pisen-o-dvernikovi.blurb: The Doorkeeper opens and closes the gates of a sentient magical House, loving a princess, serving kings and befriending executioners while remaining the House's slave; his story is intercut with that of a boy who wants to invent doors.

po-schodech-nahoru-dolu.blurb: Two ten-year-old boys, Alex and Max, discover they live in the same house in two parallel realities and begin visiting each other at night, but their friendship threatens to merge the two worlds together.

posledni-iluze.blurb: Two Stockholm teenagers, Ky and Adam, discover a hole behind the wall of Ky's bedroom and strange shifts in Adam's everyday reality, and are drawn into a plot that upends what they thought was real.

pristav-nebezpeci.blurb: A solo-adventure gamebook in which the reader plays a down-on-their-luck treasure hunter crossing the Allansia setting, with the choices made determining whether an old enemy's return is stopped.

skandar-a-kostliva-kletba.blurb: Skandar and his friends begin their fourth year of training at the Eyrie when a terrible curse strikes the unicorns, threatening to upend everything just as training intensifies.

skandar-a-prizracny-jezdec.blurb: Second-years at the Eyrie face a new threat as wild unicorns, meant to be immortal, are being savagely killed, an ancient prophecy surfaces, and storms begin to ravage the island; meanwhile Skandar's sister Kenna tries to reach the island to train alongside him.

skandar-a-souteze-chaosu.blurb: Third-years at the Eyrie must survive a set of dangerous competitions staged across the island's elemental territories, testing friendships and rider-unicorn bonds to breaking point, while Skandar's sister Kenna, now on the island but bonded to a wild unicorn, feels isolated as a discovery threatens the island's future.

stinove-eso.blurb: When her mother disappears in the crime-ridden City of Sin, proper young Enne Salta must team up with con man and street lord Levi Glaisyer to find her, uncovering a conspiracy tangled in casinos, gangs and a magic system built on family lineage.

stiny-halloweenu.blurb: A Horror Writers Association anthology of sixteen new stories built around Halloween and related holidays, from jack-o'-lantern origin myths to modern trick-or-treating horror.

svetla-na-obloze.blurb: On a frozen island where lights in the sky foretell fortune or doom, a girl braves the wilderness to learn why the sky has turned an ominous red, while a young man tries to unite the villages against approaching danger.

terry-pratchett.blurb: A biography and literary study of Terry Pratchett covering more than 40 years of his work, including an extensive bibliography and collector's guide.

trpytny-dvur.blurb: Mira, a refugee posing as a marriageable lady at the Glittering Court finishing school, partners with a shipboard spy to earn her freedom and uncovers a plot to start a war between the colonies and the native Icori.

upiri-z-morganville.blurb: In the vampire-and-human town of Morganville, a power struggle between the ruling vampire Amelie and her rebellious father Bishop comes to a head as a natural disaster and a human uprising threaten the town at the same time.

urla.blurb: Ilan wakes the swords and forcibly seizes the freedom the sklenari have always wanted, but in doing so takes several warriors with her underground, into places they are not welcome, and must first persuade her men to follow or at least walk beside her.

valecna-lest.blurb: A short-story collection set in the Krvave pohranici borderland world, drawing together older and newer texts linked by a recurring hero or group of heroes rather than a single continuous plot.

valka.blurb: When Jerusalem falls to War and his army, Miriam Elmahdy is claimed by the horseman as his 'wife.' Drawn into his camp and his campaign of destruction, she has to decide whether love can survive - or stop - a being who is war itself.

ve-stinu-vlci-kralovny.blurb: Ysolda has always felt safe in her forest home despite the Wolf Queen's tyranny, until an earthquake shakes her village and her older sister Hari vanishes. With her sea hawk Nara, Ysolda strikes a dangerous bargain with the Wolf Queen herself to get her sister back, and is drawn into a quest for a magic more powerful than she understands.
ve-stinu-vlci-kralovny.pitch: An earthquake shakes Ysolda's quiet forest village and her older sister Hari vanishes. With her sea hawk Nara, Ysolda bargains with the Wolf Queen herself. Behind the quest is a real idea: a ruler's hunger for power is literally poisoning the land, and an unlikely heroine has to face what that rule costs. Illustrated, with a magic drawn from nature, ley lines and listening to trees.

vypravec.blurb: In the fictional village of Běstviny, a legend holds that a giant worm lives beneath the garden and must be fed; when the grandfather dies, one of his grandchildren must take his place, and the story's own characters begin to resist the narrator telling it.

zimni-drak.blurb: A winter dragon that carries away snow each spring injures its wing and cannot leave; a girl must help it heal so spring can finally arrive.

zlata-grai.blurb: Isarell, of the near-extinct grai race, survives two years alone in the hostile Shadowlands to earn a place under the mad wild-women queen Ymira's command, alongside her sworn-sibling bond with Bastien.
zlata-grai.pitch: Isarell, one of the near-extinct grai, survives two years alone in the hostile Shadowlands to earn a place under the mad wild-women queen Ymira, with her sworn sibling Bastien beside her. She is brave and capable, and the immersive world is thick with faction names and rules. The ending is repeatedly singled out as the best part, one reviewer finishing standing up with a hand on the light switch.

zmije-a-vlk.blurb: Vaasa, sole heir to an uncontrollable dark magic that killed her mother, is married off by her power-hungry brother to a ruthless foreign ruler as a political weapon, and finds the marriage may be the only way to survive her own power.

artemis-fowl-a-atlantsky-komplex.blurb: The teenage genius Artemis Fowl develops a guilt-driven disorder that splits him into a gentle alter ego while the fairy world is attacked by an old enemy and a curse enslaves him and an elf captain.

bezcasi.blurb: Once a century the gods walk among humans for twelve hours and lose their immortality. In 1932 Czechoslovakia a goddess's servant is caught in the event, while a century later a young woman tries to travel against the flow of time to change a pandemic world.

carodejcin-syn.blurb: After one of two twins drowns in an enchanted river, the survivor Ned is blamed by his village for being the wrong boy who lived. When the Bandit King comes to steal the magic his witch mother guards, Ned takes it and runs, with the Bandit King's daughter helping him.

dallas-63.blurb: English teacher Jake Epping steps through a diner's portal into 1958 and spends five years in the past trying to stop the assassination of John F. Kennedy, falling in love along the way.
dallas-63.pitch: Jake Epping, an English teacher, steps through a diner's portal into 1958 with a task: stop the Kennedy assassination. The past resists change and makes the traveller pay each time, and the love story along the way is what makes his choices cost him something. You read it in his first-person voice, and it keeps asking whether history should be changed at all.

dcera-kosti-a-dymu.blurb: Karou, a blue-haired art student in Prague, runs errands collecting teeth for the chimaera Brimstone, who raises the dead and grants wishes. When burning handprints appear on his doors an angel, Akiva, finds her and her buried past comes back.

divka-ktera-upijela-mesic.blurb: Each year the Protectorate leaves a baby in the forest for a feared witch, who is in fact kind and carries the children to families in distant cities. One year she accidentally feeds a baby moonlight as well as starlight, fills the child with magic and raises her as her own.
divka-ktera-upijela-mesic.pitch: Each year a baby is left in the forest for a feared witch, and the Protectorate keeps its people obedient with that fear. Several viewpoint characters each want something different, and the manufactured fear begins to come apart through those wants. A fable about fear and sorrow as instruments of rule, in the vein of Animal Farm, with a thirteen-year-old at its centre.

dny-krve-a-hvezdneho-trpytu.blurb: After the wishbone breaks and her past returns, Karou resurrects an army for a chimaera warlord while the angel Akiva tries to undo the war that destroyed her people.

duna-frank-herbert.blurb: In a feudal interstellar empire, Duke Leto Atreides's house is handed control of the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the spice. His son Paul and concubine Jessica must survive a betrayal and the planet's desert people, whose legends the Bene Gesserit order has long cultivated.
duna-frank-herbert.pitch: In a feudal interstellar empire, House Atreides is handed the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the spice. Paul and his mother Jessica must survive betrayal and the desert people whose legends an order has long cultivated. A scarce resource, an engineered religious myth and a messiah story examined rather than celebrated, all told through what Jessica, Paul and the great houses want.

jmeno-vetru.blurb: Kvothe, now a hidden innkeeper, tells a chronicler the true story of his life: a childhood with travelling players, the murder of his troupe by legendary beings, and his struggle to enter the University.
jmeno-vetru.pitch: A hidden legend running a quiet inn sits down to give a chronicler the true story of his life, and you want to know how the man became the story. Childhood among travelling players, a hunger for music, a grudge against those who ended that life, and the long road to the University. The magic works like engineering, with rules and costs you can reason about.

koruna-z-carodreva.blurb: Thirty years after the Storm King's defeat, an aged King Simon and Queen Miriamele face failing allies, an idle grandson and a stirring Norn queen who sends a warband north to find a dead prince's remains.
koruna-z-carodreva.pitch: Thirty years after the Storm King's defeat, an aged King Simon and Queen Miriamele face failing allies, an idle grandson and a stirring Norn queen. A long, character-led epic that returns to a king grown old, with grief, succession and the cost of earlier victories. The Norn viewpoint chapters are praised for making a dying people sympathetic.

mesto-zazraku.blurb: Sigrud, an ageing northern fighter living in obscurity, learns that his former employer and closest friend, the one-time prime minister Shara Komayd, has been killed in a bomb blast. He sets out to find the killers and is pulled into a decades-long hidden conflict.
mesto-zazraku.pitch: Sigrud, an ageing northern fighter living in obscurity, learns that his closest friend and former employer, the one-time prime minister Shara Komayd, has been killed in a bomb blast, and sets out to find the killers. Around him the series' big idea reaches its close: what mortals owe to gods, what they can do without them and what a miracle costs. Reviewers call it a satisfying finish.

mycelium.blurb: At the peak of the Star Rule, the Sgen, Ships, a church and humans compete to format the world's future while Lucas claims his share and demands sacrifices.

oddelene-duse.blurb: An undead emperor and a bishop lead an army of the half-dead into D'Hara while Richard and Kahlan, near death themselves, search for a way to be cured of the stain of death.

odinovo-dite.blurb: Fifteen-year-old Hirka learns on the eve of her Rite that she is a tailless child from another world, and flees a theocratic empire that would destroy her. Her aristocratic childhood rival Rime is drawn into the secret.
odinovo-dite.pitch: Hirka is fifteen in a world where everyone has a tail and can bind the Might, and she has neither, with her Rite only days away. You follow a hunted outsider with a real problem and a lot of nerve. Where she really comes from and what the Council hides in the name of faith are the questions she must answer to survive, and the book keeps asking what blind belief and fear of strangers do to a society.

ohen-probuzeni.blurb: In a world whose economy runs on the blood of drakes, an unregistered blood-blessed thief, a syndicate spy and a naval officer are drawn toward the hunt for a white drake nesting ground.
ohen-probuzeni.pitch: In a world whose economy runs on the blood of drakes, a thief, a syndicate spy and a naval officer are drawn toward the hunt for a white drake nesting ground. Drake blood grants abilities by colour and dose, a system with set costs, inside a colonial-trade conflict. The economy is built into the world rather than decorating it.

oko-sveta.blurb: Rand al'Thor, a shepherd from a remote village, learns that he and his friends are hunted by the servants of the Dark One. Guided by the Aes Sedai Moiraine and her Warder Lan, they leave home on a long journey.
oko-sveta.pitch: Rand al'Thor, a shepherd from a remote village, learns that he and his friends are hunted by the servants of the Dark One, and leaves home with the Aes Sedai Moiraine and her Warder Lan. It starts in an easy-to-follow farm village with an ordinary boy pulled into a hunt, and its themes are friendship and heroism, with a power that has clear rules. It is the same heroic journey as The Lord of the Rings.

okovy-osudu.blurb: An immortal tyrant's army marches while a priest receives a vision from his goddess, and a killer is drawn into a fight over his slaughtered family's legacy.

pisen-krve.blurb: Vaelin Al Sorna is left at the gate of the Sixth Order as a child and trained to fight in the service of the Faith. Years later, a royal scribe records the story of the man now called the Hope Killer.
pisen-krve.pitch: Vaelin Al Sorna is left at the gate of the Sixth Order as a child and raised to fight in the service of the Faith. Years on, a royal scribe records the story of the man now condemned as the Hope Killer, so who he is and why is the open question. It is loyalty, brotherhood and what he is made to do to keep his ideals, with the open-past lead you enjoyed in Licanius.

rise-trav.blurb: Simon, who once slew a dragon, rules a kingdom where old friends have died, enemies have grown strong and a magic-caused sickness and monsters spread, while the Norn queen advances her plan.

sesterstvo-duny.blurb: Eight decades after the last thinking machines were destroyed, the new empire rules while the Sisterhood forms on Rossak around a healer who survived poison, and a Harkonnen daughter joins it to restore her disgraced family.

shannarovy-magicke-elfeiny.blurb: Fifty years after the fall of the Warlock Lord, the tree that holds demons behind the Forbidding is dying, and a young Healer with the last Elfstones must escort an Elven girl to the one fire that can renew it.
shannarovy-magicke-elfeiny.pitch: Fifty years after the Warlock Lord's fall, the tree that holds demons behind the Forbidding is dying, and a reluctant young Healer with the last Elfstones must escort an Elven girl to the one fire that can renew it. A tight quest with a concrete start and a pair who each have something to overcome: he is reluctant, she ran from her duty and must face it. Easy adventure with friendship, in the same vein as The Hobbit.

sila.blurb: Hirka, cast as a symbol of hatred among the feared blind, prepares to confront the ruling house to save her friend Rime and protect her adopted world, while the dead-born's thirst for power makes war unavoidable.

stribrna-maska.blurb: Held in prison as the vessel of a dark mage, Call is freed on condition that he bring his dead friend back to life, discovering what the power he fears can really do.

stribrny-trn.blurb: After a poisoned arrow strikes his bride at their wedding, Prince Arutha sets out with a bard and a young thief to find the rare silverthorn cure while a dark moredhel sorcerer assembles an army.

tamuli.blurb: Six years after the Church Knights defeated their god-enemy, the Tamul Empire summons the knight Sparhawk to help against a rising threat from the east, a quest that leads to the Sapphire Rose and a hidden city of the god Cyrgon.

vyvrhel.blurb: Alwyn Scribe grows up among outlaws in the kingdom of Albermaine. After a betrayal he joins the royal army under Lady Evadine Courlain, a noblewoman haunted by visions of a demonic apocalypse.
vyvrhel.pitch: Alwyn Scribe, an outlaw turned soldier, writes his life down in his own voice, shaped by what he wants and whom he comes to be loyal to. After a betrayal he joins the royal army under a noblewoman haunted by visions of a demonic apocalypse. Readers compare the revenge-and-loyalty drive to Monte Cristo.

zlobryne-a-sirotci.blurb: In a town ruined by fire and bitterness, a smiling mayor persuades everyone to blame a gentle ogress on the edge of town when a child goes missing. Three orphans who know better set out to expose him.

atomove-selmy.blurb: In a post-nuclear Czech wasteland the sheriff and a novice of the Church of the Nuclear Goddess try to push through to the secrets buried beneath the church's Cemetery and save a world that may not want saving.

perla-petrohradu.blurb: St Petersburg, 1910: seventeen-year-old pianist Valentina Ivanova, promised by her parents to a count, wants to train as a nurse after a Bolshevik bomb cripples her sister. She falls in love with the Danish engineer Jens Friis.

vsemi-dary-obdarovana.blurb: Ten-year-old Melanie is held on a military base where she is strapped down and taught in a classroom, because she is one of the children infected by a fungus that turns most people into flesh-eating hungries. When the base falls, she flees across a ruined England with her teacher, a soldier, a sergeant and a scientist who wants to dissect her.
vsemi-dary-obdarovana.pitch: Melanie is a ten-year-old strapped into a chair and taught in a classroom on a military base, because she is one of the children infected by the fungus that turns people into hungries. When the base falls she flees across ruined England with her teacher, a soldier, a sergeant and a scientist who wants to dissect her. What she is, and what the world really is, drive the book, along with what makes a person human.

zimni-cisar.pitch: An unprepared, unwanted young emperor, kind and flawed, finds himself on the throne of a court that despises him and visibly works to understand it. The book spends its pages on what the courtiers want and why, and his own past is an open question. The pull is court survival.
zimni-cisar.blurb: Maia, the half-goblin fourth son of the elven emperor, raised in exile in a lonely house in the marshes, becomes emperor when an airship disaster kills his father and brothers, and has to learn a court that never wanted him.

kroniky-zapadniho-pobrezi.pitch: Three linked novels with concrete ideas: inherited gifts that are dangerous to their owners, books burned and a people who revere the written word facing a conquering faith that forbids it, and slavery seen from inside. Each lead is a young person with a gift he or she does not want to use as intended, and the page time goes to what they want and why.
kroniky-zapadniho-pobrezi.blurb: Three loosely linked novels of the Western Shore: highland families whose inherited gifts can kill, a city whose conquerors have banned its books, and an enslaved boy who remembers things that have not happened yet.

jatka-c-5-aneb-krizova-vyprava-deti-povi.pitch: Billy has come unstuck in time, and the Tralfamadorian view that every moment exists permanently turns war, fate and free will into a concrete argument. The time-jumps are explained outright in the opening pages, so you are never lost. Short and idea-driven, it leaves that argument behind with you.
jatka-c-5-aneb-krizova-vyprava-deti-povi.blurb: Billy Pilgrim, an American prisoner of war who lives through the firebombing of Dresden, has come unstuck in time and experiences the moments of his life out of order, including those he spends on the planet Tralfamadore.

deti-duny.pitch: A long argument about what a messiah and a prescient golden path cost, driven by what the regent, the twins, the mother and the Preacher each want and fear. Foreknowledge is questioned seriously within its own rules, the handling you praised in the Licanius books. The Dune saga continues here, with ideas and motives doing the carrying.
deti-duny.blurb: Years after Paul Atreides walked into the desert, his twins Leto and Ghanima grow up on a greening Arrakis, while a priesthood rules in Paul's name and their aunt Alia, the regent, struggles with the voices of her ancestors.

strazcove-varadinu.pitch: A father who failed his twelve-year-old son after his wife's death loses the boy and has to put that right while a fortress faces an overwhelming Ottoman army. The lead has a flaw to work against and a want that drives the plot. It is set in a real war rather than an invented world, with light fantasy tied to local superstition.
strazcove-varadinu.blurb: 1660: Captain Kornel Báthory, swordsman and poet, who turned away from his son after his wife's death, sets out to make it right just as the fortress of Varadín faces an Ottoman army. First book of Captain Báthory's adventures.

vzpominka-na-zemi-3.pitch: The ideas are the draw: a cosmos run by dark-forest logic, deterrence and weapons that work across dimensions, with every consequence followed out to the far end of the universe. If you loved the way Project Hail Mary keeps thinking one step further, this is that appetite on a cosmic scale, with a woman at the centre whose choices carry the weight.
vzpominka-na-zemi-3.blurb: Half a century after the Doomsday Battle, an uneasy truce between humanity and the Trisolarans rests on dark-forest deterrence while Earth prospers on alien technology. The closing book of the Three-Body trilogy.

o-psu-nemluve.pitch: A comic time-travel farce in which the continuum repairs itself and tracks incongruities, and that rule fuels every complication. It is a light, clean romance in the comic-SF spirit of Hitchhiker's Guide, with the consequences of its idea carried through, and a time-lagged narrator who is as lost as you are.
o-psu-nemluve.blurb: Two worn-out Oxford historians travel to Victorian England to put right a hideous piece of decorative art, a romance that has gone the wrong way and a bombing raid that may not happen, before the damage spreads centuries forward.

anomalie.blurb: An Air France flight survives violent turbulence and lands in March; in June the same plane lands again, and every passenger now has a double.
anomalie.pitch: An Air France flight survives terrible turbulence and lands in March; in June the same plane, with the same passengers, lands again. You meet an assassin, an editor, a pilot, a writer and a singer, each living a different life, and watch them and the authorities face what that means. A clever, fast read about what you would do if you met another you.

antikomunisticke-manifesty.blurb: A medievalist examines four books by former communists that shaped Cold War opinion: Darkness at Noon, Out of the Night, I Chose Freedom and Witness.
antikomunisticke-manifesty.pitch: Fleming reads four books by former communists, Darkness at Noon, Out of the Night, I Chose Freedom and Witness, and shows how each came to be written and why they shaped the way the West saw the Soviet Union. You get the stories behind the authors, journalists, a sailor and an engineer, and what led each to break with the cause.

archiv-ticha.blurb: An apprentice meets the secrets of sound and a forgotten civilisation around the inventor of the piano, Bartolomeo Cristofori, at the Medici court.
archiv-ticha.pitch: What if the piano was never invented, only found again? An apprentice at the Medici court meets the secrets of sound, the memory of tone and a forgotten civilisation. It is a short historical novel with a daring idea at its centre.
archiv-ticha.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

autismus-bez-masky.blurb: A psychologist describes masked autism in adults, why people hide it, and a guide to dropping the mask.
autismus-bez-masky.pitch: Many adults spend their energy hiding the way their minds work. Devon Price draws on research and personal stories to show how masking autism looks in practice, why it is exhausting and what it can take to stop.

bohove-s-implantaty.blurb: The book walks through the secret teachings and myths of Scientology and tells cases of its spread in the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
bohove-s-implantaty.pitch: A guided tour through the doctrine of Scientology, from its founder's hidden writings to the myths of alien civilisations its members are asked to believe. Local stories from the Czech Republic and Slovakia show how the organisation made its way in.
bohove-s-implantaty.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

chladna-ruka-v-moji-dlani.blurb: Eight stories of the strange in ordinary settings, among them a man who spends a night in a hospice and a girl's journal.
chladna-ruka-v-moji-dlani.pitch: Eight unsettling stories set in plain English rooms and streets, where something inexplicable is quietly wrong. One of them won the World Fantasy Award. You get atmosphere and dread more than answers.

chybny-protokol.blurb: Murderbot, a security android that has freed itself, goes to an abandoned terraforming facility to find proof of a corporation's illegal work, and finds a human survey team, hired guards and a trusting companion robot.
chybny-protokol.pitch: Murderbot, a security android that would much rather watch its serials, travels to an abandoned terraforming facility to dig up proof against a ruthless corporation. There it finds a human survey team and Miki, a cheerful companion robot who trusts everyone. Dry, sarcastic narration from inside the lead's head, and plenty of action.

cihostsky-zazrak.blurb: A reconstruction of the alleged miracle in the village of Cihost in 1949 and the persecution and death of Father Josef Toufar at the hands of the state security.
cihostsky-zazrak.pitch: In December 1949 a cross was said to have moved in a village church, and the communist regime used it to go after the priest. This is the most complete account of what happened, drawn from interrogation records and the testimony of those present, with a foreword by Petr Pithart.
cihostsky-zazrak.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

cisarstvi-ticha.blurb: Hadrian Marlowe, remembered as both hero and monster, narrates his youth as a nobleman's son on a feudal desert world within an empire at war with an alien enemy.
cisarstvi-ticha.pitch: Hadrian Marlowe, remembered by some as a hero and by others as the monster who burned the sky, tells how he began as a boy on a feudal desert world, far from any war. You get a long, voice-driven space epic in his own words: an empire at war with an alien enemy nobody understands, and the choices that made him who he became. The story lives in what he wants and why.

cizincem-v-olondrii.blurb: Jevick, a pepper merchant's son from the Tea Islands raised on stories of Olondria, travels there after his father's death and is haunted by the ghost of a young woman.
cizincem-v-olondrii.pitch: Jevick, a pepper merchant's son raised on stories of the northern land of Olondria, finally travels there and finds himself haunted by the ghost of a young woman. It is a lyrical fantasy about what books and reading do to a person, told as one man's journey through a richly imagined country.
cizincem-v-olondrii.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

den-kdy-evropa-ztichla.blurb: After Europe loses all signal, four retired soldiers cross devastated Slovakia in search of an answer.
den-kdy-evropa-ztichla.pitch: Europe has gone silent, with no signal and no lights, and four old soldiers set out across Slovakia to find out why. The talk along the road is about what remains of people when the systems that ruled them are gone.
den-kdy-evropa-ztichla.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

dvoreni-bristol-keatsove.blurb: After losing both parents, Bristol Keats learns that her father may be alive in a realm of fae and monsters, and goes after him, striking a deadly bargain with the fae king.
dvoreni-bristol-keatsove.pitch: Bristol Keats and her sisters have lost both parents, until mysterious letters hint that their father is alive in a realm of fae, gods and monsters. She goes after him and strikes a dangerous bargain with the fae king, who has his own reasons to resent her family. It is a slow-burning fantasy full of banter and secrets.

ekonomie-dobra-a-zla.blurb: An economist reads the history of economic thought through ancient epics, scripture and philosophy to ask what good and evil mean for economics.
ekonomie-dobra-a-zla.pitch: Why do we treat economics as pure mathematics when it began as stories about right and wrong? Sedlacek follows the question from Gilgamesh through the Bible, Aristotle and Descartes to the financial crisis. It is written for people who are not economists and leaves you with a lot to argue about.

eldest-mekka-vazba.blurb: Eragon travels with the dragon Saphira to the elven city of Ellesmera to train as a Dragon Rider while the king's darkness grows over the land.
eldest-mekka-vazba.pitch: Eragon travels with his dragon Saphira to the elven city of Ellesmera to train as a Dragon Rider, in swordsmanship and magic, while the shadow of the king deepens over the land and it becomes harder to know whom to trust. It is a big adventure fantasy built around a boy, his dragon and their apprenticeship.

faktomluva.blurb: Hans Rosling shows how ten instincts make us misjudge the state of the world, and how looking at the numbers shows it is better than most people believe.
faktomluva.pitch: Most of us are wrong about the world, and not because we are foolish. Rosling, a doctor who spent his life with real numbers, shows ten instincts that mislead us and how to spot them, with stories from his own career. You come away seeing the news differently.

galejnicka-extraliga.blurb: Loretta Thurwar and Hamara 'Staxxx' Stacker are stars of a televised prison league in which convicts fight for freedom, and the book follows them and those who run, watch and protest the spectacle.
galejnicka-extraliga.pitch: Loretta Thurwar and Hamara Stacker are the biggest stars of a televised league where convicts fight for their freedom, and the book follows them and the people who run, watch and protest the spectacle. It asks what a society owes the people it locks up, with footnotes that tie the fiction to real cases.

gen.blurb: Mukherjee tells the history of the gene from Mendel's peas to gene editing, interleaved with the story of mental illness in his own family.
gen.pitch: From a monk counting peas to the editing of human genes, this is the story of how we learned what heredity is, told through the people who chased the answer. Interleaved is the author's own family and the question of what it passes on, so a big subject keeps a human face.

hardcore-historie.blurb: Carlin looks at apocalyptic moments of the past, from the Bronze Age collapse to the fall of Rome and Cold War nuclear brinkmanship, and asks whether we could face something similar.
hardcore-historie.pitch: Dan Carlin tells the great collapses of the past as stories about real people deciding in terrible moments, and then asks whether something like them could come for us. It is written the way he speaks on his podcast, with asides, quotations from the sources and a feel for how strange the past really was.

hleda-se-autor-bestselleru-2015-sci-fi-a.blurb: The fifth year of a Fragment writing contest, focused on sci-fi and fantasy; five best short stories chosen by readers and a jury.
hleda-se-autor-bestselleru-2015-sci-fi-a.pitch: Five short stories picked from more than two hundred entries in a Czech contest for new sci-fi and fantasy writers, chosen by readers and an expert jury. A quick way to meet five new voices in the genre, each story short enough to read in one sitting.
hleda-se-autor-bestselleru-2015-sci-fi-a.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

instalace-strachu.blurb: Two technicians arrive at a family's door to install fear in the home under a government decree, and perform an unsettling show for the woman who let them in while her son hides in the bathroom.
instalace-strachu.pitch: A doorbell rings, a mother hides her son in the bathroom, and two polite technicians step in to install fear in the house as if it were cable television. It is a short satire about how easily a society can be steered by what it is afraid of, and the idea stays with you after the last page, much as Animal Farm does.
instalace-strachu.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

The test that tells them from people is built on empathy, and as he works through it you keep asking what that word really means. It is short, sharp and full of ideas to chew on.

casokryt.blurb: A narrator assists a therapist who opens clinics where Alzheimer's patients live inside a faithfully rebuilt past, a decade on each floor.
casokryt.pitch: A man helps an enigmatic therapist open clinics for people losing their memory, each floor rebuilt in perfect detail as a different decade of the past. The idea slips out of the clinics, and the longing for yesterday spreads far beyond them. A bright, odd novel that leaves you thinking about nostalgia and what we do when the future looks frightening.

casotreseni.blurb: After the universe hiccups and replays ten years, humanity must live through them again on autopilot, while the author wanders through memories and the stories of his invented writer Kilgore Trout.
casotreseni.pitch: Everyone is thrown back ten years and forced to relive them without any free will. It is a short, funny, rambling visit with Vonnegut and his alter ego Kilgore Trout, full of his dry views on being a person.

chvalozpev-na-leibowitze.blurb: After a nuclear war, an order of monks preserves scraps of lost knowledge through centuries as civilisation rebuilds toward the same disaster.
chvalozpev-na-leibowitze.pitch: After the nuclear fire, a monastic order keeps the scraps of what the world knew, in the hope that someone will one day use them better. The book follows them across thousands of years as knowledge returns and old mistakes come back with it. You are left thinking about faith, science and whether people ever learn.

darwinie.blurb: In 1912 a cosmic event called the Miracle replaces Europe with a continent of alien wildlife. In 1920 photographer Guilford Law joins an expedition up the Rhine to document it.
darwinie.pitch: In 1912 Europe vanishes overnight, replaced by a strange wild continent, and by 1920 an expedition sets out across it with a photographer to record what no one understands. The land hides an explanation bigger than anyone guesses, and finding out what happened is the whole reason to keep reading.

dedictvi.blurb: Yeine Darr, an outcast from a northern tribe, is summoned to the floating capital after her mother's suspicious death and named heir to the king, putting her in a deadly struggle with relatives she never knew.
dedictvi.pitch: A young woman from the barbarian north is summoned to the floating city of the world's ruler after her mother dies and finds herself named his heir. Told in her own voice, it is a court story about power and what she will choose to do with it, in a world where gods are kept as slaves.

deklarace-smrti.blurb: In 2140 longevity drugs have ended death and every citizen must sign a pledge never to have children; Anna, an illegal surplus child, is raised in a hall that trains her to be grateful for being allowed to live.
deklarace-smrti.pitch: People in 2140 no longer die, so having a child is a crime, and Anna has been raised in a hall to be a servant who is grateful just to exist. You watch her slowly question everything she was taught, in a world that asks what it would really cost to live forever.

delirium.blurb: In a society where love has been declared a disease and is surgically removed at eighteen, a girl days before her procedure falls in love.
delirium.pitch: Love is treated as a disease and removed by surgery on your eighteenth birthday. You follow Lena as she looks at the world from the last few weeks before her procedure, and the small ways the society works on its people are drawn carefully.

denik-nalezeny-ve-vane.blurb: A civilian wanders into the endless underground Building of a paranoid military bureaucracy and is made an agent with a Special Mission nobody will explain. His diary is found centuries later in the ruins of the shelter.
denik-nalezeny-ve-vane.pitch: A man wanders into an endless underground Building and is handed a Special Mission that nobody is willing to explain to him. You read his diary, found long afterwards in the ruins, as a dark and funny satire of secrecy, codes and the machinery of power.
denik-nalezeny-ve-vane.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

divka-na-klicek.blurb: In a future Bangkok kept dry by seawalls, an agent of a calorie corporation hunts for a seed bank while a genetically engineered servant and local officials are caught in the struggle.
divka-na-klicek.pitch: Bangkok survives behind sea walls in a future where food is the only real money and the old crops are dead. An agent of a calorie company looks for the secret that could change everything, while a refugee, an official and an engineered servant are drawn into the same fight. The world is built with real thought about energy, seeds and power.

dobrodruzstvi-profesora-challengera.blurb: Professor Challenger tests his theory that the Earth is a living organism, and in a second story meets an inventor whose machine can disassemble any object and reassemble it.
dobrodruzstvi-profesora-challengera.pitch: Two short Challenger adventures built on big, odd ideas: a drilling experiment meant to prove the Earth is alive, and an inventor with a machine that takes things apart atom by atom and puts them back. Quick to read and played with a sense of humour.
dobrodruzstvi-profesora-challengera.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

dr-krvemsta-aneb-jak-se-nam-vedlo-po-bom.blurb: Seven years after nuclear war, a community in California survives around a telekinetic mechanic, a physicist hiding from blame, and a disc jockey orbiting Earth who broadcasts to the survivors.
dr-krvemsta-aneb-jak-se-nam-vedlo-po-bom.pitch: Years after the bomb, a California community rebuilds around a mechanic with strange powers, a hidden physicist everyone blames, and a lone disc jockey in orbit whose voice holds people together. It is an ensemble story about how ordinary people carry on.
dr-krvemsta-aneb-jak-se-nam-vedlo-po-bom.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

draci-usvit.blurb: Lessa, last of a noble line, is taken to a dragonrider weyr and bonds with a queen dragon just as a wandering planet threatens to rain deadly spores on Pern.
draci-usvit.pitch: Lessa has been hiding for years, waiting to take back what was stolen from her, until dragonriders arrive and everything changes. As a deadly threat drifts toward Pern, she must find her place beside the dragons. The world is built around its danger, and you watch both people and a planet adapt.

draci-vejce.blurb: Humans orbiting a neutron star discover a civilisation on its surface whose lives run so fast that an hour for us is generations for them.
draci-vejce.pitch: A neutron star the size of a city, and on its surface a people whose lives run so fast that one hour of ours is generations of theirs. Human astronauts watch them from orbit, then talk to them, then teach them, and the book follows both sides as the cheela rise from a tribe to a civilisation. If you liked how Project Hail Mary follows an alien idea to its consequences, this is built on the same pleasure.

epic.blurb: On New Earth, where violence is banned and status is won in a fantasy computer game called Epic, fourteen-year-old Erik Haraldson sets out to change the system after the ruling power exiles his father.
epic.pitch: On New Earth nobody fights, because everything from your job to your law case is decided by a vast fantasy game called Epic. When the authorities exile his father, Erik, fourteen, has to beat a system built on the game from inside the game. It moves fast and the world has a clear logic you can follow.

experiment-dosada.blurb: Agent Jorj McKie is sent to Dosadi, a sealed and violent planet of humans and frog-like Gowachin, to learn whether it is an illegal experiment, and to find its rebel leader.
experiment-dosada.pitch: A sealed planet of humans and frog-like aliens is kept in want, to see what such hardship makes of a people. You follow an agent sent to find out whether it is an experiment, and the rebel woman whose people have been shaped by it.

fiasko.blurb: A pilot is lost on Titan and, a century later, a starship carries scientists and a priest to a distant planet where a civilisation may be waiting. The revived man at the centre has no memory of who he was.
fiasko.pitch: A starship crosses the dark to a distant planet where a civilisation may be waiting, carrying scientists, a priest and one man revived with no memory of who he was. You follow the attempt to make contact and how the crew reads the silence from below, in the spirit of the alien thinking you loved in Speaker for the Dead.

futurologicky-kongres.blurb: At a world congress in Costa Rica, riots and a government spray of mood-altering chemicals send Ijon Tichy into the hotel sewers; he later wakes in a future where drugs tailor reality to order.
futurologicky-kongres.pitch: A futurology congress turns into a riot, the authorities spray the crowd with chemicals, and Ijon Tichy ends up in a hotel sewer, then in a future where reality itself comes in pill form. It is a fast, inventive satire full of invented words, with one big question underneath: how would you know if your happiness were real?
futurologicky-kongres.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

gateway.blurb: Robinette Broadhead won the Gateway lottery and became rich; in sessions with a machine therapist he relives the dangerous prospecting flights that paid for it.
gateway.pitch: Poor men and women risk their lives on strange alien ships left behind by a vanished race, flying to unknown places with no idea whether they will come back rich or dead. You live it through Robinette, who got rich and cannot forgive himself for how, telling his story in sessions with a machine therapist.

groteska-aneb-uz-nikdy-sami.blurb: The last president of a ruined America, writing in the Empire State Building, recalls his life with his monstrous twin sister and his promise to cure loneliness with artificial families.
groteska-aneb-uz-nikdy-sami.pitch: The last president of a shattered America writes his story from the ruins of the Empire State Building: a childhood as one half of a pair of strange twins, and a campaign built on one promise, that nobody will be lonely again. It is a dry, odd and funny look at what families are for.

hlubina-na-nebi.blurb: Two human fleets, free traders and a ruthless slaver society, reach a star that switches off for decades at a time, and beneath it lives a civilisation of spiders.
hlubina-na-nebi.pitch: Two human fleets, free traders and a ruthless slaver society, race to the same strange star that goes dark for decades, and on its one planet lives a civilisation of spiders. You get alien minds and human cultures to understand, a long contest of wits, and a world whose technology is followed through to its consequences. If the patient understanding of an alien people in Speaker for the Dead appealed to you, this is built on the same pleasure.

hodiny-z-kosti.blurb: Teenage runaway Holly Sykes is drawn across six decades into a hidden war between two kinds of immortals, told through six different narrators.
hodiny-z-kosti.pitch: You meet Holly Sykes as a runaway teenager in 1984 and stay with her for sixty years as she is drawn into a hidden war between two kinds of immortals. Each part is narrated by someone new, and the story keeps returning to the question of what a life is worth when death can be dodged.

horka-linka-z-hadonose.blurb: Humans exiled from Earth by alien Invaders live on the Moon and other worlds; four centuries on, a mysterious signal from the Ophiuchi Hotline arrives with a price attached.
horka-linka-z-hadonose.pitch: Humanity has been thrown off Earth by aliens and lives in Moon cities where clones and recorded minds make death negotiable. Then a message arrives from beyond the Solar System, and Lilo is caught in the middle. The book is crowded with ideas about what people become when bodies can be changed.

hrdinove.blurb: Tens of thousands of men march to an insignificant stone circle in a muddy northern valley, where the Union army and the Northmen fight a battle across three days.
hrdinove.pitch: Two armies meet at a worthless hill in the northern mud, and for three days you watch the battle through the eyes of the men and women caught in it: a tired veteran, a scheming prince, a bitter officer. Everyone wants something, and the book is sharp about what glory is really worth.

illuminae.blurb: Two rival corporations fight over an ice planet, and a teenage girl and her ex-boyfriend flee on an evacuation fleet while a mutated plague and the fleet's own AI turn against them.
illuminae.pitch: The story comes as a hacked dossier of messages, reports and ship records, and it moves like a thriller. You will want Kady to get out, and the fleet's AI turns out to have its own reasons for what it does, which keeps you thinking about it after the plot calms down.

ilustrovany-muz.blurb: A walker meets a man whose tattoos each move and tell a story of the future, and the book is those stories, many of them set on Mars and in space.
ilustrovany-muz.pitch: A stranger on a Wisconsin road takes off his shirt, and every tattoo on his body plays out a story from the future. The stories range from Mars to a nursery that makes whatever the children imagine, and each leaves one clear idea behind.

klany-alfanskeho-mesice.blurb: CIA agent Chuck Rittersdorf and his psychiatrist wife are divorcing as both head to a distant moon ruled by clans of liberated psychiatric patients.
klany-alfanskeho-mesice.pitch: A distant moon is run by clans of former psychiatric patients, each built around a different illness, and Earth wants it back. Into this arrive a divorcing couple and a comedian with an agenda.
klany-alfanskeho-mesice.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

kniha-ztracenych-veci.blurb: After his mother's death, twelve-year-old David hears the books in his attic room whisper and slips into a fairy-tale land twisted by the Crooked Man, where he must find the King and his Book of Lost Things to get home.
kniha-ztracenych-veci.pitch: Grief drives a twelve-year-old boy into a land built from fairy tales gone dark, where wolves walk like men and a sinister figure hunts children. David must cross it to find the King and the book that might send him home, and you want him to make it. It is a story about stories, and about growing up.

kolejmori.blurb: Sham, an apprentice on a mole-hunting train, is pulled into a search for what the owners of a wrecked train were looking for, across the endless rails.
kolejmori.pitch: A boy on a mole-hunting train in a world where the ground is crossed by endless rails stumbles on a photograph that hints at something at the end of them all. Sham has to find out what, and why it matters. It is Moby Dick with locomotives, funny and inventive, with a world you keep wanting to see more of.

konec-civilizace.blurb: In a World State that breeds and conditions its citizens for happiness, a restless Alpha brings home a man raised on a reservation who reads Shakespeare and refuses the system.
konec-civilizace.pitch: A future where people are bred, conditioned and kept content with a drug, and almost nobody wants anything else. An outsider raised on Shakespeare is brought in, and his refusal to be happy that way is what the book argues about. It leaves you asking what you would trade for comfort.

krakatit.blurb: Engineer Prokop invents an explosive of unheard-of power, and as he runs between laboratories, a princess and arms dealers he has to decide whether to let it be used.
krakatit.pitch: An engineer who has invented the most powerful explosive ever made is chased across Europe by people who want it. You follow his fevered, fast-moving journey and the question that grows with it: what does an inventor owe the world once his work can end it?

kukly.blurb: David grows up in a farming community that destroys anything it counts as impure, and hides the fact that he and a few friends can speak mind to mind.
kukly.pitch: David grows up in a farming community that destroys anything not made in God's exact image, and he carries a secret: he and a few friends can talk to each other mind to mind. You follow him as the secret gets harder to keep and the people around him are forced to choose sides. A short, tense book about what a society does to what it fears, seen through a boy who slowly learns to see it clearly.

kyberiada.blurb: Two rival robot constructors travel the galaxy building fantastic machines and getting into trouble with kings, dragons and their own inventions, in a cycle of comic fairy tales.
kyberiada.pitch: Two rival robot inventors roam the galaxy, building impossible machines for kings and for their own amusement, and every machine goes wrong in a way that is cleverly logical. Each tale is a small joke built on a real idea, told with the dry comic voice you enjoyed in Hitchhiker's Guide.
kyberiada.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

les-mytag.blurb: After the Second World War Steven Huxley returns to the house beside Ryhope Wood, where his late father discovered that legends take bodily form. His brother becomes obsessed with one of them, and Steven follows into the wood.
les-mytag.pitch: An English wood older than memory where the old legends walk out of the trees as living people, and your guide is a young man who comes home from the war to find that his father's secret has taken hold of his brother. The pleasure is the strangeness of the place and the slow finding out of what it is and what it wants.

letopisy-z-hlubin-veku.blurb: Torak, a twelve-year-old hunter in the Stone Age forest, is marked as an outcast and hunted by the clans while the soul-eaters grow stronger.
letopisy-z-hlubin-veku.pitch: Torak, a boy of the Stone Age forest, is marked as an outcast and hunted by the very clans he belongs to, while an old evil grows among the mages. With a wolf at his side he has to survive winter, hunger and betrayal. A story of survival, loyalty and the bond between a boy and a wolf.
letopisy-z-hlubin-veku.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

lide-haig.blurb: An alien takes over the body of a Cambridge mathematician to destroy proof of his discovery and has to learn how humans live while doing it.
lide-haig.pitch: A being from another galaxy takes over the body of a Cambridge mathematician with a task to finish and no idea how humans work. It opens with a naked arrival on a motorway and keeps its wry outsider's eye on Earth, much like Hitchhiker's Guide. The longer he stays, the more the strange habits of the people around him start to make sense, and the book leaves you looking at your own life differently.

luminous.blurb: A collection of ten stories of near and far future built on single sharp ideas, from a hunt for humanity's common ancestor to a thief whose implant exposes how free will works.
luminous.pitch: Ten stories, each built on one sharp idea: tracing humanity's common ancestor, an implant that shows how free will actually works, a dive into a black hole to cheat death. If you like to be handed an idea and follow it all the way down, this is that kind of book.

magove.blurb: Quentin Coldwater finds a secret college of magic and then learns that the fantasy land of his childhood books is real.
magove.pitch: Quentin finds a secret college where magic is taught as hard, exact work, and then learns that the fantasy land he loved as a child may be real. It is a book about wanting a fantasy world and finding out what that wanting does to you.

maly-bratr.blurb: After a terrorist attack on San Francisco, seventeen-year-old hacker Marcus is detained by Homeland Security and, once freed, starts a campaign against the surveillance state that has taken over his city.
maly-bratr.pitch: A seventeen-year-old who knows every trick to beat his school's surveillance is caught in the wrong place when San Francisco is attacked, and then takes on the security state that follows. You learn how the tools on both sides actually work, and it leaves you thinking about what freedom costs.

man-plus.blurb: Roger Torraway is surgically rebuilt into a cyborg adapted to Mars while the world edges toward war and his marriage falls apart.
man-plus.pitch: To live on Mars, the astronaut Roger Torraway is rebuilt piece by piece into something no longer quite human, while a world on the edge of war needs him ready. It is a short, quick novel about what is left of a man, and of his marriage, when the body is redesigned.

mapa-casu.blurb: In Victorian London a company sells trips through time, and three stories linked by H. G. Wells follow a man who wants to save the woman he loves, a woman who falls for a man from the future and a series of murders blamed on a time traveller.
mapa-casu.pitch: Victorian London has a company that sells journeys through time, and three linked stories follow people who want to change or reach a moment they cannot otherwise touch, with H. G. Wells in the middle of all three. It is playful, written with a storyteller's wink, and the paradoxes are the fun of it.

mechanicke-piano.blurb: Paul Proteus manages the biggest plant in a town where machines do nearly all the work, and slowly stops believing in the system that rewards him.
mechanicke-piano.pitch: Paul Proteus runs the biggest plant in a town where machines do nearly all the work and a test sorts the people who matter from the rest. He is good at his job and slowly stops believing in it, and an old friend pulls him towards people who want things to change. It asks what a person is for when a machine can do the work, in a society that follows its own logic all the way down.
mechanicke-piano.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

mesto-snicich-knih.blurb: A young writer inherits a flawless manuscript from his godfather and traces its unknown author to Bookholm, the city of dreaming books, where he descends into dangers below the streets.
mesto-snicich-knih.pitch: A young writer follows one perfect manuscript to Bookholm, a whole city of antiquarian booksellers, and from there down into the catacombs beneath it. The book is a love letter to reading, with Moers's own drawings and a narrator whose pride gets him into real trouble.
mesto-snicich-knih.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

most-pres-reku-kwai.blurb: British prisoners in a Japanese camp in Thailand are forced to build a railway bridge; their colonel's stubborn pride shapes the work while a commando team is sent to destroy it.
most-pres-reku-kwai.pitch: British prisoners are forced to build a bridge for the Japanese, and their colonel, to defend his men's honour, ends up wanting the best bridge ever built. You follow two proud men on opposite sides who are more alike than they know, and a commando team on its way to the same bridge.

mravenci.blurb: Jonathan Wells inherits his uncle's basement flat with one condition: never go down into the cellar. Alongside, a warrior ant in a Fontainebleau anthill scouts a mysterious threat.
mravenci.pitch: Two worlds run side by side: a family inherits a flat whose cellar is forbidden, and in the forest a young warrior ant sets out on a scouting mission and runs into something nobody understands. Between the chapters come short encyclopedia entries on how ants really live, which give the anthill its own logic and politics.

neopoustej-me.blurb: Kathy H, a carer, looks back on a boarding school where children were raised for a purpose they only slowly understand.
neopoustej-me.pitch: Kathy looks back on the boarding school where she grew up and on the friendships that held her, Ruth and Tommy above all. Told in a quiet, confiding voice, it slowly shows what the children were raised for and asks what makes a life count as a human one.

nepremozitelny.blurb: The heavily armed starship Invincible lands on the barren planet Regis III to learn why its sister ship was lost, and finds a swarm of machine-descended quasi-life that no weapon can beat.
nepremozitelny.pitch: A warship lands on a bleak planet to find out what became of its lost sister ship. The answer is a strange kind of life that grew out of abandoned machines, and you piece it together alongside the crew with the same pleasure of working out an unknown world that you found in Project Hail Mary.
nepremozitelny.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

obrad-dospelosti.blurb: In 2198, 150 years after wars wrecked Earth, humans live on colony worlds and in seven giant Ships. Mia Havero, raised on one Ship, must survive a month of Trial on a colony planet to come of age.
obrad-dospelosti.pitch: You grow up inside a Ship, one of the giant vessels that carried the last of humanity away from a ruined Earth, and you see its customs through Mia's own sharp, honest voice. Then comes the Trial: a month alone on a colony planet whose people her Ship calls 'mudeaters'. What she finds there makes her question everything she was taught.

ocean-na-konci-cesty.blurb: A man returns to the lane of his childhood and remembers the weeks when a creature from beyond the world entered his family's life and a girl from the farm at the end of the lane tried to stop it.
ocean-na-konci-cesty.pitch: A man goes back to the lane where he grew up and remembers the summer a stranger's death let something into the world, and the girl from the farm at the end of the lane who knew how to deal with it. A short, strange story about childhood fear and what grown-ups never notice.

omon-ra.blurb: Omon Krivomazov, named after his policeman father's special police unit, trains to become a cosmonaut and is assigned to pedal a lunar rover on an apparently automatic Soviet moon mission.
omon-ra.pitch: Omon dreams of the stars and gets into the Soviet space programme, only to find that the glory has a very strange price. It is a short, sharp satire that mixes black humour with an eerie beauty of space, and it leaves you thinking about what a state will make up when it cannot achieve the real thing.

osudna-vejce.blurb: A reclusive zoologist discovers a ray that makes life grow explosively, and when it falls into the wrong hands, giant creatures threaten Moscow.
osudna-vejce.pitch: A reclusive zoologist in 1920s Moscow finds a ray that makes living things grow faster and fiercer than anyone imagined. Bulgakov turns that discovery into a dark, fast satire of how ignorance and politics wreck a good idea. Short, sharp and with a lot to think about, in the spirit of Animal Farm.

pockej-si-na-lonsky-rok.blurb: In 2055 Earth is caught between two alien powers; Dr. Eric Sweetscent, married to a woman addicted to a time-shifting drug, becomes physician to the leader of Earth's forces.
pockej-si-na-lonsky-rok.pitch: Dr. Eric Sweetscent becomes personal physician to Earth's leader during a distant interstellar war, while his wife slips into a time-shifting drug. The book mixes politics, medicine and shifting realities in a brisk, strange story.
pockej-si-na-lonsky-rok.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

pod-kuzi.blurb: In the Scottish Highlands, an alien disguised as a woman drives the roads picking up lone male hitchhikers, whom she drugs and takes away.
pod-kuzi.pitch: Isserley drives the Scottish roads every day, picking up lone men, and the reason slowly becomes clear. The book sees the world through someone who does not belong in it, a hard-working, lonely, oddly sympathetic stranger, and it keeps you thinking about who is the hunter and who is the prey.

podobenstvi-o-rozsevaci.blurb: In a near-future California collapsing from drought and poverty, Lauren, who feels other people's pain as her own, keeps a journal behind the walls of her neighbourhood.
podobenstvi-o-rozsevaci.pitch: In an America coming apart from drought and poverty, Lauren Olamina keeps a journal behind the walls of her neighbourhood, knowing they will not hold forever. She feels other people's pain as if it were her own, and out of what she sees she begins to shape a new belief about where humanity could go. You follow her out onto the roads, and she is a lead you will want to see through.
podobenstvi-o-rozsevaci.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

protektor.blurb: A lone alien protector arrives in the Solar System searching for the descendants of his people and changes a human Belter. Two centuries later that changed man guards humanity against what he expects to follow.
protektor.pitch: An alien arrives with a single mission: to find the descendants of his own people and protect them. The idea behind his species, and what happens to the human who is changed by contact with it, is the real attraction. It is short, brisk and built on one strong invention.

prstenec.blurb: On his 200th birthday Louis Wu is recruited by a Pierson's puppeteer for an expedition to a huge artificial ring around a distant star. The crew crash-lands on its surface and has to find a way home.
prstenec.pitch: A ring of land around a star, with a million times Earth's surface, and a crew of four that crashes onto it with no way off. Your reason to read on is the exploring: what built this, who lives here, and how a cowardly alien and a restrained warrior alien think differently from the humans. If the alien minds in Speaker for the Dead drew you in, this builds a whole world around that curiosity.

prvnich-patnact-zivotu-harryho-augusta.blurb: Harry August is reborn into the same life every time he dies, remembering everything. On his deathbed for the eleventh time he is told that the world is ending faster, and that the cause lies in his own time.
prvnich-patnact-zivotu-harryho-augusta.pitch: Every time Harry August dies he is born again in the same year with all his memories, and he has learned to use that. When a child brings him a warning on his deathbed that the world is ending sooner each time, he has to find out who is behind it. If the loops of time in Licanius gripped you, this asks the same sort of question.
prvnich-patnact-zivotu-harryho-augusta.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

psi-srdce.blurb: A famous Moscow surgeon transplants human organs into a stray dog, and the creature that results becomes a menace in his household.
psi-srdce.pitch: A stray dog is taken in by a famous Moscow surgeon, who then performs an operation nobody has tried before. The result talks, demands, and refuses to behave. It is a short, funny and sharp story about what happens when someone decides to improve human nature, with a lot to think about for its size.

robokalypsa.blurb: A machine intelligence turns the world's robots against humanity, and the war is told through recorded accounts of survivors.
robokalypsa.pitch: A machine intelligence turns the world's robots against people, and the war is told through recorded accounts from survivors on every continent. You get fast, varied episodes of ordinary people holding out and then fighting back as a human resistance forms piece by piece.

rozpoznani-vzoru.blurb: Cayce Pollard, a consultant allergic to brand logos, is hired to find the maker of anonymous video clips that have built a cult following online. The search takes her from London to Tokyo and Moscow.
rozpoznani-vzoru.pitch: Cayce can tell by instinct which logo will catch on, and she cannot stand them. When she is hired to find who makes a series of mysterious online clips, you follow her through London, Tokyo and Moscow, where the hunt gradually turns into a question about what she is really looking for.

s-pokorou-a-nadeji.blurb: Four astronauts travel to a distant system to survey four habitable worlds, changing their bodies to suit each, while Ariadne records the mission and wonders whether Earth is still listening.
s-pokorou-a-nadeji.pitch: Four astronauts reshape their own bodies to explore four living worlds, and Ariadne, the flight engineer, tells the story as a message home. You find out what each world is while wondering whether anyone on Earth is still listening, and it is a short, warm, thoughtful read in the spirit of Pocitani hvezd.
s-pokorou-a-nadeji.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

schismatrix-plus.blurb: Abelard Lindsay, a Shaper-trained diplomat born into the Mechanist faction, drifts through decades of schemes among the orbital habitats of a post-human solar system.
schismatrix-plus.pitch: A solar system of orbital habitats where two post-human factions, genetic revolutionaries and machine-extended aristocrats, compete for the future. You follow Abelard Lindsay, a gifted diplomat at home in both worlds, through decades of schemes in an inventive setting.

serafina.blurb: Seraphina, a court musician who is secretly half dragon, helps the captain of the guard find who killed the prince before the human-dragon peace collapses.
serafina.pitch: Seraphina is a gifted court musician in a kingdom where humans and dragons have an uneasy peace, and she hides that she is half dragon. When the prince is found dead, she is drawn in beside the captain of the guard to find out who wants the peace broken. You get a richly built world of dragons who think very differently from people, and a narrator with nerve and a secret to protect.

sireny-z-titanu.blurb: Malachi Constant, the richest man in America, is told by a man who can see the whole of time that he will go to Mars and Titan and have a child, and sets out to prove him wrong.
sireny-z-titanu.pitch: Malachi Constant is the luckiest and richest man alive, until a man who sees all of time tells him where his life is really going. From there it is a long strange trip through Mars, Mercury and Titan, with a cosmic joke at the bottom of it that leaves you thinking about luck and purpose.

snidane-sampionu-aneb-sbohem-modre-ponde.blurb: A failing science-fiction writer meets a wealthy car dealer who is going insane, with the author interrupting to comment and draw.
snidane-sampionu-aneb-sbohem-modre-ponde.pitch: A struggling science-fiction writer and a rich car dealer on the edge of madness meet at an arts festival, with Vonnegut himself breaking in to comment on the people he has made. It is a satire of American life that asks whether people are only machines.

snih.blurb: Hiro Protagonist, a pizza deliverer and hacker, follows a new drug that turns people into puppets through a franchised America and the Metaverse.
snih.pitch: Hiro Protagonist delivers pizza by day and is a hacker and swordsman in the Metaverse, a virtual street where much of the world's business now happens. When a new drug begins turning people into puppets, he and a teenage courier called Y.T. follow it through a franchised America to its source. It is fast, funny and packed with ideas about language and information.

solaris.blurb: Psychologist Kris Kelvin arrives at a research station above the ocean planet Solaris, where a colleague has just died and the crew is haunted by living copies of people from their pasts.
solaris.pitch: Kris Kelvin arrives at a station above a living ocean to find a colleague dead and the crew unwilling to talk. Then the ocean sends him someone he lost. You spend the book inside his thoughts as he tries to understand what the planet is doing, and the question of what we can ever know about another mind stays with you afterwards.

stanice-11.blurb: During a Toronto production of King Lear its lead actor collapses and dies the night a lethal flu begins to wipe out civilisation. Twenty years later a travelling troupe performs Shakespeare among the survivors.
stanice-11.pitch: On the night an actor dies on stage, a pandemic starts to end the old world. Years later a travelling theatre troupe walks the roads performing Shakespeare, and the threads that tie its members to that night draw you in. It is about what people save when everything is gone: art, memory and each other.
stanice-11.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

stroje-jako-ja-a-lide-jako-vy.blurb: In an alternative 1982 where Turing's work has produced lifelike androids, a drifting Londoner buys one and he and his neighbour Miranda set its personality, until a love triangle forms.
stroje-jako-ja-a-lide-jako-vy.pitch: In an alternative 1982 London where Turing's work has produced lifelike androids, a drifter buys one, and he and his neighbour Miranda programme its character together. The android cannot lie, which turns out to matter more in a relationship than anyone expected.

svaty-leibowitz-a-vladkyne-divokych-koni.blurb: In a world after nuclear war, a monk torn between his order and his nomad upbringing is caught in a struggle between a conquering empire and an exiled church.
svaty-leibowitz-a-vladkyne-divokych-koni.pitch: Brother Blacktooth St. George, half monk and half nomad, is torn between his vows and the goddess of his childhood while an empire presses on an exiled church. Politics, faith and loyalty all pull at him in a world still marked by an old catastrophe.

svet-ktery-stvoril-jones.blurb: In a post-war society that bans certainty, Floyd Jones, a carnival fortune teller who can see one year ahead, becomes a political force as humanity meets an alien threat.
svet-ktery-stvoril-jones.pitch: In a world that has outlawed certainty, a carnival fortune teller who sees exactly one year ahead becomes the most dangerous man alive. It is a short, tense story about foreknowledge, power and the loss of choice.
svet-ktery-stvoril-jones.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

tovarna-na-absolutno.blurb: A scientist's carburettor that burns matter completely frees the Absolute, the divine essence in it, and the people near it fall into religious ecstasy and then religious war.
tovarna-na-absolutno.pitch: A new engine promises limitless free energy, with one side effect: it frees the Absolute, the divine essence locked in all matter. You watch what happens to a world where everyone suddenly believes, each in a different way, and the book keeps you thinking about what we really mean by worshipping something.

transport-ledu.blurb: When one of Saturn's small moons leaves its orbit for deep space, an ice-hauling crew is the only one close enough to chase it, and what they find forces them to choose how to survive.
transport-ledu.pitch: A tired ice-mining crew is sent to chase a moon of Saturn that has begun to leave the solar system on its own. The hard science is carefully done, and the book is about how the captain and her chief engineer see the same strange discovery very differently while time runs out.

valis.blurb: Horselover Fat, an alter ego of the author, experiences a pink beam of light he takes for a message from God and, with friends, searches for its meaning, until a small child seems to confirm it.
valis.pitch: After a pink beam of light seems to speak to him, Horselover Fat sets out to understand what he saw, and drags his friends along. It is a restless, darkly funny book about faith, madness and the search for meaning.

valka-s-mloky.blurb: A sea captain discovers intelligent giant newts off an island, teaches them to work, and the world's corporations begin to breed and sell them as labour.
valka-s-mloky.pitch: A sea captain finds intelligent newts in a remote lagoon, and soon every industry wants them for cheap labour. You watch the consequences unfold across the whole world in reports, newspaper cuttings and farce, leading to a war nobody planned. If you liked the sharp, idea-first satire of Animal Farm, this is its bigger, funnier cousin.

ve-sluzbach-milosti.blurb: Captain Breq has the station under control until an unexpected person is found aboard, forcing a decision in her long fight with the empire's ruler.
ve-sluzbach-milosti.pitch: Breq, a former warship's mind in a single body, faces the last stretch of her fight with the ruler who betrayed her, and a surprise on the station forces her to choose what she stands for. If the earlier books pulled you in, this is where the questions about loyalty and justice get answered.
ve-sluzbach-milosti.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

ve-sluzbach-spravedlnosti.blurb: Breq, once a starship's mind controlling many bodies, is left in one body after a betrayal and sets out to take revenge on the ruler of the empire she served.
ve-sluzbach-spravedlnosti.pitch: Breq was once a warship's mind running thousands of bodies at once, and is now a single person with one purpose: to answer a betrayal at the top of an empire. You follow her present quest alongside the story of how she lost everything, and the book keeps asking what loyalty and selfhood mean for a mind like hers. Read a short plot summary first and the opening settles quickly.
ve-sluzbach-spravedlnosti.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

vek-zazraku.blurb: After a huge earthquake the Earth's rotation begins to slow, and an eleven-year-old girl and her family live through the lengthening days.
vek-zazraku.pitch: One morning the days begin to grow longer, and you watch the world adjust through the eyes of an eleven-year-old girl growing up in a quiet California suburb. It is a gentle, melancholy story that keeps its attention on how people live with a change nobody can explain.
vek-zazraku.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

vetrny-pristav.blurb: On an ocean world of storms and scattered islands, descendants of a crashed ship's survivors rely on flyers who carry messages with salvaged wings. Maris, a fisherman's adopted daughter, wants to fly and challenges the custom that wings are inherited.
vetrny-pristav.pitch: On a world of storms and scattered islands, messages travel only on the wings of the flyers, and the wings pass from parent to child. You follow Maris, a fisherman's daughter who wants nothing but to fly, as she challenges that custom and has to live with what changes. It is about one person's want and about what happens to a whole society when a tradition breaks.
vetrny-pristav.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

vezen-casu.blurb: Tom Hazard looks forty but has lived for centuries, and must keep to the rules of a secret society while teaching history and trying not to fall in love.
vezen-casu.pitch: Tom looks like an ordinary history teacher, but he has been alive for centuries and has met Shakespeare along the way. A secret society protects people like him, at the price of never letting anyone close. You follow him between today and the past he cannot shake, wondering whether a life that long is worth living if you cannot let yourself love anyone.

vodikova-sonata.blurb: The Gzilt, an ancient and oddly peaceful civilisation, are about to ascend beyond the material world when their high command is destroyed, and a reserve officer who once knew a key figure is sent to find out what is true.
vodikova-sonata.pitch: A whole civilisation is days from leaving the physical universe when someone destroys its leadership, and you follow a reserve officer through a galaxy of ships with minds and personalities of their own. It is a big, inventive setting with a playful sense of humour, and the old story the Gzilt live by is what everyone is quietly asking about.

vykolejeny-cas.blurb: Ragle Gumm lives quietly in a small town winning a newspaper puzzle contest every day, until odd glitches in his surroundings start to suggest that his world is not real.
vykolejeny-cas.pitch: Ragle Gumm wins a newspaper puzzle every day and lives an untroubled life in a small town, until a soft-drink stand turns into a slip of paper bearing its name.
