You follow him as small cracks widen and he has to find out what his world is really made of, with the same pleasure of uncovering an unknown that you got from Project Hail Mary.
vykolejeny-cas.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

vyprava-na-zemi.blurb: Eleven early science-fiction stories by Arthur C. Clarke, from first contact to discoveries on the Moon.
vyprava-na-zemi.pitch: Eleven short stories from the early career of a master of big ideas, among them the Moon discovery that later grew into a famous film. Each one is built around a single, clear what-if about humanity and what might be out there.

vyslanci-do-prazdna.blurb: A starship crew of expendable clones, losing their ship's brain, must create an artificial consciousness to reach a distant star, under a psychologist who knows the true purpose of the voyage.
vyslanci-do-prazdna.pitch: A starship crew has lost its guiding brain and the only way to reach a new world is to build a mind that can think. You follow them as they argue about what consciousness is and what they are willing to do to make one.

vzpominka-zvana-rise.blurb: Mahit Dzmare arrives as ambassador from a small mining station to the capital of the vast Teixcalaanli Empire to find that her predecessor is dead. She must work out who is responsible while protecting her home.
vzpominka-zvana-rise.pitch: You arrive with the ambassador, Mahit, in an empire that thinks everyone else is barbarian, carrying in your head the remembered voice of the man she replaces. It is a book about what it costs to belong to a huge culture and what it costs to resist it, with a court full of clever people who all want something different.
vzpominka-zvana-rise.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

zaplat-nebo-zemri.blurb: In a near future where artificial organs can be repossessed for missed payments, a top repo man falls behind on his own heart and goes on the run from his former partner.
zaplat-nebo-zemri.pitch: A repo man whose job is taking back artificial organs from people who can't pay is himself unable to keep up with the bill for his new heart. It is a dark, darkly funny story with a narrator who does not look away from his own work.

zhrouceny-cas.blurb: A deadly epidemic erases people's memories and replaces them with false lives, and a New York cop and a neuroscientist are drawn into what is causing it.
zhrouceny-cas.pitch: People start waking up with the memories of a whole life they never lived, and you follow a cop and a scientist who realise the cause reaches into time itself. It moves fast, and each turn of the memory idea changes what the characters stand to lose, much like the time loops you liked in Licanius.

zlomeni-andele.blurb: Thirty years after his first case, ex-Envoy Takeshi Kovacs fights as a mercenary on Sanction IV, then is offered a chance to recover the most valuable alien artefact ever found.
zlomeni-andele.pitch: Takeshi Kovacs, a former elite soldier, fights as a mercenary on a world torn apart by war until he is offered the biggest prize in human history: an alien artefact that could change everything. The setting, where minds are moved between bodies, is a strong backdrop for a hard-edged adventure.

lide-sawyer.blurb: Months after the portal to a Neanderthal world opens, Ponter returns to our Earth with a delegation of scientists, while Mary is drawn into a think tank studying them and the bond between her and Ponter deepens.
lide-sawyer.pitch: Ponter, a Neanderthal physicist from a parallel Earth, comes back through the portal with a delegation of his world's best minds, and our world has to decide how to meet them. You follow his bond with Mary, a geneticist, and how two very different societies see justice, belief and each other.

ostrov-ztracenych-vzpominek.blurb: On an island where objects vanish from existence and memory, a young novelist hides her editor from the secret police who hunt people who still remember.
ostrov-ztracenych-vzpominek.pitch: On a small island, things keep disappearing, first ribbons and perfumes, then birds and roses, and with each one it vanishes from everyone's memory. A young novelist hides her editor from the secret police who hunt the few people who still remember. It is a quiet, haunting story about what we hold on to and what is left of a person when memories are taken away.
ostrov-ztracenych-vzpominek.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

potopena-mesta.blurb: In a war-ravaged, flooded future, a one-handed girl and a boy soldier try to survive, and she shelters a wounded, genetically engineered war beast.
potopena-mesta.pitch: In a flooded future torn apart by endless war, Mahlia, a girl with one hand, fights to stay alive among soldiers who see her as an enemy. She shelters a wounded, genetically engineered war beast who turns out to be the most human of all of them. It is a fast, hard-edged survival story with a lead you will want to see make it through.

pustina-zvana-mir.blurb: A Teixcalaanli fleet at the frontier is fighting alien ships. A negotiator asks her friend, a former ambassador, to help find a way to talk to the enemy.
pustina-zvana-mir.pitch: A war on the edge of a huge empire, against an enemy no one can talk to. You follow the people who try, through language and cultural misreading, and the question is how you speak to something that does not think the way you do.
pustina-zvana-mir.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

spici-obri.blurb: A girl falls into a pit in South Dakota and wakes in a chamber lit with strange symbols, resting in a giant metal hand, and seventeen years later the mystery of the artifact is still unsolved.
spici-obri.pitch: A child falls through the ground into a buried chamber and lands in the palm of a giant metal hand. Decades later, a small team is still trying to learn who made it. It is short and quick to read, and the unnamed interviewer holding it all together is a character in his own right.

za-modrym-horizontem-udalosti.blurb: Rich ex-prospector Robinette Broadhead funds an expedition to a newly found alien food factory, whose dream-couch starts disturbing minds on Earth.
za-modrym-horizontem-udalosti.pitch: A huge alien food factory has been found at the edge of the solar system, and the wealthy Robinette Broadhead sponsors the expedition to reach it. There is a strange couch inside that makes people dream of wonders, and as you read you learn what it is doing to the people who touch it.

zeleny-mozek.blurb: Brazilian ecologist Joao Martinho exterminates jungle insects for a world short of land, but a hidden hive intelligence begins fighting back.
zeleny-mozek.pitch: An overcrowded world sends men into the Amazon to wipe out the insects that block new farmland, and something in the jungle begins to answer. You follow the battle on both sides, including through the eyes of the insect mind itself.

2666.blurb: A sprawling novel in five parts that follows literary critics searching for a vanished writer and the unsolved murders of women in a Mexican border town.
2666.pitch: Four scholars of one reclusive German writer set out to find him, and the search pulls you toward a Mexican border town. It is a very large book that rewards a reader happy to follow many lives at once.

alias-grace.blurb: In 1859 Canada a young servant convicted of two murders tells her life to an American doctor who is trying to judge whether she is guilty, insane or both.
alias-grace.pitch: Grace Marks, a servant convicted of a notorious double murder, tells her story to a young doctor who has to decide what she really is. You are drawn into a calm, precise voice that never quite lets you know how much to believe.

amsterodam.blurb: At the funeral of Molly Lane, two of her former lovers, a composer and a newspaper editor, make a pact about the end of their lives, and both go on to make choices that test the pact.
amsterodam.pitch: A short, sharp Booker winner that starts at a funeral and follows two old friends, once rivals for the same woman, into a pact whose consequences neither expects. If you enjoy watching careers, friendships and principles collide, it is told with a cold wit.

baltasar-a-blimunda.blurb: In early eighteenth-century Portugal a one-handed ex-soldier and a woman who can see inside people join a priest-inventor building a flying machine, while a convent is raised by forced labour.
baltasar-a-blimunda.pitch: In eighteenth-century Portugal, a soldier who has lost a hand falls in with Blimunda, a woman with an uncanny gift, and a priest who dreams of flying. Behind them a royal convent is being built on the backs of thousands of workers. It is a love story told with irony and a big idea about who pays for monuments.

bezbarvy-cukuru-tazaki-a-jeho-leta-putov.blurb: Tsukuru Tazaki was abruptly cut off by his four closest friends at twenty; years later his girlfriend urges him to find each of them and ask why.
bezbarvy-cukuru-tazaki-a-jeho-leta-putov.pitch: At twenty, Tsukuru Tazaki was cut off without explanation by his four closest friends. Years later a new girlfriend urges him to find them one by one and finally ask why. A quiet journey through memory, friendship and what we never say to each other.

carodejka-z-florencie.blurb: A yellow-haired traveller arrives at Emperor Akbar's court claiming a link to the royal family and tells the story of a woman of legendary beauty, Qara Koz, who travelled from the Mughal world to Renaissance Florence.
carodejka-z-florencie.pitch: At Akbar's court a stranger claims to be the emperor's kin and tells a story that moves from the Mughal Empire to Renaissance Florence, where the woman at its centre is said to charm a whole city. It sets two great courts side by side and plays with the question of what a good story is worth.

cerni-psi.blurb: Jeremy, orphaned young, becomes close to his parents-in-law, who split over a single frightening encounter on a French road, and he tries to piece together what happened. The couple stand for opposite answers about good, evil and belief.
cerni-psi.pitch: A short novel about two people who cannot agree on what one frightening day in France meant, told by the son-in-law who tries to reconstruct it. If a quiet argument about reason and faith that never quite settles is what you want in a short book, this is a compact one.

cesta-do-hlubin-noci.blurb: A French soldier of the First World War drifts from the front through colonial Africa and an American factory town to a poor Paris suburb, where he works as a doctor.
cesta-do-hlubin-noci.pitch: A drafted soldier drifts from the trenches to a colonial trading post, a Detroit factory and a poor Paris suburb, telling it all in a savagely funny voice. The book asks what is left of a person after he has seen how people really treat each other.

clovek-bez-osudu.blurb: A teenage Budapest boy is deported to Auschwitz and then on to other camps, and tells it in a calm, matter-of-fact voice.
clovek-bez-osudu.pitch: A teenage boy from Budapest is taken off a bus and deported, first to Auschwitz and then on through other camps. He tells it in a calm, matter-of-fact voice, step by step, like someone trying to make sense of a new reality. It leaves you with hard questions about survival and fate.

cosi-divneho-v-me-hlave-aneb-zivot-dobro.blurb: Mevlut, a boza seller who came to Istanbul from Anatolia, lives through four decades of the city's change, from a love-letter elopement that goes wrong to his later years.
cosi-divneho-v-me-hlave-aneb-zivot-dobro.pitch: Mevlut sells boza in the streets of Istanbul, and over forty years you watch the city grow around him. The story is told by him and by the many relatives who each remember events their own way, so you see the same life from many sides.

dedictvi-spionu.blurb: Retired intelligence officer Peter Guillam is called back to London to answer for a Cold War operation whose consequences have reached the next generation.
dedictvi-spionu.pitch: Called back to London from his retirement, an old intelligence officer must answer for a Cold War operation, with the secret archive as his only witness. It is a look back at what a service did in the name of a cause, and who paid for it.

demian.blurb: Emil Sinclair grows up between a safe home and a darker world, and a mysterious older schoolmate, Max Demian, shows him a different way to read old stories and think for himself.
demian.pitch: Young Emil Sinclair is pulled between a safe, orderly home and a darker world, until a strange older schoolmate, Max Demian, shows him a different way to read old stories and to think for himself. A coming-of-age book about becoming who you are, told by a man looking back.

demon-copperhead.blurb: A boy born to a teenage mother in a trailer in Virginia's Appalachians tells how he survives foster care, child labour, school and a football injury that opens the door to opioids.
demon-copperhead.pitch: Demon is born in a trailer in the Virginia hills and tells his own story with a sharp tongue: foster homes, work he should never have had to do, a football injury and the pills that follow. It is a modern retelling of a Dickens novel, with a voice that will stay with you.

deti-pulnoci.blurb: Saleem Sinai, born at the stroke of midnight on the day India became independent, tells the story of his family and country, and discovers that the other children born in that hour have gifts.
deti-pulnoci.pitch: The boy born at the exact moment India became independent tells you how his life and his country's history are knotted together. The children born in that hour share strange gifts, and you follow what becomes of them.

dobreho-cloveka-tezko-najdes.blurb: A collection of stories set in the American South in which ordinary people meet something larger than they expected.
dobreho-cloveka-tezko-najdes.pitch: Stories of the American South in which ordinary people run into something far larger than they expected. Each one is short and sharp, and built around a moment that forces a character to see themselves. The title story is one of the best-known in American writing.

drahy-zivot.blurb: A collection of short stories about lives turned by desire, sudden feeling and chance events.
drahy-zivot.pitch: Quiet, precise stories about ordinary lives in small Ontario towns, where one small decision or hidden fact changes how a life runs. Each one is a self-contained world told with close attention to what its people want and conceal.
drahy-zivot.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

duha.blurb: The book follows three generations of the Brangwen family on an English farm as the old rural world gives way to the industrial one, ending on the youngest daughter Ursula.
duha.pitch: Three generations of one farming family in the English Midlands, from the old rural world to the new industrial one, each trying to work out how to live with a spouse and with oneself. The youngest, Ursula, wants more from life than her mother's world offered. It follows how what people want changes over a century.

evangelium-ohne.blurb: Theo Griepenkerl, an expert in Aramaic, finds nine scrolls in a looted Iraqi museum: an eyewitness gospel of the crucifixion, and publishing it sets off consequences for believers and others.
evangelium-ohne.pitch: A scholar of Aramaic pulls nine scrolls out of a looted museum in Iraq and finds an eyewitness account from the days of the crucifixion. The book follows what happens when he gives it to the world, in a story short enough to finish in one sitting.

fantastic-tales.blurb: A selection of Poe's fantastic tales printed with the English text alongside the Czech.
fantastic-tales.pitch: A compact selection of Poe's strange tales, printed with the original English alongside the Czech. Short pieces built on a single unsettling thought, a narrator who cannot trust his own mind.

gertruda.blurb: Kuhn, a young composer lamed by an accident, pours himself into music and a friendship with a famous singer, and falls in love with a woman he does not dare ask.
gertruda.pitch: Kuhn, a young composer left lame by an accident, pours himself into his music and into a friendship with a famous singer, and falls in love with a woman he cannot bring himself to ask. A quiet novel about what art costs and where it comes from.

hanebnost.blurb: After a scandal over a student costs him his university post, a divorced professor retreats to his daughter's smallholding in the Eastern Cape, where violence changes both of their lives.
hanebnost.pitch: A South African professor loses his job and his good name and retreats to his daughter's farm in the country. There, in a society that has changed around him, he has to face what he has done and what he owes the people near him. A short, hard novel that leaves you thinking about guilt, dignity and the new South Africa.

henderson-kral-deste.blurb: A restless American millionaire travels to Africa to escape his empty life, meets two tribes and is made their rain king.
henderson-kral-deste.pitch: A loud, restless American millionaire hears a voice in his head that only says 'I want', and flies off to Africa to find out what. He wrestles a prince, blows up a water supply with good intentions and ends up a tribe's rain king. It is funny and a bit wild, told in his own voice.

hluk-a-vrava.blurb: The Compson family's decline in Mississippi, told in four sections by three brothers and then by the family's servant Dilsey.
hluk-a-vrava.pitch: A Southern family comes apart, told through four different voices, each with its own way of seeing. If you know who the Compsons are before you start, the first voice makes sense and the rest of the book opens up.

honorarni-konzul.blurb: In an Argentine border town a doctor is drawn into a kidnapping by old school friends, who grab the British honorary consul by mistake.
honorarni-konzul.pitch: A kidnapping goes wrong from the first move: revolutionaries meant to seize an ambassador and took a minor consul instead, and the doctor who knows them is pulled into the hut where he is held. The book puts one question to every character in it, what you owe to the people you are caught up with by accident. A tense, grown-up story about loyalty and conscience.

istanbul.blurb: Orhan Pamuk's memoir of growing up in Istanbul, blending his family's history with the city's melancholy after the fall of the Ottoman Empire.
istanbul.pitch: Pamuk grew up among the faded grandeur of Istanbul, and he writes about the city and his own childhood as one picture. He gives a name to its shared melancholy, huzun, and you leave with a new way of looking at a city.

jako-rak.blurb: A journalist born on the day the Wilhelm Gustloff was torpedoed tells the history of the ship, from its launch to the sinking, and how his mother and his own teenage son carry that night differently.
jako-rak.pitch: A journalist born on the day the Wilhelm Gustloff was sunk tells the story of the ship from its launch to the night it went down, and of how his mother and his own son carry that night differently. It asks who is allowed to remember, and what happens when nobody speaks about it.

jama-a-kyvadlo-jine-povidky.blurb: A selection of twenty-seven tales by Poe, from the title story of torture in an Inquisition cell to other macabre and gothic stories.
jama-a-kyvadlo-jine-povidky.pitch: Twenty-seven of Poe's tales of dread: a prisoner in a cell with a slowly swinging blade, narrators haunted by their own minds. The title story in particular is a short, gripping survival piece.

jeden-den-ivana-denisovice-a-jine-povidk.blurb: A collection of Solzhenitsyn's prose built around a single day in a labour camp, with further stories of ordinary people caught in the Soviet system.
jeden-den-ivana-denisovice-a-jine-povidk.pitch: You spend one ordinary day with a prisoner in a labour camp and see how a man holds on to his dignity through bread, work and small acts of loyalty to the men around him. It is short, plain and concrete, and it leaves you with a hard question about what survives when everything is taken away.

jeden-den-ivana-denisovice-a-jine-prozy.blurb: A 1965 Czech edition of Solzhenitsyn's camp novella together with other short prose.
jeden-den-ivana-denisovice-a-jine-prozy.pitch: You spend one ordinary day with a prisoner in a labour camp and watch how he keeps his dignity through work, food and loyalty to the men beside him. It is short and plain, and it leaves behind the question of what a person still owns when everything is taken away.
jeden-den-ivana-denisovice-a-jine-prozy.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

joseph-anton.blurb: Salman Rushdie tells, in the third person, the years after the fatwa of 1989 that forced him to live in hiding under the name Joseph Anton, and the life that led to it.
joseph-anton.pitch: The true story of ten years in hiding under police protection after a death sentence for writing a novel, told by the man who lived it. You get the daily detail of a life lived in secret, and a clear look at what free expression cost and who stood with him.

kaddis-za-nenarozene-dite.blurb: During a walk at a conference, an unnamed man is asked about children and breaks into a long monologue on his marriage, his past and Auschwitz.
kaddis-za-nenarozene-dite.pitch: On a walk during a conference, a narrator is asked a casual question about children, and a long, bitter monologue pours out of him about his marriage, his schooling, Auschwitz and what it means to be Jewish without faith. A single intense voice that offers its whole life as a kaddish.

kapitan-a-nepritel.blurb: Three Greene stories in one volume, including the occupied-Vienna story first written as a film script.
kapitan-a-nepritel.pitch: Three stories by a master of morally troubled characters, from occupied post-war Vienna to a casino honeymoon and a boy taken away by a stranger. Each is short enough to read in an evening, so it is an easy way into an author known for characters who do the wrong thing for understandable reasons.

kentaur.blurb: A Pennsylvania science teacher wounded in the ankle by a student's arrow spends three winter days trying to get home with his teenage son, told alongside the myth of Chiron.
kentaur.pitch: A small-town Pennsylvania science teacher is hit in the ankle by a student's arrow and spends three winter days trying to get home with his teenage son. The story is told both as plain family life and as an ancient myth. It is a portrait of a father's love and struggle.

kocici-oko.blurb: A painter returns to Toronto for a retrospective and relives her childhood under a group of girls led by a charismatic friend.
kocici-oko.pitch: A painter goes back to Toronto for a retrospective of her work, and the city brings back the girls who ruled her childhood, with Cordelia the sharpest of them. The book follows how those years still shape the woman she became.
kocici-oko.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

kontrapunkt.blurb: A web of London intellectuals, artists and socialites in the 1920s, around two families, whose affairs, quarrels and ideas run alongside each other.
kontrapunkt.pitch: London in the 1920s, seen through a wide circle of writers, painters and hangers-on whose lives and opinions keep cutting across each other. It is built like a piece of music, with each voice answering the others.

krejci-z-panamy.blurb: Harry Pendel, a tailor to Panama's elite with a hidden past, is blackmailed by a British intelligence officer and begins inventing secrets that grow far beyond what he intended.
krejci-z-panamy.pitch: Harry Pendel is the tailor everyone in Panama City trusts with their secrets, and a British spy blackmails him into passing them on. Pendel, who has almost nothing to tell, starts inventing, and his stories grow beyond his control. A dark comedy about lies and what happens when powerful people want to be lied to.

kulicka-a-jine-povidky.blurb: A selection of Maupassant's stories led by the title novella, in which a prostitute nicknamed Boule de Suif travels through occupied France during the Franco-Prussian war.
kulicka-a-jine-povidky.pitch: Maupassant's best-known story follows a woman nicknamed Boule de Suif on a coach journey through occupied France, where her fellow passengers show what their respectability is worth. The other stories turn the same dry eye on soldiers, peasants and townspeople.

laska-dobre-zeny.blurb: A collection of short stories of ordinary lives in small-town Canada, led by a novella about a drowned optometrist and a nurse who learns something about it.
laska-dobre-zeny.pitch: The title story begins in a museum, with a box of an optometrist's instruments and three boys who find his body in a river, and follows a young nurse who has to decide what to do with a dying woman's secret. The other stories keep to the same quiet attention to what ordinary people hide.
laska-dobre-zeny.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

lionel-aspo.blurb: Desmond, a decent teenager from a rough London borough, lives under the thumb of his violent criminal uncle Lionel Asbo, until the uncle wins a huge lottery prize.
lionel-aspo.pitch: A teenager from a rotten corner of London tries to educate himself and stay decent while his violent uncle, a career criminal, rules the only home he has. When that uncle wins a fortune on the lottery, the gap between the two only widens. A dark, funny satire of modern England with a tender thread about learning, love and fatherhood.

lokalni-umrtveni.blurb: In 1967 Berlin a gymnasium pupil plans to burn his dachshund in front of a luxury hotel to shock a comfortable society into noticing napalm in Vietnam, while his teacher tells it all from a dentist's chair.
lokalni-umrtveni.pitch: A gymnasium student plans to burn his dachshund in front of a Berlin hotel to jolt a comfortable society that stays silent about napalm in Vietnam. Most of the story is told from a dentist's chair, by the teacher who is trying to talk him out of it.

luzinova-obrana.blurb: A gifted, awkward chess master is destroyed by the game that made him, as a marriage and a tournament press on him.
luzinova-obrana.pitch: A boy who finds in chess the only place he makes sense grows into a master the world admires and does not understand. You follow his mind from the inside as the game starts to organise everything else in his life.

malir-pomijiveho-sveta.blurb: In postwar Japan an ageing painter who once made propaganda for the militarists looks back on his career while arranging his younger daughter's marriage.
malir-pomijiveho-sveta.pitch: An old painter in postwar Japan tells you his own story while his youngest daughter's marriage talks hang on how his past is judged. What he wants you to think and what he actually did slowly come apart, and you are left weighing how far an artist answers for the cause he served.

ministerstvo-strachu.blurb: At a wartime charity fete in London, a man released from a psychiatric hospital wins a cake that a ring of spies badly wants.
ministerstvo-strachu.pitch: Blitz London, a charity fete, and a cake a man should never have won. A quiet, haunted man is hunted by people who will do anything for it and cannot tell whom to trust. It moves fast and it is all about what fear does to a person.

mlsoun.blurb: After Cambridge, Serena Frome is recruited into MI5 and sent to secretly fund a young writer, Tom Haley, as part of a 1970s campaign against communism. Her feelings for him are real, and the deception is hers.
mlsoun.pitch: A 1970s MI5 operation hides behind a literary grant, and the woman running it falls for the writer she is supposed to be steering. Expect a book about how fiction and lies shade into each other, with a last-chapter twist that rewrites what came before.

moc-a-slava.blurb: In 1930s Tabasco, where the church is outlawed, the last priest, an alcoholic with a child, flees from a zealous police lieutenant while still ministering to the poor.
moc-a-slava.pitch: The last priest in a Mexican state that has outlawed the church is on the run: a drinker, a failure by his own account, and still the one man people turn to. You will want him to get away, and the lieutenant hunting him is no cartoon villain but a man who believes just as hard.

modrovousovo-vejce.blurb: A 1983 collection of stories by Atwood on marriage, love and the quiet betrayals between men and women in contemporary Toronto.
modrovousovo-vejce.pitch: Atwood's stories follow couples and families in Toronto as they try to work out what went wrong in the rhythm of their lives. They are wry and observant, and a few reach back to the narrator's own childhood.
modrovousovo-vejce.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

moudra-krev.blurb: Hazel Motes returns from the war convinced that sin is avoided by believing in nothing, and starts preaching a Church Without Christ until a swindler copies his idea.
moudra-krev.pitch: Hazel Motes comes home from the war convinced that the only way to avoid sin is to believe in nothing, and starts preaching the Church Without Christ from the hood of his car. Then a swindler copies his idea to make money. A sharp, strange Southern novel about belief and stubbornness.

nas-clovek-v-havane.blurb: A struggling vacuum-cleaner salesman in Havana is recruited by British intelligence and, to pay for his daughter, invents a network of agents.
nas-clovek-v-havane.pitch: A mild salesman in Havana needs money for his daughter, so when British intelligence recruits him he invents agents and sends in drawings of vacuum-cleaner parts as secret installations. London believes every word, and the lie begins to follow him. It is funny, humane and sharp about spies and gullibility.

navstevni-barak.blurb: An old Russian recounts to his American stepdaughter the years he and his brother Lev spent in a Soviet labour camp, and the woman both of them loved before their arrest.
navstevni-barak.pitch: An old man writes a long confession to his stepdaughter while revisiting the Arctic camps where he was held. Two brothers jailed under Stalin once loved the same woman, and the book follows what that rivalry and the camp did to them over fifty years. A short, intense novel about love, brotherhood and guilt under tyranny.

nekdy-proste-prsi.blurb: Fifteen stories by Michel Faber, mixing fantastical satires of where civilisation is heading with realistic portraits of critical moments in ordinary lives.
nekdy-proste-prsi.pitch: Short stories by Michel Faber that move between the strange and the everyday: a god who finds Earth on a rubbish heap, a substitute teacher facing a class after a tragedy. Each one takes a single odd idea and follows it to the end.

neutesenci.blurb: A famous pianist arrives in an unnamed Central European city to give a concert and is drawn into the private troubles of everyone he meets.
neutesenci.pitch: A celebrated pianist arrives in a city that has pinned its hopes of renewal on his concert, and every person he meets hands him a problem of their own. It reads like a long anxious dream, with an idea about what an artist owes the people around him.

neznicitelna-laska.blurb: After a balloon accident at a picnic, science writer Joe Rose is followed by Jed Parry, a stranger who is convinced Joe loves him. Joe's certainty that he can explain everything starts to crack as Parry's attention turns dangerous.
neznicitelna-laska.pitch: A picnic, a runaway balloon and a man who dies in front of you, and then a stranger decides your life is his. Joe, a science writer used to explaining the world, has to work out what to do when no explanation helps, and you keep guessing what is really going on.

obraceni-casanovy.blurb: Two stories by Hesse: an ageing Casanova in a moment of self-reckoning, and a priest whose path leads him away from his order.
obraceni-casanovy.pitch: Hesse brings together two people who lived by their own rules and reach a turn in their lives: an ageing Casanova and a priest. Two short stories with the author's gentle humour and a sharp eye for hypocrisy.

odlesky-zapadu-slunce-a-jine-povidky.blurb: Short stories by a Russian writer in exile, shaped by memories of childhood and the Berlin emigre years.
odlesky-zapadu-slunce-a-jine-povidky.pitch: Short stories by a Russian exile who writes about the lost world of his childhood and the odd, lonely life of the emigre community in Berlin. Each piece is a small, carefully made picture, so you can dip in without a long commitment.

ostrov.blurb: A cynical journalist is shipwrecked on the isolated island of Pala, a society that mixes Eastern spiritual practice with Western science to build the best possible life for its people.
ostrov.pitch: Shipwrecked on an island that really tries to build the best possible life for everyone, a cynical journalist has to take in how schooling, family and work are all arranged differently there. You are left comparing it with the world outside.

pasazer.blurb: In 1980 a New Orleans salvage diver finds a sunken plane with a passenger missing, and strange officials start asking about it.
pasazer.pitch: A salvage diver discovers a sunken plane with one seat empty, and soon people are asking him questions he cannot answer. McCarthy follows his drifting, grieving life through long conversations about science, loss and chance.

penize.blurb: John Self, a hard-drinking maker of bad adverts, is offered the chance to direct his first feature film and flies between London and New York trying to make it happen.
penize.pitch: John Self, a hard-drinking maker of bad adverts, is offered the chance to direct his first feature film and flies between London and New York chasing it. He narrates his own self-destruction with a sharp, funny eye on the money culture that is swallowing him. It leaves you thinking about what greed does to a man who can still see himself clearly.

pi-a-jeho-zivot.blurb: Pi, a zookeeper's son who practises Hinduism, Christianity and Islam at once, is the sole human survivor of a shipwreck, adrift in a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger.
pi-a-jeho-zivot.pitch: Pi grows up in a zoo in India, curious about everything, including three religions at once. When the ship carrying his family and their animals sinks, he is left in a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger and 227 days of ocean. You get the clever, practical problem-solving of a survival story and a question to chew on afterward about which story you would choose to believe.

platejs.blurb: A narrator who has lived in every age since the Stone Age tells his pregnant wife about the cooks who fed him through history, while a tribunal puts the magic fish that advised him on trial.
platejs.pitch: A narrator who has lived in every age from the Stone Age to today recounts the great cooks who fed him, one for each month of his wife's pregnancy. History is seen from the kitchen, and a talking fish that once advised him is put on trial over who really ruled the world.

pod-koly.blurb: Hans Giebenrath, the brightest boy in a small town, is pushed by father and teachers into a rigorous seminary, and the pressure slowly breaks him.
pod-koly.pitch: Hans is the brightest boy in his town and everyone, father and teachers included, has plans for him. This is the story of a gifted boy and the schooling that wants to shape him, with a friendship with a restless young poet at its heart.

portugalske-velehory.blurb: Three linked stories, set in 1904, 1938 and the early 1980s, in which grieving men are drawn to the same Portuguese mountain village and to a chimpanzee.
portugalske-velehory.pitch: Three men, in three decades, each carrying a loss, are drawn toward the same remote mountain village in Portugal, and each story turns on a chimpanzee. The strange, tender tales ask what belief is for when grief takes over.

pozvani-na-popravu.blurb: Cincinnatus C. is sentenced to beheading for being opaque to the people around him and waits in a prison cell for an execution date nobody will tell him.
pozvani-na-popravu.pitch: A thirty-year-old teacher is condemned for something that cannot be named and spends his last days in a cell, arguing with jailers who treat his death as a pleasant social event. It is a short, strange story about one person who refuses to dissolve into the crowd. If Proměna worked for you, this is its livelier, funnier cousin.

pri-loupani-cibule.blurb: Gunter Grass recounts his Danzig youth, the war and the years after it, up to the writing of his first great novel, mixing documented fact with imagination.
pri-loupani-cibule.pitch: Grass looks back at his own youth in Danzig and the years after the war, peeling memory layer by layer and admitting how little of it he can fully trust. You get a famous writer's own account of growing up in a country that was falling apart, told up to the moment he sits down to write his breakthrough novel.

pribehy-vasne-a-lhostejnosti.blurb: Four Zweig novellas from the 1920s on the forms feeling and passion take, including Leporella and a woman's account of twenty-four hours.
pribehy-vasne-a-lhostejnosti.pitch: Four novellas by Zweig, each following one person gripped by a feeling they cannot manage. He is at his best on what drives people to do what they do, and each story is short enough to be read in a sitting.
pribehy-vasne-a-lhostejnosti.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

promluv-pameti.blurb: Nabokov's memoir of his life from 1903 to his emigration in 1940: a privileged Russian childhood, the revolution, exile.
promluv-pameti.pitch: You get a Russian childhood before the revolution told by a man who remembers everything, the nursery, the estate, the butterflies, and then the loss of all of it. Each chapter stands alone, so you can read it a piece at a time.

pruzracne-veci.blurb: Editor Hugh Person visits one Swiss town four times over twenty years while memory, love and a crime accumulate in the objects around him.
pruzracne-veci.pitch: A shy editor returns to the same Swiss town four times across twenty years, and the book looks at his life through the things he touches and what they remember. It is short and carefully built, for someone who likes a book that leaves an idea behind.

prvni-clovek.blurb: Jacques Cormery, in his forties, goes looking for the father who died before he knew him, and the search leads back to his childhood in a poor district of Algiers and to his silent, illiterate mother.
prvni-clovek.pitch: A man in his forties goes looking for the father he never knew and finds the poor Algiers childhood he grew up in, with a silent mother at its centre. It is the most personal book of an author known for his ideas, and a teacher who changes a boy's life is its warmest thread.

putovani-jednoho-slona.blurb: In 1551 King John III of Portugal sends an elephant, Solomon, and his keeper Subhro on foot across Europe as a wedding gift to an Austrian archduke.
putovani-jednoho-slona.pitch: An elephant and his keeper are given away as a wedding present and set off on foot from Lisbon to Vienna. The book is short and warm, with a bond between man and animal at its heart and a dry narrator who enjoys every stop on the road.

ravelstein.blurb: A dying university professor asks his friend, a writer, to write his memoir, and the narrator recalls their talks on philosophy, politics and friendship.
ravelstein.pitch: A brilliant, extravagant professor knows he is dying and asks his friend to write about him afterwards. What you read is that friendship: long talks about philosophy, politics and how to live, with a narrator who is amused and moved by the man.

setkani-v-telgte.blurb: In 1647, while peace is negotiated nearby, a company of German poets gathers at an inn to read, quarrel and decide whether literature should try to influence the war's end.
setkani-v-telgte.pitch: In 1647, while peace is negotiated nearby, a company of German poets gathers at an inn to read their work, quarrel and decide whether writing can change anything in a country ruined by war. A short book about real writers and one question: what is literature for when the world is burning?

slecna-fifi-a-jine-povidky.blurb: About forty Maupassant stories from the Franco-Prussian war and from Norman country life, among them the well-known tale of a prostitute on a coach journey.
slecna-fifi-a-jine-povidky.pitch: About forty short stories by Maupassant, from the occupied France of the Prussian war to the farms of Normandy. They are dry, fast and sharp-eyed about what people do for money, pride and country.

smrt-na-uver.blurb: A doctor in a grim clinic recalls his boyhood among the poor of Paris, from the family shop in a covered arcade to an English boarding school and a string of failed jobs.
smrt-na-uver.pitch: A fevered doctor looks back at his boyhood in the Paris arcades: the stubborn parents, the nightmare school, the schemers and inventors who took him on. Everything goes wrong and the voice makes it ferociously funny.

souostrovi-gulag-3.blurb: The final instalment of Solzhenitsyn's literary investigation into the Soviet camp system, covering katorga, exile and the years after Stalin's death.
souostrovi-gulag-3.pitch: Solzhenitsyn assembles witness accounts into a record of how the camp system ran and how people resisted it, including escape attempts and the Kengir uprising. You come away understanding the mechanism, not only the suffering.

spion-ktery-prisel-z-chladu.blurb: Alec Leamas, a British spy whose agents have been wiped out in East Berlin, is given a final assignment: pose as a defector and bring down the officer behind it.
spion-ktery-prisel-z-chladu.pitch: Britain's spy Alec Leamas waits at the Berlin Wall for an agent who never makes it across, and is handed one last job: bring down the man who wrecked his network. You follow a worn-out, embittered man into a scheme where every move has a reason you only see later, and it leaves you thinking about what a country may ask of one person.

srdce-temnoty.blurb: Marlow recounts his journey up the Congo River as a steamboat captain for a trading company, and his search for the company's most successful and most feared agent, Kurtz.
srdce-temnoty.pitch: Marlow tells, on a boat anchored in the Thames, how he went up the Congo to find a legendary trader deep in the interior. It is short and carries a hard idea about what happens to people when no one is watching them.

stella-maris.blurb: In 1972 a young mathematics prodigy at a Wisconsin psychiatric hospital speaks with her doctor about her illness, her brother and the limits of what can be known.
stella-maris.pitch: A gifted young mathematician sits across from a psychiatrist in a Wisconsin clinic, and over seven conversations they argue about numbers, God and whether anything outside the mind can be trusted. It is a short book made entirely of talk, with a sharp and funny voice at its centre.

stepni-vlk.blurb: Harry Haller, a middle-aged intellectual who feels half man and half wolf, contemplates suicide until a young woman draws him into dancing, drugs and a hallucinatory Magic Theatre.
stepni-vlk.pitch: Harry Haller, a middle-aged writer who feels half man and half wolf, is on the edge of giving up when a stranger shows him how to dance, laugh and live a little. It is a book about the many people each of us contains, and about the strange theatre where he meets them.

suttree.blurb: A wealthy man's son lives on a houseboat among the outcasts of 1950s Knoxville, and the novel follows his encounters over several years.
suttree.pitch: A man from a good family abandons his place in the world and lives on a houseboat among the thieves, drunks and dreamers of Knoxville. It is darkly funny, full of oddballs and schemers, and written in prose unlike anything else.

svedomi-proti-nasili.blurb: Sixteenth-century Geneva under Calvin's rule: the scholar Sebastian Castellio stands alone against the reformer's theocracy after the execution of Michael Servetus, in Zweig's essay on freedom of conscience.
svedomi-proti-nasili.pitch: Geneva under Calvin is a city where a wrong belief can cost you your life, and one scholar, Castellio, decides to answer it with nothing but words. Zweig tells it as a David-and-Goliath story that moves quickly and keeps asking what each man wants and why. You are left with a question that outlasts the century: who has the right to force a conscience?

synove-a-milenci.blurb: Paul Morel grows up in a Nottinghamshire mining family, torn between his possessive mother and the two women he loves.
synove-a-milenci.pitch: Paul Morel grows up in a Nottinghamshire mining family, pulled between a mother who adores him and the two women who love him. It is a close look at what we owe the people who raised us, and what that bond costs. Observant and warm, and drawn from the author's own life.

tajny-agent.blurb: In 1880s London a shopkeeper secretly serves as an agent for a foreign embassy, and is ordered to provoke an outrage that will turn the public against anarchists.
tajny-agent.pitch: A shabby London shop is the cover for a double life, and an embassy official orders one man to stage an outrage that will turn the city against the anarchists. The book follows what the plan does to the people nearest him, told with a dry, ironic eye.

telegraph-avenue.blurb: Two Oakland families, one running a used-record store and the other a midwifery practice, are tested by a planned megastore and by fathers who left their sons.
telegraph-avenue.pitch: A used-record store and a midwifery practice in Oakland, two families, and a business threatened by a big new neighbour. The book is about what fathers owe their sons, and it is written with a love of music that you can hear on the page.

treti-rise.blurb: A young German war-game champion on holiday on the Costa Brava keeps a diary as a friend disappears and he is drawn into a game with a local stranger.
treti-rise.pitch: A German war-game champion spends a summer on the Costa Brava planning a new strategy, and a friend's disappearance draws him into a high-stakes match against a stranger. The diary form keeps you inside his head.

uz-davno-ti-chci-neco-rict-a-jine-povidk.blurb: A selection of short stories centred on the inner lives of mainly female characters.
uz-davno-ti-chci-neco-rict-a-jine-povidk.pitch: Quiet, precise stories about ordinary lives in small Ontario towns, where one small decision or hidden fact changes how a life runs. Each one is a self-contained world told with close attention to what its people want and conceal.
uz-davno-ti-chci-neco-rict-a-jine-povidk.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

valka-na-konci-sveta.blurb: In 1890s Brazil a wandering preacher gathers the poor of the backlands into a community the new republic treats as a rebellion, and the army is sent against it.
valka-na-konci-sveta.pitch: In the dry backlands of Brazil in the 1890s, a preacher draws thousands of outcasts into a town of their own, and the young republic decides it is a threat. You watch both sides, soldiers and believers alike, move toward a war nobody can stop.

verejna-tajemstvi.blurb: A collection of eight short stories set mostly in a small Ontario town, built on things everyone half knows and nobody says.
verejna-tajemstvi.pitch: Eight stories set mostly in the small Ontario town of Carstairs, each built on something everyone half knows and nobody says. The title piece follows a girl who vanishes on a hike and the town that cannot stop talking about it.
verejna-tajemstvi.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

vybledla-krajina-s-kopci.blurb: A widow in England, haunted by her elder daughter's suicide, recalls a summer in postwar Nagasaki and a friendship that mirrors her own choices.
vybledla-krajina-s-kopci.pitch: A woman living alone in the English countryside revisits one summer in postwar Nagasaki and the neighbour she befriended then. The memory keeps shifting under her, and you read closely to work out what she is really remembering.

vzdalena-hvezda.blurb: A Chilean narrator tells of a poet and air-force pilot whose sky-writing hides murder under Pinochet, and of the later hunt for him.
vzdalena-hvezda.pitch: A narrator in exile traces a charismatic young poet through the coup, and the skywriting he does becomes something far darker. It is a short, unsettling book that asks what art is worth when it feeds on other lives.

vzorove-dny.blurb: Three linked novellas set in New York: a nineteenth-century factory ghost story, a thriller after a terror attack and a far-future tale of an android who recites Whitman.
vzorove-dny.pitch: Three stories set in the same city, from an industrial nineteenth century to a far future, tied together by the same characters returning in new forms and by the poems of Walt Whitman. Each part is a different kind of story, so you get a ghost story, a suspense piece and a science-fiction chase in one book.

zapisniky-i.blurb: A volume of Camus's private notebooks: observations, drafts of ideas, reading notes and travel jottings kept across several years.
zapisniky-i.pitch: Camus's private notebooks, where you can watch the ideas behind his novels and essays take shape in short entries, travel notes and passing observations. It is a book to dip into for the thinking itself, not for a story.

zapisniky-ii.blurb: A volume of Camus's private notebooks: observations, drafts of ideas, reading notes and travel jottings kept across several years.
zapisniky-ii.pitch: Camus's private notebooks, where you can watch the ideas behind his novels and essays take shape in short entries, travel notes and passing observations. It is a book to dip into for the thinking itself, not for a story.

zapisniky-iii.blurb: A volume of Camus's private notebooks: observations, drafts of ideas, reading notes and travel jottings kept across several years.
zapisniky-iii.pitch: Camus's private notebooks, where you can watch the ideas behind his novels and essays take shape in short entries, travel notes and passing observations. It is a book to dip into for the thinking itself, not for a story.
zapisniky-iii.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

zazracni-hosi.blurb: Over one chaotic weekend, a Pittsburgh professor with a never-ending manuscript is left by his wife, learns his mistress is pregnant and gets entangled in a student's crime.
zazracni-hosi.pitch: A professor with a half-finished 2,600-page manuscript has one weekend in which everything he has been putting off arrives at once. It is a funny, fast-moving campus comedy with a brilliant and troubled student at its centre.

zeny-milujici.blurb: Two sisters in a Midlands mining town each fall for a very different man, and the two relationships test what love and freedom between two people can mean.
zeny-milujici.pitch: Two sisters in a Midlands mining town fall for two very different men, and each couple becomes a test of what love and freedom between two people can be. The talk matters as much as the events: the characters argue out how to live. It is a book of ideas about marriage and independence, dense but full of strong personalities.

zivot-a-doba-michaela-k.blurb: In a South Africa torn by civil war, a simple gardener with a cleft lip sets out to carry his sick mother to the farm she remembers and then tries to live off the land.
zivot-a-doba-michaela-k.pitch: In a country torn by civil war, a simple gardener sets out to carry his dying mother to the countryside she remembers. Slipping past the authorities, he tries to live on the land on his own terms. A short, quiet novel about freedom and what it means to be left alone.

zivot-za-zivot.blurb: A young surfer dies in a car accident on the way to the sea, and in twenty-four hours his parents, doctors and a transplant coordinator face the question of donating his heart to a woman waiting for one.
zivot-za-zivot.pitch: In the space of one day, a family has to decide whether to let the heart of their dead son save another life. You follow the parents, the doctors and the woman waiting for the heart, with the real details of how a transplant happens, and it leaves you thinking about what a body is.

zradce-mezi-nami.blurb: A young Oxford academic and his barrister girlfriend, on holiday in Antigua, are asked by a Russian money-launderer to pass an offer to British intelligence in exchange for his family's safety.
zradce-mezi-nami.pitch: On holiday in Antigua, an Oxford lecturer and his barrister girlfriend are befriended by a Russian millionaire who asks them to carry an offer to British intelligence: his secrets for his family's safety. Two ordinary people find out what they will risk for a man who has asked them for help.

co-ti-svira-hrdlo.blurb: Twelve stories of Nigerians at home and in America: a student sheltering in a riot, a writer at a workshop, a young woman who marries through an arrangement.
co-ti-svira-hrdlo.pitch: Twelve stories about Nigerians at home and in America: a student sheltering through a riot, a writer at a workshop, a young woman who comes to the US through an arranged marriage. Adichie has an eye for the small moments where two cultures, and two people, fail to understand each other.
co-ti-svira-hrdlo.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

bratri-karamazovovi.blurb: The Karamazov family: a shameless father and his three very different sons, a quarrel over money and a woman, and a murder that puts the eldest on trial.
bratri-karamazovovi.pitch: A violent, shameless father and his three very different sons, a quarrel over money and a woman, and a murder that puts one of them on trial. What pulls you through is why each of them acts as he does, and the long arguments about faith, freedom and guilt the brothers have with one another. It leaves you with ideas that stay.

druhy-sesit-smesnych-lasek.blurb: Three early stories about desire and the roles people play, including a young couple on holiday who start pretending to be strangers.
druhy-sesit-smesnych-lasek.pitch: Three early stories of the kind that made Kundera's name: short, ironic tales about desire and the roles people play. One follows a young couple on holiday who start pretending to be strangers. Each is built around a clear idea.
druhy-sesit-smesnych-lasek.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

elizabeth-finchova.blurb: Neil, a struggling actor, befriends his adult-education teacher Elizabeth Finch, who leaves him her library and notebooks; he takes up her interest in the Roman emperor Julian the Apostate.
elizabeth-finchova.pitch: Neil, a struggling actor, becomes an unlikely friend of his formidable teacher Elizabeth Finch, and when she dies she leaves him her books and notebooks. Going through them he takes up her fascination with Julian the Apostate, the Roman emperor who tried to turn back the Christianisation of his empire. It is a book about what a teacher leaves in a student, and about a moment she believed history took a wrong turn.

flaubertuv-papousek.blurb: Geoffrey Braithwaite, a retired doctor and widower, tries to find out which of two stuffed parrots was the one on Flaubert's desk while he wrote A Simple Heart.
flaubertuv-papousek.pitch: A retired doctor sets out to find which of two stuffed parrots really sat on Flaubert's desk, and the hunt turns into a playful, argumentative portrait of a writer and of how little a biography can ever know. You follow a narrator who is clearly keeping something back behind all the scholarship, and why he cannot stop searching comes out slowly. It leaves you with a real idea to chew on.

hrac.blurb: Three Dostoevsky works: The Gambler, about a tutor in a German spa town and roulette; The Eternal Husband, about a widower and his late wife's former lover; and An Unpleasant Predicament, a short satire.
hrac.pitch: Three Dostoevsky stories in one book. In The Gambler a tutor in a German resort town is drawn to the roulette tables while chasing a woman he cannot win. The Eternal Husband sets two men against each other in a tense psychological duel. The third is a short satire about a well-meaning official.
hrac.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

kniha-smichu-a-zapomneni.blurb: A novel in seven variations: Tamina, an exile, tries to recover her diaries from Prague, around stories of friends, lovers and politics in communist Czechoslovakia.
kniha-smichu-a-zapomneni.pitch: Seven linked pieces, a novel in variations, about forgetting: of a person, of a country's history, of one's own past. At its centre is Tamina, an exile who wants her diaries back from Prague, and around her Kundera weaves stories of friends, lovers and politics, stepping into the book himself to comment. It is a book to think with as much as to follow.

netocka-nezvanovova.blurb: Netochka grows up in poverty with her stepfather, a failed musician who thinks himself a neglected genius, and is later taken in by an aristocratic family where she attaches herself intensely to the proud younger daughter.
netocka-nezvanovova.pitch: A girl grows up in a poor, chaotic household with a stepfather who believes himself a neglected musical genius, and is later taken in by an aristocratic family where she is still an outsider. Her intense childhood attachment to a proud, headstrong girl is the heart of the story. Dostoevsky wrote it in 1849, shortly before his arrest.

pohlednout-do-slunce.blurb: Jean Serjeant grows up in wartime England; her life from girlhood to extreme old age is traced through the men who pass through it, a marriage, a late son, and questions about death and how to live.
pohlednout-do-slunce.pitch: Jean Serjeant grows up in wartime England, and you follow her through a long life of ordinary-looking choices, odd encounters and a restless search for answers to the big questions. It is told from inside her head, with dry humour, and keeps circling one thing: how to live well when you know how it ends.

purpurovy-ibisek.blurb: Fifteen-year-old Kambili, in Enugu, lives under her wealthy, devout and violent father; after a coup she and her brother stay with their aunt, a university lecturer, and see another way of living.
purpurovy-ibisek.pitch: Fifteen-year-old Kambili lives in a big house in Nigeria with a father everyone admires for his generosity and piety, and who is feared at home. When a coup upends the country she and her brother are sent to stay with their lively aunt, and a different way of living and speaking opens up. You follow a quiet girl finding her own voice, with faith, family and politics around her.
purpurovy-ibisek.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

slova-pojmy-situace.blurb: Kundera's own glossary of the words he keeps returning to, an essay on aesthetics and existence, and short texts on novels.
slova-pojmy-situace.pitch: Kundera's own glossary of the words he keeps returning to, such as kitsch, irony and the comic, followed by essays on the novel as a way of exploring human existence. At about ninety pages it is a short way into the ideas behind his fiction.
slova-pojmy-situace.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

stolek-s-citrony.blurb: Eleven stories about people growing old and facing death, from a man and his haircuts to a concertgoer with no tolerance for coughing.
stolek-s-citrony.pitch: Eleven stories about growing old, each with its own voice and situation: a man and his haircuts across the years, a concertgoer with no patience for coughing, a loan scheme where only the last survivor collects. Humour and sadness sit side by side, and the theme is looked at from many sides rather than just one.

valcik-na-rozloucenou.blurb: A famous trumpeter, a spa nurse who tells him she is pregnant, a doctor with a secret scheme and others cross paths during a few days in a Czech spa town.
valcik-na-rozloucenou.pitch: A few days in a Czech spa town where a famous trumpeter, a spa nurse, a doctor with a secret scheme and a man about to leave the country for good all cross paths. Kundera plays it as a dark farce, with a sharp eye for what people want and what they will do to get it.

zapisky-o-smutku.blurb: Adichie writes in thirty short reflections about the sudden death of her father, a statistics professor, in June 2020.
zapisky-o-smutku.pitch: Adichie writes about the sudden death of her father, a statistics professor who survived the Biafran war, in thirty short reflections. It is a portrait of him and of how grief rearranges a person, raw and exact.
zapisky-o-smutku.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

zapisky-z-mrtveho-domu.blurb: Aleksandr Petrovich Goryanchikov, a nobleman sentenced to hard labour in Siberia, records the inmates, the work, the holidays and the punishments of the prison.
zapisky-z-mrtveho-domu.pitch: A nobleman sentenced to hard labour in Siberia tells what he sees: the inmates, the guards, the holidays and the punishments. Dostoevsky wrote it from his own years in a prison camp, and its strength is the gallery of unforgettable characters and the question of what a person needs to stay human when freedom is taken away.

gilead.blurb: A 77-year-old Iowa preacher with a failing heart writes a long letter to his young son, drawing on family memories and the return of a troubled godson.
gilead.pitch: An elderly preacher in small-town Iowa, with a failing heart, writes a long letter to his young son so the boy will know him after he is gone. Memories of his grandfather and father, and the return of a troubled godson, fill its pages. A quiet book about love for the world's small things, and about forgiveness.

24-tvari-billyho-milligana-slovak-editio.blurb: The true story of Billy Milligan, charged with kidnapping and raping women in Ohio, who was found to have twenty-four distinct personalities and was acquitted by reason of insanity.
24-tvari-billyho-milligana-slovak-editio.pitch: In 1977 a man was arrested in Ohio, and the doctors who examined him found not one personality but many, each with its own skills and memories. You follow the investigation and the trial that asked how responsibility works for a mind split into pieces.

a-darkling-sea.blurb: A human research lab studies the blind crustacean natives of an ice-covered ocean world under a strict ban on contact, until an Ilmataran kills a human diver and the ban is tested.
a-darkling-sea.pitch: Under the ice of a distant moon lives a blind, shelled people with a sonar world of their own, and one of them is a scientist as curious as any human. You see humans and aliens misread each other from both sides, with the rules imposed by a stronger species making it worse. The aliens are the reason to read, in the way Speaker for the Dead was about understanding another culture.

a-long-way-gone.blurb: Ishmael Beah, a twelve-year-old boy in Sierra Leone, loses his family in the civil war, is recruited into the government army as a child soldier and is later taken into a rehabilitation programme.
a-long-way-gone.pitch: Ishmael Beah is twelve when the civil war reaches his village in Sierra Leone, and he wanders the countryside with other boys until an army takes them in. The book is a plain, direct account of how a child is changed by war and what it takes to become someone again. You come away with a first-hand picture of a conflict many people know only from the news.

armor.blurb: A soldier in powered armor fights an insect enemy on a hostile planet, and years later a space pirate finds his armor.
armor.pitch: Felix drops with his company onto a planet where the enemy waits in the mountain. Years later a space pirate finds his armor and begins to uncover what it recorded. The battle sections are vivid, and the book is partly about the armor people build around themselves.

beacon-23.blurb: A badly wounded war veteran keeps a lonely gravity-wave beacon that warns ships about an asteroid belt, until visitors and his own memory start to upset the routine.
beacon-23.pitch: One man, a lighthouse in space and a lot of silence, until the visitors start to arrive. The narrator is sarcastic and haunted, and the humour is what makes the loneliness bearable. It is a character study of a damaged soldier that also asks what war leaves behind.

brigady-duchu.blurb: The Colonial Defense Forces copy a traitor's mind into a new body, but the transfer seems to fail, and the young soldier who wakes up is raised by the Special Forces instead.
brigady-duchu.pitch: You follow a soldier who was grown for war and has never had a childhood, as he learns that another man's memories are waking up inside him. The question running through the book is who he will choose to be once he knows. Scalzi keeps it quick and wry, and the ethics of breeding soldiers who never got a say stay with you.

cervena-sestra.blurb: Eight-year-old Nona is saved from the gallows by a nun and taken to a convent where girls are trained to fight in a world of ice.
cervena-sestra.pitch: On a world of ice with a dying sun, a condemned girl is rescued and taken to a convent that trains novices as fighters. You follow Nona and the friends she makes there over years of training, in a setting whose ice, peoples and powers hang together. It starts with one of the best opening lines in recent fantasy.

cesta-do-babylonu.blurb: Schoolmaster Thomas Senlin loses his new wife at the foot of the Tower of Babel and climbs through its strange levels to find her.
cesta-do-babylonu.pitch: Thomas Senlin, a mild schoolmaster, loses his wife within minutes of arriving at the great Tower of Babel on their honeymoon. To find her he must climb its levels, each one a different society with its own rules and tricks. You watch a naive, proud man learn how the Tower works and become someone harder and wiser. It is inventive, funny and full of things to think about.

cesta-kralu.blurb: A disgraced soldier sold into slavery, a warlord troubled by visions of a lost age and a young woman who seeks a famous scholar's help in order to steal from her, all on a world swept by storms that reshape the land.
cesta-kralu.pitch: A world scoured by storms that remake the land, where a soldier-turned-slave, a general haunted by visions he cannot explain and a young scholar with a secret each want something different. You spend the pages inside their reasons and their flaws, and the oaths and bonds with living spirits that give them power feel like something being slowly uncovered. A big epic with the long-arc friendships you loved in Licanius.

city-of-pearl.blurb: An environmental enforcement officer leads a military team to a distant world to find a lost human colony and finds a pair of alien species with very different ideas about humans.
city-of-pearl.pitch: A hardened ex-cop commands a team sent to see what became of a lost human colony and finds alien neighbours with their own moral rules. It is a first-contact story where the argument is what a species owes the world it lives on, and the lead is stubborn enough to hold your attention.

cizinec.blurb: Bren Cameron, the human translator to an alien species, survives an assassination attempt and tries to understand who wants him dead and why.
cizinec.pitch: Humans and the alien atevi have lived apart for centuries, and Bren is the only human who speaks to them. When someone tries to kill him he has to read a culture that does not feel what he feels, and every misreading could cost him his life. If you liked Speaker for the Dead, this is a book about understanding something truly different.

dark-age.blurb: Darrow and the heir to the old order are caught in a brutal war across the solar system as the cast of viewpoints widens.
dark-age.pitch: The war that was supposed to bring peace turns into a siege, and the story follows Darrow and several people who each want something different. It is the largest and fiercest turn the saga takes, with the people at its centre pushed hard.

dark-eden.blurb: Generations after a starship crew was stranded on a planet with no sun, their descendants live around warm lantern trees, waiting for rescue, until a young man decides to leave and explore the dark.
dark-eden.pitch: A few hundred descendants of two stranded explorers cling to a warm valley on a planet without a sun, telling the story of Earth as a legend. You follow two young people and a restless leader who will not just wait. What it costs to look beyond the valley is the question, and the world feels real because of how the Family talks.

dauntless.blurb: Captain John Geary wakes after a century in a survival pod and finds himself commanding a stranded fleet deep in enemy territory.
dauntless.pitch: Black Jack Geary wakes up a hundred years after a battle everyone remembers differently. The fleet that reveres him is trapped deep in enemy space and has forgotten the discipline he knew. You learn his changed world alongside him while he decides what kind of leader to be.

divoke-labute.blurb: Jung Chang tells the story of her grandmother, a warlord's concubine, her mother, a Communist official, and herself, growing up in China through the Mao years and the Cultural Revolution.
divoke-labute.pitch: Three women in one family live through warlords, Japanese occupation, civil war and Mao: Jung Chang's grandmother, her mother and herself. You get an inside view of how an enormous country actually felt from the kitchen table, and you keep wondering what each of them wanted and why they chose as they did. It is long, but it moves like a family saga and leaves you with a different picture of a century of Chinese history.

dorsai.blurb: Donal Graeme, a young Dorsai mercenary, rises quickly through the ranks of the armies of the human colony worlds.
dorsai.pitch: The Dorsai sell their soldiers to the other human worlds, and Donal Graeme is the best of them. You follow his rise through the ranks, with battles won by unexpected moves. The book is built on a world that breeds its cultures for different strengths.

earth-unaware.blurb: A family-run mining ship and a corporate rival work the asteroid belt while a hidden alien presence draws near.
earth-unaware.pitch: A mining ship crewed by one family works the asteroid belt while a rival corporate vessel competes for the same ore and the first sign of something alien creeps closer. You get ambitions and loyalties colliding in a believable frontier of cheap labour and big money, with the long dread of knowing what is coming.

enclave.blurb: Deuce, a huntress in an underground enclave, is paired with a boy from outside and the two are exiled to the ruined surface.
enclave.pitch: Deuce hunts for her underground community in the dark tunnels of a wrecked New York, until she is paired with a stranger and both are cast out to the surface. Fast, tense and full of fights with the creatures that haunt the tunnels. You follow her as she learns what her enclave kept from her.

ender-ve-vyhnanstvi.blurb: After the war, Ender leaves Earth with his sister to govern a new colony world, and faces a ship captain who wants to rule through him.
ender-ve-vyhnanstvi.pitch: Ender is done with the war and with Earth. He sails to a new colony as its governor, with his sister beside him and a ship's captain scheming to use him as a puppet. It is quiet, interpersonal power play and a young man trying to build something that will outlast his own reputation, the same thinking-over-fighting side of him you loved in Speaker for the Dead.

eon.blurb: A hollow asteroid appears in Earth orbit during a Cold War standoff, and a relativistic mathematician is brought inside to explore its chambers and the impossible corridor that runs out of them.
eon.pitch: A mysterious asteroid arrives in orbit and turns out to be hollow, with a seventh chamber that goes on forever. You explore it through a mathematician whose work may unlock its secret, and the question of who built it and why pulls you through. If the alien-world wonder of Project Hail Mary appealed, this is wonder on a much bigger scale.

furies-of-calderon.blurb: In a valley on the edge of a realm where everyone commands elemental spirits, a boy with no such gift is caught up when a neighbouring people goes to war.
furies-of-calderon.pitch: Tavi is the one boy in the valley with no gift for the elemental spirits everybody else commands, so he gets by on cunning. A border war is brewing around him, and several storylines, from a young spy to his stubborn uncle, converge on it. It is a brisk, swashbuckling epic with a lead you will want to see win.

gregor-a-mesto-pod-mestem.blurb: Gregor falls through a grate in his apartment's laundry room into a hidden world beneath New York, where humans, giant rats and spiders are on the edge of war.
gregor-a-mesto-pod-mestem.pitch: Gregor falls through a grate in his laundry room and lands in an underground world of giant spiders, rats and pale humans. His father is somewhere in it, and he cannot go home without him, so he takes his small sister Boots and goes looking. It is a fast adventure with a hero who cares about his family, from the author of The Hunger Games.

grisa-svetlo-a-stiny.blurb: An orphaned mapmaker in the army discovers a power that might end the Shadow Fold that splits her country.
grisa-svetlo-a-stiny.pitch: Alina is an orphaned army cartographer when a crossing of the dark Shadow Fold reveals a power nobody expected. She is brought into the glittering court of the magic-wielding Grisha, and the man who rules it draws her in. The setting is Russian-flavoured and the magic is built on a kind of small science, which makes it feel unusual.

half-way-home.blurb: A few dozen teenagers wake on a distant planet with their ship burning and half their training, and must decide how to live together before they can survive.
half-way-home.pitch: A group of teenagers wakes up on a planet with half their training and no adults, and the way they organise themselves is the heart of it. Porter, a young trainee psychologist, watches the group split along lines nobody chose. It is short and quick, with a feel of Lord of the Flies in space.

halucinace.blurb: Oliver Sacks describes the many kinds of hallucination, from those of the blind and the grieving to those of migraine, sleep and drugs.
halucinace.pitch: Hallucinations are far more common than most people think, and a neurologist shows what is going on in ordinary people who see faces, hear music or sense a presence that is not there. It is a calm, curious look at where the line between what is real and what the brain makes up actually sits.

hrdina-veku.blurb: A year after the old tyrant's end, the world is ending in ash and quakes, and the heroine, her husband and a faithful scholar search for what the oldest records hid, hoping to save it.
hrdina-veku.pitch: The end of the world is close, and the clues to stopping it were hidden long ago in the history you have been learning. Vin, Elend and Sazed race for answers, and Sazed's struggle with what he believes sits at the heart of it. The mysteries laid down across the series come together, and the pieces fit.

hvezdna-pechota.blurb: Johnnie Rico joins the Federal Service after school, trains as a mobile infantryman and fights an arachnid species in an interstellar war.
hvezdna-pechota.pitch: Rico signs up for the service that decides who gets to vote, and you follow him from boot camp to the armored drop onto an enemy world. The book keeps asking what a citizen owes a society, and the army it builds follows from that one answer. If Old Man's War held you with its soldiers and its world, this is where that tradition started.

inkarceron.blurb: Finn, a seventeen-year-old with no memory of life before, is a prisoner inside Incarceron, a living prison that is a world of its own. A crystal key lets him speak to Claudia, the Warden's daughter, who lives in the Outside and is promised in an arranged marriage she wants no part of.
inkarceron.pitch: You are inside Incarceron, a prison so vast and alive it has become a world, and Finn, who remembers nothing before it, is certain there is an Outside. A strange key lets him talk to Claudia, a Warden's daughter who has her own reasons to dig into the prison's secrets. If you liked the way the unknown gradually opens up in Project Hail Mary, this has the same pull: two people, two worlds, and the need to find out what is really going on.

iron-gold.blurb: Ten years after the war, Darrow, a Red girl, a Gray soldier and the deposed heir of the old order each live in the war's aftermath.
iron-gold.pitch: Darrow's war is won, but peace is not what anyone expected, and the story now splits among a Red girl, a Gray former soldier, the old order's deposed heir and Darrow himself. You get the same fierce, thinking-heavy world you loved in Red Rising, seen from people who want very different things.

isles-of-the-emberdark.blurb: On a small island, a trapper pushes his people to modernise before invaders from the stars arrive, while a dragon captain gathers a crew of misfits to explore the wider Cosmere.
isles-of-the-emberdark.pitch: An islander who has spent his life with rare birds has five years to drag his people into a modern age before outsiders from the stars come to take what they have. Alongside him, a dragon captain gathers a crew of misfits that reviewers compare to a spaceship family. You get a clash between old ways and new, and companions who learn to rely on each other.

kalamita.blurb: David closes in on the source of the Epics' powers and has to decide how far he will go for the people he loves.
kalamita.pitch: David closes in on the source of Epic powers and on the Epic who has stood at the centre of everything. The questions the whole series has raised get answers, and he has to decide who he is willing to save. It is a fast ending with the plans and tricks you came for.

krev-a-jed.blurb: Fitz, the unwanted bastard of a prince, is brought to a royal castle as a child and quietly trained as the king's assassin.
krev-a-jed.pitch: You live inside Fitz's head from childhood on: a boy nobody wanted, learning what loyalty to a king costs and what he himself wants. The bond he forms with an animal is one of the most affecting threads in the book. Court intrigue builds slowly around him, and the people around him are drawn with real depth.

krvava-cesta.blurb: On her eighteenth birthday Saba's twin brother is kidnapped, and she sets off across a ruined desert land to bring him back.
krvava-cesta.pitch: Saba's twin brother is taken on their birthday, and she crosses a dried-out, ruined land to get him back. She is angry and stubborn, and her rough way of speaking carries you straight into her head. It moves quickly, with cage fights, escapes and a few unexpected friends.

light-bringer.blurb: Darrow and the former heir of the old order continue through a solar-system war told from four viewpoints.
light-bringer.pitch: The saga continues through four viewpoints, with readers saying that looking at the world through Lysander's eyes gives real insight. It brings the same thinking-heavy, high-stakes war you loved in Red Rising to a new chapter in the lives of the people who started it.

mame-na-vybranou.blurb: Edith Eger survives Auschwitz as a teenage dancer, emigrates to the United States and becomes a clinical psychologist; she mixes her own story with the stories of the patients she helps.
mame-na-vybranou.pitch: Edith Eger was a sixteen-year-old gymnast and dancer when she was taken to Auschwitz, and she later became a psychologist who treats other survivors of trauma. The book braids her own story with the stories of her patients around one idea: that you can choose how you carry what happened to you.
