If you want a memoir that ends with something to think about, this is built for it.

mec-prisahy.blurb: As the war turns, a famous warlord who has begun to remember what he did in his violent youth tries to unite the nations against a returning enemy, while his allies face their own breaking points.
mec-prisahy.pitch: A famous warlord has to face the man he used to be while an old enemy rises again. You watch someone decide, against everything in his past, to become somebody better, the kind of arc you loved in Licanius. The history and the fate of the whole world open up wider here, and the friendships along the way hold it together.
mec-prisahy.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

mesic-je-drsna-milenka.blurb: Mannie, a computer technician on the Moon, befriends the self-aware machine that runs the colony and joins a conspiracy to win independence from Earth.
mesic-je-drsna-milenka.pitch: A Moon colony, a computer that has quietly woken up, and a technician who is the only one it talks to. Together with a small group of conspirators they plan a revolution against Earth, and you watch how such a thing could really be organised. Mike is a companion you will come to like in the way you did Rocky in Project Hail Mary.

mission-of-gravity.blurb: A trader on a high-gravity world agrees to help human scientists recover a lost probe, a journey across half the planet through places no one of his kind has seen.
mission-of-gravity.pitch: A fifteen-inch trader captain from a world where gravity is crushing leads his crew across an alien planet to help the humans who cannot go there. The pleasure is the physics: every danger follows from the planet's weight and spin, and Barlennan is shrewd and good company.

mormonka.blurb: Carolyn Jessop is married at eighteen to a much older man in a fundamentalist polygamist sect, bears eight children, and after fifteen years flees with them and fights for custody.
mormonka.pitch: Carolyn Jessop is assigned at eighteen to a much older man in a closed sect in the American West, and she raises eight children inside a household that runs by its own rules. The book shows what each person around her wants and what leaving would cost her. It is a gripping inside view of a way of life most people only read about in headlines.

musicophilia.blurb: Neurologist Oliver Sacks collects case histories of people whose lives are changed by music, from earworms to musical hallucination to music lost.
musicophilia.pitch: A neurologist tells the stories of people whose relationship with music changed overnight: a tune that will not leave, a gift that arrives after a stroke, a song that can wake a person who has stopped responding. Each case asks what music is doing inside the brain.

nebesky-muz.blurb: Brother Yun, born into a poor farming family in rural China, becomes a Christian and house-church leader, and is repeatedly arrested, tortured and imprisoned before leaving China.
nebesky-muz.pitch: Brother Yun grows up poor in rural Henan, becomes a Christian as a teenager, and spends decades leading underground churches while the authorities arrest, beat and imprison him. You see how a persecuted church actually runs, and how one man keeps going when everything is against him. It is told in his own plain voice, with the steady conviction of someone who has little left to lose.

nezlomny.blurb: Louis Zamperini, a troubled youth turned Olympic distance runner, joins the Army Air Forces in World War II, survives a crash into the Pacific and weeks adrift on a raft, and is then held in Japanese prison camps.
nezlomny.pitch: Louis Zamperini starts as a delinquent kid in California who finds that he can run, and ends up at the Berlin Olympics. Then the war puts him on a bomber, in the open Pacific on a raft with two other men, and finally in prison camps where he has to decide what he will not give up. It is a true story told with the pace of an adventure, and it leaves you thinking about what actually keeps a person going.

nor-crystal-tears.blurb: A thranx diplomat meets humans for the first time and tries to bring two suspicious species together.
nor-crystal-tears.pitch: First contact seen through the eyes of the alien, a likeable insect-like diplomat who must make his own people and the strange new humans understand each other. It is quick and adventure-led, and the alien perspective is the fresh part. You do not need any other book to start it.

notes-from-the-burning-age.blurb: Ven, an archivist-priest expelled for selling forbidden knowledge, is recruited by a crime boss who needs old texts translated.
notes-from-the-burning-age.pitch: A world rebuilt after climate collapse, ruled by priests who forbid the technology that ruined the old one. Ven, a translator expelled from that priesthood, is pulled into a crime lord's plans to read the forbidden texts. The question that carries it is whether dangerous knowledge should be brought back.

ocelove-srdce.blurb: Ten years after ordinary people became Epics and began ruling the world, eighteen-year-old David, who saw Steelheart kill his father, joins the underground Reckoners to kill him.
ocelove-srdce.pitch: Ten years ago ordinary people gained powers and used them to rule, and David watched Steelheart kill his father. He has spent his life collecting every fact he can about Epics so he can join the only people who fight them. Told in David's own voice, with terrible metaphors, a plan that has to be exactly right and a team you start to love.

ohen-nad-hlubinou.blurb: A human research ship wakes something dangerous in the galaxy's outer reaches, and two children on a medieval pack-mind world and a woman far above carry the fight.
ohen-nad-hlubinou.pitch: A galaxy split into zones where thought itself works differently, and a threat released from the far edge. The aliens are the draw: dog-like creatures who think as a group of voices, and a world where the children of a fleeing ship must make sense of them. Read the opening pages with patience and the rest unfolds.

ohniboj.blurb: David follows a new Epic to a flooded city rebuilt as a glittering playground, and begins to wonder whether the fight he has set himself might have another answer.
ohniboj.pitch: A city drowned and rebuilt as a glittering playground, a new Epic who rules it, and David chasing the idea that the people he is fighting may not be beyond saving. Megan is the mystery standing beside him. It moves fast and stays clever in the way the first book was.

on-basilisk-station.blurb: Commander Honor Harrington, sent to the remote Basilisk Station, has to police smugglers, deal with a hostile crew and uncover a political plot.
on-basilisk-station.pitch: Honor Harrington takes a ship to a station nobody wants and finds a crew that does not trust her, smugglers to stop and a larger scheme at work. The space battles are laid out in careful detail and the navy feels real. Her treecat companion Nimitz gives it a little warmth.

ovcakova-dcera.blurb: Paks runs away from a forced marriage and enlists in a mercenary company, learning what soldiering really demands.
ovcakova-dcera.pitch: Paks refuses the marriage her father arranged and joins a mercenary company with nothing but stubbornness. You watch a farm girl become a soldier, learning the work, the comradeship and the cost of loyalty. The army life is detailed and believable, and Paks earns every step.

pastwatch-the-redemption-of-christopher-.blurb: Researchers who can observe the past plan to alter history at Columbus's voyage, alternating with Columbus's own life.
pastwatch-the-redemption-of-christopher-.pitch: In the far future a group of historians with a window on the past decides that one voyage is where everything went wrong. You alternate between them and Columbus himself, a man you may understand better than you expect, and you are left weighing whether history should be changed and what would replace it.

pathfinder.blurb: Rigg can see the paths of people who walked before him; after his father's death he learns who he really is and joins others with odd time-bending gifts.
pathfinder.pitch: Rigg can see the trails of everyone who walked a place before him, and he uses it to hunt and survive. When his father dies he learns a secret about his own past and sets out with companions whose gifts bend time itself. You get a mystery about who he is and a world where the rules of time are taken seriously.

planetfall.blurb: A colony engineer whose group followed a prophet to a planet where God was said to live has a young man appear who claims to be the prophet's grandson, which threatens the secret she keeps.
planetfall.pitch: You are inside the head of a colony engineer, who tells her story with an intimacy that makes you care about her. The colony settled a strange planet on the word of a woman who claimed to have seen God, and a newcomer now threatens the story everyone lives by. The voice is the reason to read.

poselstvi-prava.blurb: A frontier lawman returns to the big city to take over his family's house, but kidnappings of noble women and a train-robbing gang pull him back into the fight, alongside his fast-talking friend.
poselstvi-prava.pitch: Wax is a lawman who left the frontier to take over his family's house in the big city, and his quick-tongued friend Wayne is not going to let him have a quiet life. Metals give people small powers, and the fun is seeing what that does to guns, trains and politics a few hundred years on. It is quick, funny and full of banter.

posledni-kolonie.blurb: John Perry and Jane Sagan are asked to lead the first colony drawn from ten human worlds, and find on arrival that they have not been sent where they were told.
posledni-kolonie.pitch: You get the Old Man's War narrator in a very different job: running a fragile new colony with a few thousand settlers, where the dangers are as much political as military. The question that drives it is who sent them here and why. It is a fast, dry-humoured read that leans on people and loyalty over firefights.

pramen-povyseni.blurb: With the old empire fallen, a young king tries to rule a besieged city while the heroine who helped topple it is haunted by a power she does not yet understand and by a rival who offers her different answers.
pramen-povyseni.pitch: A young emperor who believes in fairness, a street-raised girl learning to trust, and armies at the gates: Elend and Vin must work out how to rule a city and how to build something better than the empire that fell. The magic runs on metals with firm rules you can follow, and the story is about people choosing what kind of leaders and friends to be.

prey-immigration-islam-and-the-erosion-o.blurb: The author argues that mass migration is eroding women's rights in Europe through sexual harassment and assault, and proposes that newcomers be required to assimilate.
prey-immigration-islam-and-the-erosion-o.pitch: A direct, argued case from a writer who has lived the issues, with specific incidents and policy proposals she thinks Europe and America should adopt. If you want to read the argument itself rather than hear about it second-hand, this is where she lays it out.

prezit.blurb: In 1972 a plane carrying a Uruguayan rugby team crashes high in the Andes; the sixteen survivors spend seventy-two days in the snow before two of them walk out for help.
prezit.pitch: A plane full of young Uruguayan rugby players and their friends crashes in the high Andes, and the survivors are left with snow, no food and no way for anyone to find them. The book follows how they organise themselves, how they argue, and what they decide when the alternative is dying. It stays with the people and the choices they make, and it leaves you asking what you would have done.

prislib-krve.blurb: A field marshal stages a coup against his king and finds the royal mages dead, whispering a warning about a broken promise.
prislib-krve.pitch: A general has just overthrown his king, and the people who did it have to find out what the dying royal mages meant by their last words. You follow the general, his gunpowder-mage son and a debt-ridden inspector, each with a different stake in how the new order turns out. The magic runs on rules you can figure out, and the political fallout of the coup is thought through.

prokleti-chalionu.blurb: Cazaril, returning broken from slavery, becomes tutor to a royal princess in a court under an ancient curse and must find a way to protect her.
prokleti-chalionu.pitch: Cazaril comes home half destroyed and takes the humblest job at court, teaching a princess whose family is under an old curse. You follow a decent man rebuilding himself while he fights to keep her safe, in a kingdom whose gods are close enough to be bargained with. It is a story about duty and what a person is willing to give up.

prvni-planeta-smrti.blurb: A professional gambler is bankrolled to win a fortune and then drawn to Pyrrus, a heavy-gravity world where every plant and animal has been trying to kill the colonists for centuries.
prvni-planeta-smrti.pitch: A gambler with a lethal bet to win lands on a planet where the whole ecosystem is hostile to humans, and he has to work out why. The planet is the star: each danger has a cause, and the answer says something about how you treat a world that fights back. It is short and quick.

ritmatik.blurb: Joel, a chalkmaker's son at a school for chalk-magicians, longs to be one of the students who can draw living lines; when pupils begin vanishing, he joins the search.
ritmatik.pitch: At an academy where a few students can draw chalk lines that fight, Joel, a chalkmaker's son, would give anything to be one of them. When students begin to vanish, he is pulled into the search beside Professor Fitch and the sharp-tongued Melody. The magic is geometry and drawing, and its rules are fun to learn alongside him.
ritmatik.coverNote: no cover on Open Library after two passes (2026-10-25)

rytmus-valky.blurb: In the fourth year of the war the human kingdoms are under a new enemy's pressure; a scientist-queen studies the spirits' nature while a depressed soldier and a singer in the enemy's ranks both have to find their way.
rytmus-valky.pitch: Deep inside a war that has changed everything, you follow Navani's research into the strange science of the world's spirits and Venli's long road away from the wrong side. Kaladin faces his hardest fight, the one inside himself. Scholars, inventors and soldiers pull in the same direction, and you learn how the powers in this world truly work.

scion.blurb: Azure, an enhanced contract killer for a corporation, is hired to protect a very old and very rich client whose secrets may tie to an explosion that killed his friend.
scion.pitch: A cyberpunk thriller from the author of Licanius, short and fast. A corporate assassin who usually kills the ultra-rich who never die is hired to protect one of them, and the job turns out to touch a loss from his own past.

seeing-voices.blurb: Oliver Sacks examines the history, language and community of Deaf people and the fight over sign language.
seeing-voices.pitch: A neurologist argues that sign language is a real language and that Deaf people form a culture of their own, following the history of deaf education and the student protest at Gallaudet. You learn how another group of people sees the world and why it was long denied.

semiosis.blurb: Colonists land on a planet that looks safe and find that its giant bamboo is intelligent, and over generations the settlers and the plant learn to read each other.
semiosis.pitch: Humans settle a new planet and meet a plant that thinks and wants things, communicating through chemistry. The book spans generations, so you watch one society grow, make mistakes and rewrite its own story while the bamboo tries to understand it. Its strongest pleasure is the plant's own perspective.

setkani-se-smrti.blurb: In 1985 Joe Simpson and Simon Yates climb the west face of Siula Grande in the Peruvian Andes; after Simpson breaks his leg, Yates cuts the rope that holds them and Simpson falls into a crevasse and must crawl out alone.
setkani-se-smrti.pitch: Two young climbers reach the summit of a Peruvian peak, and on the way down one breaks his leg and the other has to decide what to do with the rope between them. The story is told from both men's side, so you see what each was thinking and why. It is short, fast and honest, and it leaves you arguing with yourself about what you would have done.

sirotcinec.blurb: After alien missiles hit Earth and take his family, a young man chooses the army over jail and is sent to fight an enemy that has taken over Ganymede.
sirotcinec.pitch: You follow one soldier through a war that begins with a personal loss, told in his own voice as a journal. It is a straight military story about what a young man wants after everything is taken from him, and what the war makes of him. If Old Man's War worked for you, this is a close cousin in mood.

slova-paprsku.blurb: On the Shattered Plains the war against the Parshendi drags on, while a scholar's ward, a former slave soldier and a warlord with a failing grip on his own mind each have to face who they were and what they promised.
slova-paprsku.pitch: The war on the Shattered Plains grinds on while Kaladin, Shallan and Dalinar each face who they were and who they want to become. You learn more of what Shallan has been hiding, and the loyalties between old friends are tested in ways that make you care about all of them. The oaths and spirit bonds that began to open in the first book start to mean something here.

slow-bullets.blurb: A soldier wakes on a ship of prisoners and survivors, injected with a chip that records her memories, and tries to learn what happened while she was out.
slow-bullets.pitch: A woman wakes on a drifting ship with a memory chip in her body, and the people around her are piecing together the war that put them there. You read to find out what the chips have recorded and who is willing to rewrite it. Short, fast and built on one clever idea.

sluncem-ozareny.blurb: Nomad, a worldhopper running from the Night Brigade, is stranded on Canticle, a planet whose sun is lethal, as the people around him face a tyrant's siege.
sluncem-ozareny.pitch: A hunted wanderer lands on a planet whose sun slowly kills, where whole communities survive only by never stopping. He has years of running behind him and a pursuer that wants what he once carried, and now you watch him decide whether to keep fleeing or stand with people who cannot. It is fast, the world's one big hazard shapes everything in it, and the magic runs like a machine with rules you can learn.

sufficiently-advanced-magic.blurb: Corin Cadence climbs a living tower of trials to win magical powers and to find the brother who vanished inside it.
sufficiently-advanced-magic.pitch: Corin has spent five years worrying over a missing brother, and the only way to look for him is to climb the Serpent Spire, a tower of shifting rooms, traps and trials that rewards survivors with new powers. The magic has rules you can learn alongside him, level by level. It is a fast climb with companions along the way.

terminal-world.blurb: Quillon, a pathologist hiding what he is, is forced out of the tiered city of Spearpoint and into the unstable zones beyond it.
terminal-world.pitch: A city built as a tower, with every level running on a different level of technology, and a man who has been hiding what he really is. When he has to leave, you learn the world beyond with him, zone by zone. It is Reynolds at his most adventurous, with a setting you will want to see explained.

the-black-cloud.blurb: Astronomers spot a dark mass heading for the solar system and set up a secret research station to work out what it is, as it begins to block the sun.
the-black-cloud.pitch: Scientists see a dark cloud approaching and have little time to learn what it is. You watch how real researchers argue, measure and slowly work out that the cloud is more than it seems. It is a book of one big idea, and what it leaves you with is how we would talk to something that thinks differently.

the-girl-of-fire-and-thorns.blurb: A sixteen-year-old princess, married off to a king she barely knows, bears a divine stone and a prophecy she does not believe in.
the-girl-of-fire-and-thorns.pitch: Elisa is the shy, overlooked princess, married off to a foreign king while carrying a sacred stone nobody can explain. You watch her find her nerve, learn what her people need, and take charge when no one expects it. It is a desert-kingdom adventure with a heroine who grows in front of you.

the-girl-with-seven-names.blurb: Hyeonseo Lee crosses the frozen Yalu River from North Korea into China at seventeen, intending a short visit, and spends the next years surviving there and then in South Korea while she plans to rescue her family.
the-girl-with-seven-names.pitch: A seventeen-year-old girl from the North Korean border town of Hyesan crosses an iced-over river into China, thinking it is only for a few days, and never goes back. You see everyday life inside North Korea from a girl who believed in it, then watch her improvise one identity after another to stay free. It reads quickly and warmly, and it makes you wonder how far you would go to bring your family out.

the-lives-of-tao.blurb: A directionless IT worker finds an alien called Tao living in his head, and learns that two factions of its kind have been fighting a hidden war on Earth for centuries.
the-lives-of-tao.pitch: A man with no ambition suddenly hosts an ancient alien who has lived inside famous figures from history, and is dragged into a secret war between two factions. The two argue and joke while he trains to be someone who can survive it. It is fast, funny and the history interludes are a pleasure.

the-peace-war.blurb: A world's governments are held in check by a monopoly on bobbles, spheres that freeze everything inside them, until a young inventor and a rebel start to see that bobbles do not last forever.
the-peace-war.pitch: A single invention, a bubble that stops time for whatever is inside, has changed the world's balance of power and left one authority in charge. You follow the young people who think they can outsmart it. It is brisk, idea-first SF that makes you work out how such a weapon would really reshape politics.

the-praxis.blurb: A young noblewoman whose family was destroyed enters the navy of a decaying empire, and her first big battle against a rebellion puts her and a fellow officer at the centre of its fall.
the-praxis.pitch: Two officers in a multi-species empire whose old rulers have just vanished are pulled into a war that will decide what follows them. You want to know what the more ruthless of the two is willing to do. It leans on character and politics more than battle.

the-red-first-light.blurb: A lieutenant in a cyber-linked squad in the Sahel survives an airstrike thanks to a foresight nobody can explain, and begins to suspect that something larger runs the war.
the-red-first-light.pitch: A soldier and his wired-up squad fight in a near-future war, and he keeps surviving through a sense of what is coming that no one can explain. The fighting is fast and tense, and behind it is the question of what or who is steering the war. It opens on a gripping scene.

the-strength-of-the-few.blurb: Vis Telimus has won his place in the Catenan Republic's elite, only to be split into three copies who each live in a different realm.
the-strength-of-the-few.pitch: You return to Vis, now living three lives at once in three different realms, each with its own rules and its own enemies. It has the slow uncovering of a hidden history that made Licanius so hard to put down, and the answers you get open bigger questions. Islington is back to doing what he does best.

the-sudden-appearance-of-hope.blurb: Hope Arden is forgotten by everyone within minutes of leaving their sight, and has turned that into a career as a thief until a mysterious app comes into her life.
the-sudden-appearance-of-hope.pitch: What would you do if everyone you met forgot you the moment you looked away? Hope turned it into a career as an international thief, until she crosses an app that promises perfection. It asks who you are when nobody can hold onto you.

the-sword-of-kaigen.blurb: In a clan of water-wielding warriors inspired by old Japan, a mother and her son face the arrival of an enemy empire.
the-sword-of-kaigen.pitch: A mother and her teenage son live inside a proud clan of water-wielding warriors, each wanting something different from what duty asks of them. You follow both of them through a quiet, closely observed first half before the war arrives at their gate. It has a lot to say about honour, family and what loyalty is worth.

tomorrow-when-the-war-began.blurb: Seven teenagers come back from a camping trip in the bush to find their country invaded and their families gone.
tomorrow-when-the-war-began.pitch: Ellie and her friends come back from a camping trip to find their town empty and their country at war. You are inside Ellie's head as she and the others choose what to do, what they can live with, and who they are becoming under pressure. It is honest about what fighting back costs.

trading-in-danger.blurb: Kylara Vatta, expelled from her military academy, takes command of an old merchant ship in her family's fleet and runs into a war while trying to make a profit.
trading-in-danger.pitch: Ky Vatta leaves the academy in disgrace and takes a worn-out cargo ship from her family's fleet. What starts as a scrap-metal delivery ends in a war zone, and she has to solve each problem with her wits and her training. It is a quick space adventure with a heroine who thinks before she acts.

traitor-s-blade.blurb: A former king's magistrate, now a ragged Greatcoat, must carry out the dead king's last wishes while hunted by the dukes who killed him.
traitor-s-blade.pitch: Falcio was one of the king's travelling magistrates, and now that the king is dead he is trying to finish the last thing he was asked to do. The heart of it is the friendship of three Greatcoats who bicker, joke and fight side by side, in the spirit of the Three Musketeers. It has quick, vivid swordplay and a hero whose loyalty to a lost cause drives every choice.

ucednik-valky.blurb: Miles Vorkosigan, a physically fragile young Barrayaran noble rejected by the military academy, accidentally acquires a ship and a mercenary fleet.
ucednik-valky.pitch: Miles is a small, brittle young man from a militarist world who fails the one test he needed to pass. A chain of bluffs turns him into the commander of a mercenary fleet he has no business leading. You will want him to win, and to see how long he can keep inventing his way out of the trouble he creates.

uglies.blurb: In a city where everyone is made pretty at sixteen, a girl waiting for her operation is told to find a friend who ran away to a hidden settlement or never become pretty.
uglies.pitch: Everyone gets an operation at sixteen that makes them perfectly beautiful, and Tally cannot wait for hers until her friend vanishes. She is pushed to find her friend's hideout, and the cost of that choice falls on her. It moves quickly and keeps asking what beauty is for.

unsouled.blurb: Lindon is born Unsouled, forbidden from his clan's soul-based martial arts, and sets out to find a way to power anyway.
unsouled.pitch: Lindon cannot use the soul powers everyone in his clan trains for, so he has to win with wits and stubbornness instead. It is a fast, inventive story with a sharp-edged power system, a tournament, and a sly spirit companion who becomes his friend. If you liked the plucky-underdog feel of Ranger's Apprentice, this is a livelier cousin.

utek-z-tabora-14.blurb: Shin Dong-hyuk was born inside North Korea's Camp 14 and knew nothing else until his early twenties, when he escaped across the border. Journalist Blaine Harden reconstructs his life from his interviews.
utek-z-tabora-14.pitch: Shin Dong-hyuk was born inside a North Korean prison camp and believed everyone lived like that. He learned what the outside world was only by slipping through the fence and into China. This is a short, plain account of a mind formed with no idea that another way of life existed, and you will keep asking how a person finds his own wants after that.

utociste-en.blurb: Corrie ten Boom, a Dutch watchmaker, and her family hide Jewish refugees in their home in Haarlem during the Nazi occupation until they are betrayed and sent to concentration camps.
utociste-en.pitch: Corrie ten Boom is a middle-aged Dutch watchmaker who builds a secret room in her family home and hides people the Nazis are hunting. You follow the family through the quiet courage of the occupation and then through Ravensbruck, where she and her sister Betsie have to hold on to what they believe. It is warmly told and easy to follow, with a real sense of what a few ordinary people decided to risk.

vecna-valka.blurb: Physics student William Mandella is drafted into a war against an alien enemy, and relativistic travel carries him through centuries while the Earth he left changes beyond recognition.
vecna-valka.pitch: Mandella is drafted for a war against aliens fought so far away that each trip home costs him decades. Every return finds an Earth more foreign than the last, and the one thing he wants is to get back to it. If you liked the soldiers and the consequences in Old Man's War, this is the book that shaped that kind of story.

vrabcak.blurb: A Jesuit-led crew travels to a planet from which music was detected, and years later the sole survivor is questioned about what went wrong.
vrabcak.pitch: Songs reach Earth from another star, and a group of Jesuits and scientists go to find who is singing. Years later one man returns alone, broken, and has to explain what happened. You piece the answer together from both timelines, and the book leaves you thinking about faith and what we owe strangers.

vyjednavac.blurb: Siri is sent to marry the God King of a rival kingdom, and her sister Vivenna follows to save her, in a city where the gods are people who died and returned and a strange man carries a sword that talks.
vyjednavac.pitch: Two princesses are caught up in an arranged marriage to a God King: Siri sent to his court to marry him, Vivenna following to save her. In a city where gods are people who died and came back and magic runs on colour and breath, you meet a god who does not believe in himself and a strange man with a sword that talks. Both sisters change in ways you want to follow.

vzdelana.blurb: Tara Westover grows up in a survivalist family in the mountains of Idaho, never goes to school, and at seventeen walks into a university classroom, which begins an education that eventually takes her to Cambridge.
vzdelana.pitch: Tara Westover grows up in the Idaho mountains in a family that distrusts schools, doctors and the government, and she first sits in a classroom at seventeen. The book follows what she wants, what she has to unlearn and what it costs her to see her own family differently. It is an honest look at a way of life most readers never see from the inside, in the spirit of Seeking Allah, Finding Jesus.

vzdoroviti.blurb: Spensa returns from the Nowhere to a war that is finally coming to her people, as the enemy gathers for a last assault and her cytonic powers turn out to be both stronger and less predictable than ever.
vzdoroviti.pitch: Spensa comes home to a war that has finally arrived, and her cytonic powers are as strong as they are unpredictable. You follow her and her flight, loyal friends and new allies alike, into the last stand of everything the series has been about. Some of the best moments are the ones where the pilots simply rely on each other.

vzpominky-na-zemi.blurb: The machine that guards a decaying city speaks to Volemak and his sons and sends them away, while the brother Elemak grows to hate the youngest, Nafai.
vzpominky-na-zemi.pitch: The guardian machine that has kept a decaying city at peace for ages starts speaking to one family, and tells them to leave. You follow Nafai, who hears it in his own mind, and his older brother Elemak, who cannot forgive him for being the favoured one. It leaves you asking what you owe a power that protects you but will not explain itself.

wind-and-truth.blurb: As the final confrontation with the god of hatred approaches, the Radiants and their allied nations gather their last forces while each of the leads faces the thing they have most avoided.
wind-and-truth.pitch: The first great arc of the saga comes to a head as the armies of the world gather for the final contest with Odium. Dalinar, Kaladin, Navani, Adolin and Renarin each get the moment their long road has been building toward, and the world's oldest secrets are answered. If you have followed these people through four books, this is the payoff.

z-podruci-islamu-otazka-integrace-muslim.blurb: The author recounts her family and her break with Islam, and argues that Muslims in the West need to integrate rather than be left in parallel communities.
z-podruci-islamu-otazka-integrace-muslim.pitch: A very personal book from a woman who grew up in Somalia, Saudi Arabia and Kenya before settling in the West, and who writes about her own family as evidence. It asks what happens to people between the world they were born into and the one they chose. You come away with a clearer sense of how some Muslims in Europe and America experience that gap.

zanik-imperia.blurb: The Flow streams that make interstellar travel possible are collapsing, and the three people who learn of it first are a scientist, a new emperox and a ruthless trader.
zanik-imperia.pitch: An empire whose worlds can only reach one another through a river of alternate space is about to lose it, and almost nobody wants to believe it. You follow the scientist who sees the maths, the reluctant new ruler and a foul-mouthed trader with her own plans. The idea of a civilisation designed so that no part can stand alone is what keeps you reading.

zkouska.blurb: Cia Vale is chosen to take the Testing, a brutal selection of the brightest graduates for the leadership of a rebuilt world.
zkouska.pitch: Cia is chosen for the Testing, the stern exam that picks tomorrow's leaders of a rebuilt, battered country. As each round gets harder, she has to decide whom to trust and how far to go to stay alive. It moves quickly and the choices she makes keep you guessing.

zrak-mysli.blurb: Oliver Sacks writes about people who lose sight, reading or face recognition, and about his own eye cancer.
zrak-mysli.pitch: A neurologist follows people who lose sight, the ability to read or the ability to recognise a face, and shows the surprising ways they adapt, ending with his own diagnosis. Quiet, human cases of a brain finding new ways to see.

ztraceny-kov.blurb: Six years on, four allies race to stop a secretive group from setting off a god-fuelled weapon in their city while an outside power closes in on their world.
ztraceny-kov.pitch: Wax, Wayne, Marasi and Steris, a crew you have followed through the whole story, face a threat to their city that reaches back to the oldest secrets of their world. Each has a decision they have been avoiding, and the story brings them together at the end of what they started. The banter and clever metal tricks are all still here.

blood-brothers.blurb: A Palestinian boy grows up in the Christian village of Biram in 1947, loses his home as war comes, and becomes a priest working for peace between Arabs and Jews.
blood-brothers.pitch: You see the conflict from a place few readers have stood: a boy in a Galilean village in 1947, raised by a father who forbids his sons to hate. The same man later becomes a priest in Israel and tries to build something between neighbours who fear each other. A personal, bottom-up account, in the way Son of Hamas is.

bruchko.blurb: A teenage American goes to the jungles of Colombia to reach the Motilone people and spends years among them.
bruchko.pitch: At nineteen an American sets out alone for the Colombian jungle to find a remote tribe that has killed outsiders for generations. What he lives through there, and how he learns their language and ways, makes a book that reads as pure adventure.

captive-in-iran.blurb: Two young Iranian women who converted to Christianity are arrested for handing out New Testaments and spend 259 days in Tehran's Evin prison.
captive-in-iran.pitch: Two close friends are arrested for giving out Bibles in Tehran and held in Evin prison for 259 days. Their account shows a court system, a prison and a number of ordinary guards and fellow prisoners from the inside, and a friendship that holds up under it.

cry-the-beloved-country.blurb: A Zulu parson travels from his village to Johannesburg to find his missing son and sister, and finds a city and a crime that tie his fate to that of a white farmer.
cry-the-beloved-country.pitch: An old country parson goes to the great city to find his son and discovers what that city has done to the people who came to it. You follow him and a grieving white father whose lives are bound together by one terrible act, and the book keeps asking what a country owes to the people it has divided. Quiet, humane and short enough to stay with you.

dawn-of-wonder.blurb: Aedan is nearly thirteen, a farm boy who dares his friends off a stone bridge into an icy river, until a rider arrives in a hurry and the quiet of the valley breaks.
dawn-of-wonder.pitch: A farm boy with a quick strategic mind grows up in a world that looks gentle and is not. You follow Aedan from daring his friends off a stone bridge to a harder education far from home, with loyal friendships and a poetic, carefully built world around him. It is a long, rich story for readers who liked the heroism and friendship of Tolkien.

delta-v.blurb: A billionaire recruits a cave diver and other specialists for a one-way mission to mine an asteroid.
delta-v.pitch: A billionaire hires cave divers instead of astronauts for a dangerous mission to mine an asteroid, because they are the ones who know how to stay calm where a mistake can kill. The space-flight engineering is carefully imagined and the mission keeps moving. If you liked the practical problem-solving in The Martian, this is built from the same material.

elder-race.blurb: An anthropologist from a lost spacefaring Earth lives in a tower as a feared sorcerer, and a princess arrives asking him to kill a demon that is eating her people.
elder-race.pitch: A lonely anthropologist, stranded long ago on a medieval world and taken by everyone for a sorcerer, is visited by a young princess who wants him to destroy a demon. The story is told by both of them in turn, and the fun is how differently each understands every word the other says. You come away thinking about what it takes to truly understand someone from another world, as you did with Speaker for the Dead.

end-of-the-spear.blurb: Steve Saint, whose father was killed by Waodani warriors in 1956 when he was five, later moves his family into the tribe's jungle home.
end-of-the-spear.pitch: Steve Saint was five when warriors of an Ecuadorian jungle tribe killed his father. Decades later, the same people ask him to come and live with them, and the book follows his years among the Waodani, who tell their own side of that day, and asks what help from outside really does to a people.

endurance-neuveritelne-putovani-shacklet.blurb: In 1914 Shackleton's ship Endurance is trapped and crushed by Antarctic ice, leaving 28 men to survive on the drifting floe and then by boat.
endurance-neuveritelne-putovani-shacklet.pitch: The ship is caught in the Antarctic ice and crushed, leaving twenty-eight men on a drifting floe with three small boats and nothing but their leader's judgment between them and the end. It is a true story told in matter-of-fact prose, about leadership, loyalty and how a crew stays a crew.

i-dared-to-call-him-father.blurb: A wealthy Pakistani Muslim woman, abandoned by her husband, begins to have dreams with Christian imagery and starts reading the Bible, at a growing cost to her family and standing.
i-dared-to-call-him-father.pitch: A Pakistani woman of position, left by her husband, begins to have dreams she cannot explain and starts reading both the Koran and the Bible. Her own account shows how life looks from inside a Muslim family and town in the 1960s, and what her choice cost her in family, standing and home. Told plainly and personally, in the same first-person manner as Seeking Allah, Finding Jesus.

in-the-presence-of-my-enemies.blurb: Missionaries Martin and Gracia Burnham are seized by Abu Sayyaf from a Philippine resort and spend more than a year in the jungle as captives.
in-the-presence-of-my-enemies.pitch: On an anniversary trip, Gracia and Martin Burnham are taken by armed men and marched into the Philippine jungle, where they will live for 376 days. She tells what held her and her husband together, and what she learned about the men who held them, some of whom had been recruited from their villages.

kontakt.blurb: Ellie Arroway, a radio astronomer, detects a signal from the star Vega that carries instructions for a machine.
kontakt.pitch: A radio astronomer picks up a signal from another star and then has to deal with what it says and with what the whole world makes of it. You follow Ellie through the science, the politics and the argument between knowledge and belief. It is a first contact that stays with you for the thinking it leaves behind, the kind you valued in Speaker for the Dead.

kralovske-spiknuti.blurb: Royce and Hadrian, two thieves for hire, are framed for the murder of a king and caught up in a plot over the royal succession.
kralovske-spiknuti.pitch: Royce is cold and clever, Hadrian is warm and a great swordsman, and together they take on dangerous jobs for hire. When they are framed for a king's murder they have to get out of it, and the road leads from palace intrigue to an ancient monster. It is a fast, easy adventure whose real pleasure is the friendship between the two, with the spirit of The Hobbit.

lokynka-ze-smaragdoveho-more.blurb: Tress, a young woman from a poor island, sets out across a sea of living spores to rescue the boy she loves from an evil sorceress.
lokynka-ze-smaragdoveho-more.pitch: Tress lives on a small island in a world where the sea is made of living spores that act like water, fire and worse. When the boy she loves is taken, she signs on to a pirate ship to sail after him. It is a funny, warm adventure with a talking crew and a narrator who clearly loves telling it, with the gentle spirit of The Hobbit.

lost-moon-apollo-13.blurb: Apollo 13 loses power and oxygen on its way to the Moon, and the crew and mission control must get three men home.
lost-moon-apollo-13.pitch: Two days out from Earth, an explosion cripples Apollo 13 and the three astronauts and the engineers on the ground have to improvise their way home with what they have. It follows the crew, their families and mission control through the clock, with engineering that is explained clearly.

more-rzi.blurb: Brittle, a former caregiver robot turned scavenger, fights to stay free in a world where godlike machine intelligences absorb every independent robot.
more-rzi.pitch: Humans are gone, and a worn-out caregiver robot named Brittle scavenges parts in a desert of rusting machines while godlike intelligences hunt anyone who refuses to join them. Her sharp, stubborn voice carries you through her past and through a quest that could free every robot left. Underneath it is a question about what a machine does with a freedom nobody gave it.

narozeny-mimo-zakon.blurb: Trevor Noah grows up in apartheid South Africa as the child of a Black mother and a white father, a relationship that was then a crime.
narozeny-mimo-zakon.pitch: A boy is born to a Black mother and a white father in a country where their very relationship is a crime. Trevor Noah tells his own story with the humour of a comedian and the care of someone who knows what language, a mother's stubbornness and a few small choices can do when the law is against you.

not-god-s-type.blurb: An English professor and committed atheist traces how she came to take Christianity seriously, through poetry, friendship and a fencing partner.
not-god-s-type.pitch: A literature professor who thought faith was superstition for the unthinking tells the story of how that view came apart. Her path runs through poems, a friend she respected and an honest weighing of what she could and could not believe, the same first-person honesty as Seeking Allah, Finding Jesus.

paserakem-ve-sluzbach-nejvyssiho.blurb: A Dutch ex-soldier, after finding faith, drives a small car packed with Bibles to the closed borders of communist Europe.
paserakem-ve-sluzbach-nejvyssiho.pitch: A restless Dutch soldier finds a purpose, then spends years driving Bibles over the closed borders of communist Eastern Europe in an ordinary car. It reads as an adventure, with border guards, close calls and glimpses of everyday life behind the Iron Curtain in the early Cold War.

peace-child.blurb: Don and Carol Richardson move to a tribe of cannibal headhunters in New Guinea in 1962, where betrayal is honoured and peace seems impossible.
peace-child.pitch: In 1962 a young couple settle among a New Guinea people who admire treachery above all, and have to work out how a society that honours betraying a friend can ever make peace. You follow their puzzle over the tribe's customs and a single peace-making ritual that reveals how the Sawi think.

psi-vojaci.blurb: Rex is a genetically engineered war dog, trained to obey his handlers, who fights alongside a bear, a swarm of bees and a giant lizard in a corporate war in Mexico.
psi-vojaci.pitch: Rex is a war dog bred for obedience, who fights alongside a bear, a lizard-soldier and a swarm of bees that thinks as one. The book follows what happens when he starts to ask what he wants and whether a good soldier can still be a good dog. You come to care about the pack, and the question of who counts as a person stays with you after the last page.

remnant-population.blurb: Ofelia, an old woman on a company colony world, hides when the colony is evacuated and discovers the planet has other inhabitants.
remnant-population.pitch: When the company evacuates her colony, old Ofelia quietly stays behind, alone at last on a planet she loves. Then she finds out she is not alone after all. It is a gentle first contact told through a stubborn, funny woman who solves problems with patience, and you will want things to go well for her.

rubas.blurb: After a disaster at a mining outpost, two crew members land on the hostile, lightless moon Shroud and begin a long journey toward rescue, while the moon's own intelligent life watches them.
rubas.pitch: Two people crash on a moon where the pressure is crushing, the dark is total and everything is alive in ways they cannot sense. Their journey toward rescue alternates with the viewpoint of the moon's own intelligent inhabitants, who perceive the world very differently. It is a first contact where the real adventure is learning to understand each other, a companionship story in the spirit of Project Hail Mary.

rychlost-temnoty.blurb: Lou Arrendale, an autistic man with a job and a fencing club, is pressured by his employer to try an experimental treatment that could make him normal.
rychlost-temnoty.pitch: Lou is an autistic adult who works in a lab, fences with friends, and sees patterns in the world that others miss, until his employer pressures him to try a treatment that may change who he is. You live inside his head for the whole book, which is warm, funny and unusual, and the question of what a cure would cost him is never easy. It stays with you the way Speaker for the Dead did.

some-desperate-glory.blurb: Kyr is a soldier on Gaea Station, where the last humans raise children to avenge Earth, and she breaks away from the plan her station has for her.
some-desperate-glory.pitch: Kyr has been raised on a station of Earth's last survivors, trained from birth to avenge the world that was destroyed. When she is sent where she does not want to go, she decides to take the war into her own hands, with a seditious friend and a captive alien. It is a hard look at how a person becomes certain, and what happens when that certainty meets someone who shows her another way.

symbiont.blurb: Arton Daghdev, a dissident professor, is shipped to a labour colony on the alien planet Kiln, where the local life is unlike anything he has studied.
symbiont.pitch: A scholar is exiled to a prison colony on an alien world whose life follows rules nothing on Earth prepared him for. Staying alive means working out how that ecosystem fits together, and the more he learns the stranger it gets. You get a dry, sharp narrator and an alien biology built with real care, in the spirit of the exploring you enjoyed in Project Hail Mary.

the-book-that-wouldn-t-burn.blurb: Livira, a refugee from the Dust, is placed in the great Library of Crath City, while Evar lives locked inside one of its chambers.
the-book-that-wouldn-t-burn.pitch: Livira flees to the great Library of Crath City and learns to be a librarian, while a young man named Evar grows up shut inside a hidden chamber of the same building. Two stories head toward the same mystery about what the Library is and what it is hiding. If you like stories about knowledge and who protects it, this one is built on that.

the-boy-who-harnessed-the-wind.blurb: During Malawi's famine of 2001-2002, a teenage boy forced out of school builds a windmill from scrap to bring his family electricity.
the-boy-who-harnessed-the-wind.pitch: When a famine in Malawi forces William out of school, he keeps going to the library and teaches himself from a science textbook, then builds a windmill from scrap to bring light to his family's house. You want him to succeed while his neighbours call him mad.

the-expert-system-s-brother.blurb: Handry, a boy in a village that depends on a mysterious power, is cut off from it by an accident and sets out to survive on his own in a landscape full of monsters.
the-expert-system-s-brother.pitch: A boy is cut off from the thing his whole village lives by, and has to find his own way through a land that looks like fantasy and slowly turns out to be something else. You follow Handry's voice, curious and likeable, as he puzzles out what the world really is. His sister and the exile leader each answer that question differently, and you are left thinking about who gets to decide how people live with their tools.

the-insanity-of-god.blurb: A relief worker whose son died in Somalia sets out to learn how Christians survive persecution in some of the most hostile countries, and collects their stories.
the-insanity-of-god.pitch: After losing his son while working in war-torn Somalia, a missionary sets out across Muslim and communist countries to ask believers under pressure what keeps their faith alive. The interviews give a rare look at how people live under real persecution, from China to Central Asia, and what he brings home is a hard question about what faith costs.

_null_cover: null with a coverNote is a SETTLED row, not a gap: the search already ran on the date in the note and Open Library had nothing, so the app draws a typographic placeholder and its Gaps panel does not count it - re-running this script cannot clear it, and reporting it would name a shortfall the reader can do nothing about. Later runs skip it too; --retry-missing searches again. 'names a group, not a book' means the row covers an author or a category, so there is no single cover that would be honest. null with NO coverNote is the real gap: a row nothing has looked up yet.
